etymology_story.zh: 经中古英语借自古法语 heritable，关联 heriter“继承”，进一步追溯到晚期拉丁语 hērēditāre“继承”。“能传给继承人”的含义后来扩展到生物学，表示特征能够通过遗传传给后代。[《美国传统英语词典》](https://www.ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=heritable)
etymology_story.en: Heritable entered Middle English from Old French heritable, related to heriter, 'to inherit,' ultimately from Late Latin hērēditāre. The meaning 'capable of passing to an heir' extended into biology to describe characteristics that can pass genetically to offspring. [American Heritage Dictionary](https://www.ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=heritable)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 herit-（继承相关的黏着词干）+ -able（能够被……的）→ heritable；这是一种形态分析，不表示英语中存在常用独立动词 herit。直接词族：heritability（遗传力；可遗传性，-able → -ability）、heritably（以可遗传方式，-able → -ably）、nonheritable／non-heritable（不可遗传或不可继承的）。扩展同源词族包括 inherit（继承）、inherited（遗传的；继承所得的）、inheritable（可继承或可遗传的）、inheritance（继承；遗传）、inheritor（继承者）、disinherit（剥夺继承权）、disinheritance（继承权的剥夺）、heir（继承人）、heiress（女性继承人）、heirship（继承人资格）、heritage（传承；遗产）、heredity（遗传）、hereditary（遗传性的；世袭的）和 hereditarily（通过遗传；世袭地）。
morphology_enriched.en: A modern analysis is herit-, a bound stem relating to inheritance, + -able, 'capable of being,' → heritable; this does not imply a common independent English verb herit. Direct family members include heritability, with -able → -ability; heritably, with -able → -ably; and nonheritable/non-heritable. The broader historical family includes inherit, inherited, inheritable, inheritance, inheritor, disinherit, disinheritance, heir, heiress, heirship, heritage, heredity, hereditary, and hereditarily.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: inheritable（可继承的；可遗传的）与 heritable 最接近，常用于财产、权利及特征；hereditary（遗传性的；世袭的）强调通过家族或世代传递；genetic（基因的；遗传学的）范围更广，有基因基础并不必然意味着能够传给后代。在定量遗传学中，heritability（遗传力）描述特定群体和环境中性状差异的遗传贡献，不等于某个个体的性状“有多少百分比来自基因”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Inheritable is the closest alternative and applies to property, rights, and characteristics; hereditary emphasizes transmission through families or generations; genetic is broader, since having a genetic basis does not necessarily mean something can pass to offspring. In quantitative genetics, heritability concerns the genetic contribution to variation within a particular population and environment, not the percentage of an individual's trait that comes from genes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: herit- 联想 inherit“继承”，-able 表“能被”→ 能被下一代接过去：财产可继承，性状可遗传。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect herit- with inherit and -able with 'can be': something the next generation can receive, whether property or a genetic characteristic.

morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, knell is an unsegmented base used as both noun and verb. Inflected forms are knells, knelled, and knelling; combinations include death knell and knell-like, meaning resembling a knell. The initial k is silent.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Toll describes slow, repeated bell sounds more broadly; chime usually suggests a pleasant sound without the association with death; death knell most closely matches the figurative sense of a signal of impending failure or extinction.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：lapis lazuli → lapis，属于短语截短，不是词根加后缀。表示材料或颜色时通常不可数；lapis beads 中的 lapis 可作名词定语，不必另立形容词词性。历史同源词有 lapidary（宝石加工的；宝石工匠），但它不是现代英语中直接由 lapis 加词缀形成的。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: lapis lazuli → lapis by shortening a phrase, rather than adding an affix. It is normally uncountable as a material or colour; lapis in lapis beads functions as a noun modifier. Lapidary, meaning relating to gem cutting or a gem cutter, is a historical cognate rather than a direct modern derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lapis lazuli is the full synonymous name of the rock. Lazurite is its principal blue mineral rather than the whole rock; ultramarine primarily names a pigment or colour and is not interchangeable with lapis as a stone.

etymology_story.zh: magus 经拉丁语 magus、希腊语 magos 追溯至古伊朗语词汇，与古波斯语 maguš 有关，早期指米底和波斯的祭司成员。随着这些人物与神秘知识和法术相联系，该词又发展出“术士”义，并用于基督教传统中的东方博士。
etymology_story.en: Magus came through Latin magus and Greek magos from Iranian vocabulary related to Old Persian maguš, originally associated with Median and Persian priests. Associations with occult learning led to the magician sense, while Christian usage applied the word to the eastern wise men. [Merriam-Webster: magus](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/magus) [Merriam-Webster: magic](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/magic)

morphology_enriched.zh: magus 在现代英语中作为整体借词使用，不宜机械拆成能产词根和后缀；传统复数为 magi /ˈmeɪdʒaɪ/，其中 g 的发音由 /ɡ/ 变为 /dʒ/。历史相关词包括 mage（法师）、magic（魔法）；扩展词族有 magic + -al → magical（有魔力的）、magical + -ly → magically（神奇地）、magic + -ian → magician（魔术师；术士）。
morphology_enriched.en: Magus is a whole-word borrowing in modern English, not a productive root-plus-suffix formation. Its traditional plural is magi /ˈmeɪdʒaɪ/, with /ɡ/ changing to /dʒ/. Historical relatives include mage and magic; the wider family includes magic + -al → magical, magical + -ly → magically, and magic + -ian → magician.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mage is especially common in fantasy; sorcerer emphasizes supernatural spellcasting, sometimes with sinister associations; magician also commonly means a stage performer, whereas magus suggests an ancient, learned, or occult figure.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect magus with magic: a person associated with mysterious learning and powers. Remember one magus, several magi.

etymology_story.zh: amethyst 经中古英语、法语和拉丁语来自希腊语 amethystos，字面意思是“不醉的”，由表示“不”的 a- 与表示醉酒的词干构成。名称反映了古人认为这种宝石能够防醉的信念，后来也用来指其紫色。
etymology_story.en: Amethyst reached English through French and Latin from Greek amethystos, literally not drunk, formed with negative a- and a stem referring to intoxication. The name reflects an ancient belief that the stone prevented drunkenness; it later also named the stone's purple colour. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/amethyst) [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/amethyst)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，amethyst 通常作为整体词基学习；希腊语的否定结构属于历史词源分析。复数为 amethysts；amethyst + -ine → amethystine（紫水晶的；紫水晶色的）；amethyst + -like → amethyst-like（像紫水晶的）。名词与形容词形式相同，读音和重音不变；材料修饰语也可分析为名词定语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, amethyst is normally treated as a whole base; its Greek negative structure belongs to historical analysis. The plural is amethysts; amethyst + -ine gives amethystine, meaning relating to or coloured like amethyst, and amethyst + -like gives amethyst-like. Noun and adjective uses have identical pronunciation and stress; material modifiers may also be analysed as attributive nouns.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: purple quartz（紫色石英）是宝石义的描述性近义表达；violet（紫罗兰色）是更宽泛的颜色词，不指这种宝石；amethystine（紫水晶的；紫水晶色的）是相应的派生形容词，语体通常更正式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Purple quartz is a descriptive equivalent for the gemstone; violet is a broader colour term that does not identify the stone; amethystine is the corresponding derived adjective and generally sounds more formal.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 古希腊语“不醉”之石 → 紫水晶 → 紫水晶般的紫色；把防醉故事当作词源记忆线索。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The ancient not-drunk stone → purple quartz → its purple colour. Use the old belief as a historical memory hook.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：butter + cup → buttercup，是以 cup 为中心成分的复合名词；复数为 buttercups。常用组合有 buttercup family（毛茛科）和 buttercup-yellow（毛茛花般鲜黄色的），没有需要掌握的常用后缀派生词族。植物科名中的修饰用法，部分词典列为形容词，也可作名词定语分析。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: butter + cup → buttercup, a compound noun headed by cup; the plural is buttercups. Common combinations include buttercup family and buttercup-yellow, meaning bright yellow like the flower; there is no substantial common family of suffixed derivatives. Some dictionaries classify the botanical family modifier as an adjective; it can also be analysed as an attributive noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ranunculus is a broader, more technical plant name and often refers in gardening to showy cultivated forms; crowfoot overlaps with buttercup but commonly names particular kinds; sweetheart corresponds only to the affectionate form of address.

etymology_story.en: The word traces back to Medieval Latin disconsolatus, meaning 'uncomforted', combining negative dis- with a form related to Latin consolari, 'to comfort'. English preserves this central meaning and also uses the word for deep dejection after disappointment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常将 disconsolate 作为整体形容词学习；历史上可识别 dis-（否定）和 consol-（安慰），但不宜机械拆成现代动词 console 加 -ate。派生词：disconsolate + -ly → disconsolately（悲伤失落地）；disconsolate + -ness → disconsolateness（悲伤；难以安慰的状态）；另有较少见的 disconsolation（悲伤；无慰）。同源词族：console（安慰）、consolation（安慰；慰藉）、consolatory（安慰性的）、consolable（可安慰的）、inconsolable（无法安慰的）、inconsolably（无法安慰地）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, disconsolate is normally learned as a whole adjective; historically, negative dis- and consol-, 'comfort', are recognizable, but it should not be mechanically analyzed as the modern verb console plus -ate. Derivatives include disconsolate + -ly → disconsolately and disconsolate + -ness → disconsolateness; disconsolation is less common. Related words include console, consolation, consolatory, consolable, inconsolable, and inconsolably.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: inconsolable（悲痛得无法安慰）更强调安慰不起作用；dejected（沮丧的）常指失败或失望后情绪低落；despondent（灰心绝望的）更强调失去希望。disconsolate 侧重深深的悲伤及难以获得慰藉。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Inconsolable emphasizes that comfort cannot relieve someone's distress; dejected commonly describes low spirits after failure or disappointment; despondent emphasizes a loss of hope. Disconsolate centers on deep unhappiness and difficulty finding comfort.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dis- 否定 + consol- 安慰：安慰也难以抚平的悲伤。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Negative dis- + consol-, 'comfort': sadness that comfort cannot easily soothe.

usage_note: 是脑部疾病或功能障碍的概括性名称；不像 encephalitis 那样专指炎症。

etymology_story.zh: 这是以希腊语成分构成的医学术语：encephalo- 来自 enkephalos（脑，字面义为“头内之物”），-pathy 来自 pathos（痛苦；疾病）。这些成分结合后表示“脑的疾病”，后来广泛用于不同原因引起的脑功能障碍或脑部病变。
etymology_story.en: This medical term combines Greek-derived encephalo-, from enkephalos, 'brain', literally 'that within the head', with -pathy, from pathos, 'suffering or disease'. The combination means 'disease of the brain' and is used broadly for brain dysfunction or damage arising from various causes.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：encephalo-（脑）+ -pathy（疾病；病变）→ encephalopathy（脑病）。复数：encephalopathies；形容词：encephalopathic（脑病的）。同一组合词干的相关术语包括 encephalitis（脑炎）、encephalitis 的形容词 encephalitic（脑炎的）、encephalogram（脑部检查记录或图像）和 electroencephalography（脑电描记术）；这些是相关构词，不是 encephalopathy 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: encephalo-, 'brain', + -pathy, 'disease or disorder', → encephalopathy. The plural is encephalopathies, and the adjective is encephalopathic. Related formations using the same combining stem include encephalitis, its adjective encephalitic, encephalogram, and electroencephalography; these are related formations rather than direct derivatives of encephalopathy.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: brain disease（脑部疾病）是较通俗的近义表达；brain disorder（脑部障碍或疾病）的范围更广；cerebral dysfunction（脑功能障碍）强调功能异常，不一定指明确的疾病类别。encephalopathy 是医学总称，本身不说明病因，也不等于专指炎症的 encephalitis（脑炎）。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Brain disease is a plainer near-equivalent; brain disorder is broader; cerebral dysfunction emphasizes abnormal functioning without necessarily identifying a disease category. Encephalopathy is a medical umbrella term that does not itself specify the cause and is distinct from encephalitis, which specifically denotes inflammation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: encephalo- 是“脑”，-pathy 是“病”：脑 + 病 = 脑病。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Encephalo- means 'brain' and -pathy means 'disease': brain + disease = encephalopathy.

etymology_story.zh: 来自希腊神话人物 Oedipus（俄狄浦斯）的名字，其希腊语原名 Oidipous 通常解释为“肿足”，与他婴儿时期双脚受伤的故事有关。弗洛伊德借其不知情地弑父娶母的故事提出 Oedipus complex（俄狄浦斯情结），Oedipal 随之成为相关形容词。
etymology_story.en: The adjective comes from Oedipus, whose Greek name Oidipous is conventionally interpreted as 'swollen-foot', referring to the injury to his feet in infancy. Freud drew on the story of Oedipus unknowingly killing his father and marrying his mother to name the Oedipus complex, from which the psychological use of Oedipal developed.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：Oedipus → Oedip-（专名词干）+ -al（……的）→ Oedipal；也常写作小写 oedipal。相关形式：Oedipally／oedipally（以俄狄浦斯情结的方式，较少见）、pre-Oedipal（俄狄浦斯阶段之前的）、post-Oedipal（俄狄浦斯阶段之后的）；相关表达为 Oedipus complex（俄狄浦斯情结），相关异形形容词有 Oedipean 和 Oedipian。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: Oedipus → the proper-name stem Oedip- + adjectival -al → Oedipal; lowercase oedipal is also common. Related forms include the less common adverb Oedipally or oedipally, pre-Oedipal, and post-Oedipal. The associated expression is Oedipus complex; alternative related adjectives include Oedipean and Oedipian.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Oedipean 和 Oedipian 是较少见的近义形式，尤其可用于与俄狄浦斯本人或其故事有关的语境；incestuous（乱伦的；涉及乱伦欲望的）仅在部分语境中意义重叠，范围更广，也不包含特定的亲子竞争结构。Oedipal 在心理分析语境中可指理论上的无意识心理模式，并不必然表示实际行为。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Oedipean and Oedipian are less common alternatives, especially for references to Oedipus or his story. Incestuous overlaps only in some contexts: it is broader and does not convey the specific pattern of parental desire and rivalry. In psychoanalytic use, Oedipal may describe a proposed unconscious pattern without implying actual behavior.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Oedipus + -al, 'relating to': connect the mythic character with the psychological complex named after him.

etymology_story.en: The word was formed in the eighteenth century from pin, 'fasten with a pin', and afore, 'in front', referring to an apron pinned to the front of clothing. It later extended to a similarly shaped sleeveless dress worn over a blouse or other top.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：pin（用别针固定）+ afore（在前面）→ pinafore；这是已经词汇化的复合名词，afore 在现代普通英语中较少单独使用。复数为 pinafores；常见复合表达有 pinafore dress（围裙式无袖连衣裙）和 pinafore apron（带胸兜围裙）。该词没有常用的直接派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: pin, 'fasten with a pin', + afore, 'in front', → pinafore. This is a lexicalized compound noun, and afore is uncommon as an independent word in ordinary modern English. The plural is pinafores; common compounds include pinafore dress and pinafore apron. The word has no common family of direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: jumper 在美式英语中可指这种套穿的无袖连衣裙，但在英式英语中通常指套头毛衣；apron（围裙）强调防污用途，不一定带胸兜；pinnie／pinny（围裙）是英式非正式说法。pinafore 可指防护罩裙，也可指作为正式穿着的无袖裙。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Jumper is the American term for this type of sleeveless overdress, but usually means a sweater in British English. Apron emphasizes protection from dirt and need not include a bib. Pinnie or pinny is an informal British word for an apron. Pinafore can name either a protective garment or a sleeveless dress worn as clothing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pin + afore：别在前面，先是围裙，再成为围裙式连衣裙。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pin it afore, or in front: first a protective apron, then an apron-shaped dress.

etymology_story.zh: sherd 与 shard 是同一历史词的不同形式，源自古英语 sceard，意为“碎片”，与表示“剪切”的 shear 同属一个日耳曼语词族。现代 sherd 尤其用于考古学，指破碎陶器的残片。
etymology_story.en: Sherd and shard are historical forms of the same word, descending from Old English sceard, meaning a fragment, and belonging to the Germanic word family that includes shear. In modern usage, sherd is especially associated with fragments of pottery in archaeology.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 sherd 是不可再作有效词缀拆分的简单词；复数为 sherds。常见复合词为 pot（陶器）+ sherd（碎片）→ potsherd（陶器碎片）；shard 是同源变体，并非由 sherd 添加词缀而成。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sherd is a simple word without a productive prefix–root–suffix breakdown; its plural is sherds. The established compound pot + sherd forms potsherd, a pottery fragment; shard is a historical variant rather than an affixed derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: potsherd（陶器碎片）与 sherd 最接近，明确限定为陶器；shard（碎片）范围较广，常指玻璃或陶器的尖锐碎片；fragment（碎片、残片）最宽泛，不限定材料或形状。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Potsherd is the closest equivalent and explicitly denotes pottery. Shard has a broader range and often suggests a sharp piece of glass or pottery, while fragment is the most general term and specifies neither material nor shape.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 sherd 与 shard 连起来记：考古现场的一片碎陶，就是 sherd。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect sherd with shard: a pottery shard at an archaeological site is a sherd.

etymology_story.zh: butane 是19世纪形成的化学名称，由 butyl 的词干与烷烃命名后缀 -ane 构成。这个词干经 butyric acid（丁酸）追溯到拉丁语 butyrum“黄油”，因为丁酸与酸败黄油有关。
etymology_story.en: Butane is a nineteenth-century chemical name formed from the stem of butyl and the alkane suffix -ane. Through butyric acid, the stem ultimately goes back to Latin butyrum, meaning butter, because butyric acid was associated with rancid butter.

morphology_enriched.zh: but-（化学命名中的四碳词干）+ -ane（烷烃后缀）→ butane（丁烷，C₄H₁₀）。同词干术语包括 butyl（丁基）、butene（丁烯）、butyne（丁炔）、butanol（丁醇）、butanal（丁醛）和 butanoic acid（丁酸）；相关名称包括 n-butane（正丁烷）与 isobutane（异丁烷），这些不是全部由 butane 直接添加词缀得到的。
morphology_enriched.en: But- is the four-carbon stem in chemical nomenclature, and -ane identifies an alkane, giving butane, C₄H₁₀. Related formations sharing the stem include butyl, butene, butyne, butanol, butanal, and butanoic acid; related names include n-butane and isobutane, rather than all being direct affixed derivatives of butane.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有可在所有语境中替换 butane 的常用近义词。n-butane（正丁烷）明确指直链异构体；isobutane（异丁烷）指支链异构体；LPG（液化石油气）是更宽泛的燃料类别，可含丁烷和丙烷。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Butane has no common synonym that is interchangeable in every context. N-butane specifically identifies the straight-chain isomer, isobutane identifies the branched isomer, and LPG is a broader fuel category that may contain butane and propane.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 化学命名里，but- 提示“四个碳”，-ane 提示“烷烃”：四碳烷烃就是丁烷。
mnemonic_anchor.en: In chemical names, but- signals four carbons and -ane signals an alkane: a four-carbon alkane is butane.

etymology_story.zh: cognate 源自拉丁语 cognatus，意为“有血缘关系的”，其构成为 co-（共同）与表示“出生”的 gnatus。英语把共同出生、同属一族的概念扩展到词语的共同来源，也用于性质相近的事物。
etymology_story.en: Cognate comes from Latin cognatus, meaning related by birth, formed from co-, together, and gnatus, born. English extended the idea of shared ancestry to the historical relationship between words and to things closely related in nature.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 cognate 作为完整词基使用，名词与形容词同形；历史结构 co- + gnat-（出生）+ -us 不属于现代英语的能产构词公式。相关派生词有 cognateness（同源性、相关性）、cognately（同源地、相关地）及较少见的 cognation（亲缘关系、同源关系）；名词复数为 cognates。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats cognate as a whole base, with identical noun and adjective forms; its historical structure, co- + gnat-, born, + -us, is not a productive modern English formation. Related derivatives include cognateness, cognately, and the less common cognation; the plural noun is cognates.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: related（相关的）范围最广，不一定表示共同来源；kindred（同类的、相近的）常强调性质或精神上的相似；同源词本身必须有共同历史来源，仅仅外形或意思相似并不足以成为 cognates。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related is the broadest alternative and need not imply shared ancestry. Kindred often emphasizes similarity in character or spirit. Cognates specifically share a historical origin; resemblance in spelling or meaning alone does not establish cognacy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“共同出生”的历史逻辑：词语有共同祖先，就是同源；学科像亲属一样接近，就是相关。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the historical idea of being born together: words with a shared ancestor are cognate, and closely connected disciplines are figurative relatives.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语宜把 dowdy 作为完整词基记忆，不作可靠的能产词缀拆分。dowdy 去 y 加 -ily → dowdily（土气地）；去 y 加 -iness → dowdiness（土气、老气）；比较级和最高级为 dowdier、dowdiest。历史名词用法如今不属于常用词性。

etymology_story.zh: electrolysis 是19世纪形成的科学术语，由 electro-（电）与源自希腊语 lysis（松解、分解）的构词成分组合而成。它最初指电流引起的化学分解，后来也用于利用电流破坏毛囊的脱毛治疗。
etymology_story.en: Electrolysis was formed as a scientific term in the nineteenth century from electro-, electricity, and a combining element derived from Greek lysis, loosening or dissolution. Originally referring to chemical decomposition caused by an electric current, it later also came to denote hair removal through electrical destruction of follicles.

morphology_enriched.zh: electro-（电）+ -lysis（分解、松解）→ electrolysis。主要词族包括 electrolyse（英式动词，电解）、electrolyze（美式拼写）、electrolytic（电解的）、electrolytically（通过电解）、electrolyser/electrolyzer（电解器）及 electrologist（电解除毛技师）；相关术语 electrolyte（电解质）与它共享构词成分，并非简单添加后缀所得。
morphology_enriched.en: Electro- means electricity and -lysis means breakdown or dissolution, forming electrolysis. The main word family includes electrolyse in British English, electrolyze in American English, electrolytic, electrolytically, electrolyser/electrolyzer, and electrologist, a practitioner of electrical hair removal; electrolyte is a related formation sharing combining elements rather than a simple suffixed derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: electrolytic decomposition（电解分解）接近其化学义，但强调分解，不能覆盖所有电解用途；electroepilation（电脱毛）对应其脱毛义，是较专业的名称；laser hair removal（激光脱毛）是相关治疗而非近义词，使用的是光能。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Electrolytic decomposition is close to the chemical sense but emphasizes breakdown and does not cover every application of electrolysis. Electroepilation is a more technical term for the hair-removal sense. Laser hair removal is a related treatment rather than a synonym, since it uses light energy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: electro- 是“电”，-lysis 是“分解”：电流促成化学变化；脱毛义则联想到用电流破坏毛囊。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Electro- supplies electricity and -lysis suggests breakdown: current produces chemical change, while the hair-removal sense involves electrical destruction of follicles.

etymology_story.en: English borrowed epidermis through Late Latin from Greek epidermis, meaning the outer skin and combining epi-, meaning 'upon,' with a stem related to derma, meaning 'skin.' The term was later also applied to the protective outer cell layer of plant organs.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词识别：epi-（在……之上）+ derm-（皮肤）+ 历史词尾 -is；-is 不是这里可自由用于造词的现代英语后缀。主要词族：epidermal、epidermic（表皮的），epidermally（在表皮上；经表皮地），epidermoid（表皮样的）；相关词有 dermis（真皮）、dermal（皮肤的）和 dermatology（皮肤病学）。
morphology_enriched.en: Recognizable structure: epi- ('upon') + derm- ('skin') + the historical ending -is; -is is not a freely productive modern English suffix here. Principal family members include epidermal and epidermic ('of the epidermis'), epidermally ('on or through the epidermis'), and epidermoid ('resembling the epidermis'); related words include dermis, dermal, and dermatology.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: skin（皮肤）通常指整个皮肤器官，范围大于 epidermis；cuticle（角质层、护膜）在植物学中通常指覆盖表皮的非细胞性保护层；epithelium（上皮组织）是更广的组织类别，动物表皮属于其中一种。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Skin usually means the whole organ and is broader than epidermis; cuticle in botany usually means the noncellular protective covering over the epidermis; epithelium is a broader tissue category that includes the animal epidermis.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Epi- means 'upon' and derm- means 'skin': the epidermis is the skin's outermost layer.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自德语 Masochismus，由精神科医生 Richard von Krafft-Ebing 在19世纪末根据奥地利作家 Leopold von Sacher-Masoch 的姓氏创造，其作品描写了与受苦和屈从相关的欲望。这个词后来扩展为日常语言中“似乎喜欢自找苦吃”的说法。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed German Masochismus, coined in the late nineteenth century by psychiatrist Richard von Krafft-Ebing from the surname of Austrian writer Leopold von Sacher-Masoch, whose fiction explored desires involving suffering and submission. The word later acquired an everyday sense of apparently enjoying self-imposed hardship.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词识别：Masoch（人名词干）+ -ism（倾向或行为模式），词干中的 -och 不能再拆成英语词缀。主要词族：masochist（有受虐倾向的人），masochistic（受虐的；自找苦吃的），masochistically（以受虐或自我折磨的方式）；复合词包括 sadomasochism（施虐受虐）、sadomasochist（有施虐受虐倾向的人）和 sadomasochistic（施虐受虐的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Recognizable structure: Masoch, a surname used as a base, + -ism, indicating a tendency or pattern of behavior; the -och within the name is not an English affix. Principal family members are masochist, masochistic, and masochistically; compounds include sadomasochism, sadomasochist, and sadomasochistic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: self-punishment（自我惩罚）强调惩罚自己，不一定带来快感；self-torment（自我折磨）强调自己造成的痛苦；self-mortification（自我克制、苦修）常带有宗教或道德目的。这些词与 masochism 的日常引申义部分重叠，但不等同于其性含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Self-punishment emphasizes penalizing oneself without necessarily enjoying it; self-torment emphasizes suffering that one causes oneself; self-mortification often involves religious or moral self-denial. These overlap with the everyday extended sense of masochism but are not equivalents of its sexual sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住方向：痛苦落在自己身上，却从中得到快感。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the direction: the suffering is experienced by oneself, and pleasure comes from it.

etymology_story.zh: 这个词在中古英语时期经法语 privacion 进入英语，源自拉丁语 privatio（剥夺），对应动词 privare（使失去、剥夺）。其含义从一般的被剥夺或缺失，发展为尤其指缺少生活必需品的困苦状态。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English through French privacion, from Latin privatio, meaning deprivation, based on privare, 'to deprive.' Its meaning developed from deprivation or absence in general toward hardship caused especially by lacking basic necessities.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 privation 作为整体学习；可识别为受限词根 priv-（剥夺、缺失）+ -ation（状态），但它是历史借词，并非由常用现代动词直接新造。主要词族：privations（各种生活困苦），privative（表示缺失或否定的），privatively（以缺失或否定的方式）；同源相关词有 deprive（剥夺）、deprived（贫困的；被剥夺的）和 deprivation（剥夺；匮乏）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, privation is generally learned as a whole word; its recognizable elements are the bound root priv- ('deprivation or absence') and -ation ('state'), although it is a historical borrowing rather than a fresh formation from a common modern verb. Principal family members include privations, privative, and privatively; etymologically related words include deprive, deprived, and deprivation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: deprivation（剥夺、匮乏）适用范围更广，也可指睡眠、权利等的缺失；hardship（困苦）泛指艰难处境，不一定由物资不足造成；destitution（赤贫）强调极端贫困、几乎没有生活资料。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Deprivation is broader and can involve sleep, rights, or other needs; hardship means difficult circumstances without necessarily implying material scarcity; destitution emphasizes extreme poverty and an almost complete lack of resources.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect priv- with being deprived: when necessities are taken away, privation follows.

etymology_story.zh: retrovirus 是20世纪形成的科学术语，名称与 reverse transcriptase（逆转录酶）有关，retro- 同时呼应其“向后、逆向”的含义。这个名称突出RNA到DNA的逆转录过程，与通常所说的DNA到RNA的转录方向相反。
etymology_story.en: Retrovirus is a twentieth-century scientific term whose formation is associated with reverse transcriptase, while retro- also evokes its meaning of 'backward.' The name highlights the copying of RNA into DNA, reversing the direction of ordinary DNA-to-RNA transcription.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：retro-（逆向）+ virus（病毒）。主要词族：retroviruses（复数），retroviral（逆转录病毒的），retrovirology（逆转录病毒学），retrovirologist（逆转录病毒学研究者），antiretroviral（抗逆转录病毒的；抗逆转录病毒药物）；相关术语包括 reverse transcription（逆转录）和 reverse transcriptase（逆转录酶）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: retro- ('backward') + virus. Principal family members include retroviruses, retroviral, retrovirology, retrovirologist, and antiretroviral, which can be an adjective or a noun for a drug; related terms include reverse transcription and reverse transcriptase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有可在所有语境中替换的常用近义词。RNA virus（RNA病毒）是更大的类别；lentivirus（慢病毒）是逆转录病毒中的一个类群；oncovirus（致瘤病毒）按致瘤能力命名，可包括某些逆转录病毒，但两者范围并不相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common synonym that is interchangeable in every context. RNA virus is a broader category; lentivirus names a subgroup of retroviruses; oncovirus classifies viruses by their ability to cause tumors and overlaps with, but is not equivalent to, retrovirus.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: retro-＝逆向：记住RNA → DNA，就抓住了“逆转录”的核心。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Retro- means 'backward': remember RNA → DNA to capture the defining reverse-transcription step.

senses.meaning_zh: 血清学的；与血清研究或血清中的抗体、抗原检测有关的
senses.meaning_en: relating to the study or testing of blood serum, especially for antibodies or antigens

etymology_story.zh: 英语先由 sero-（血清，源自拉丁语 serum，原指乳清）和源自希腊语的 -logy（研究、学科）构成 serology，再形成形容词 serological。随着血清学的发展，这个词广泛用于描述血清中的抗体、抗原及相关检测。
etymology_story.en: English first formed serology from sero-, meaning blood serum and ultimately from Latin serum, originally 'whey,' and the Greek-derived element -logy, meaning study. The adjective serological developed from this noun and became widely used for investigations involving serum antibodies, antigens, and related tests.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词识别：sero-（血清）+ -log-（研究）+ -ical（……的）；也可按 serology → serological 的词族变化记忆，-logy 变为 -logical。主要词族：serum（血清；复数 serums 或 sera），serology（血清学；血清学检测），serologic（血清学的，同义形容词），serologically（从血清学上），serologist（血清学研究者），seropositive（血清检测阳性的）和 seronegative（血清检测阴性的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Recognizable modern structure: sero- ('serum') + -log- ('study') + -ical ('relating to'); alternatively, learn the family pattern serology → serological, with -logy becoming -logical. Principal family members include serum, with plurals serums or sera; serology; serologic, an equivalent adjective; serologically; serologist; seropositive; and seronegative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: serologic（血清学的）与 serological 基本同义；immunological（免疫学的）范围更广，包括血清检测以外的免疫现象；hematological（血液学的）涉及血液及相关疾病，并不限于血清或抗体检测。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Serologic is essentially synonymous with serological; immunological is broader and includes immune processes beyond serum testing; hematological concerns blood and blood disorders generally, rather than specifically serum or antibody testing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sero- 指血清，-logical 表示相关学科的：serological 就是“血清学的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sero- points to serum, and -logical marks a field-related adjective: serological means 'relating to serology.'

etymology_story.zh: solipsist 由哲学术语 solipsism 的词干加表示人的后缀 -ist 构成；solipsism 的拉丁语基础是 solus（独自的）和 ipse（自己）。它原指持唯我论立场的人，后来也被引申用于批评极端自我中心的人。
etymology_story.en: Solipsist was formed from the stem of the philosophical term solipsism with the person-denoting suffix -ist; the Latin elements behind solipsism are solus, meaning 'alone,' and ipse, meaning 'self.' The word later acquired a figurative use criticizing extreme self-centeredness.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：solips-（见于 solipsism 的词干）+ -ist（某种学说的信奉者）→ solipsist。常用词族：solipsism（唯我论）、solipsist（唯我论者）、solipsists（复数）、solipsistic（唯我论的；极端自我中心的）、solipsistically（以唯我论或自我中心的方式）；常用形容词形式是 solipsistic。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: solips-, the stem found in solipsism, + -ist, meaning an adherent of a doctrine, → solipsist. The usual family comprises solipsism, solipsist, plural solipsists, solipsistic, and solipsistically; solipsistic is the usual adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 哲学义没有严格等同的日常近义词。引申义可比较 egotist（自我中心者，强调自我重要性）、egoist（利己主义者，强调自身利益）和 narcissist（自恋者，强调自我迷恋）；solipsist 更突出把自己的主观世界当成唯一重要的世界。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The philosophical sense has no exact everyday synonym. In figurative use, egotist emphasizes self-importance, egoist emphasizes self-interest, and narcissist emphasizes self-admiration; solipsist particularly suggests treating one's own subjective world as the only world that matters.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: solus（独自）+ ipse（自己）：确定的世界里仿佛“只有我自己”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Solus, 'alone,' + ipse, 'self': imagine a world in which only your own self is certain.

morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tarot is a borrowing without a productive internal root-and-affix division. Common compounds include tarot card, tarot deck, tarot reading, and tarot reader; it has no substantial everyday inflectional or derivational family, and its final t is silent.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有严格覆盖全部词义的近义词。tarot cards 指具体牌具，cartomancy（纸牌占卜）也包括使用普通纸牌的占卜，divination（占卜）则涵盖更多方法；后两者都不表示塔罗纸牌游戏。

etymology_story.en: The verb twit is a shortened form of Middle English atwite, from Old English ætwītan, meaning to reproach or blame. The noun meaning 'a foolish person' appeared much later, and its precise origin is uncertain, so its relationship to the verb should not be treated as established.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 twit 作为完整词根处理，不再拆分古英语前缀。名词复数为 twits；动词形式为 twits、twitted、twitting，加 -ed 或 -ing 时末尾 t 双写；名词和动词拼写相同，但不能据此断言两者具有确定的现代派生关系。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats twit as a whole base rather than dividing it into its historical Old English elements. The noun plural is twits; the verb forms are twits, twitted, and twitting, with final t doubled before -ed and -ing; their identical spelling does not establish a certain modern derivational relationship.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 名词近义词 fool（傻瓜）适用范围更广，idiot（白痴、蠢货）通常语气更重；动词近义词 tease（取笑、逗弄）可以友善，而 twit 常指抓住某件具体的糗事挖苦。twit 的动词用法如今带有较旧的语感。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the noun, fool is broader and idiot is usually harsher. For the verb, tease can be affectionate, whereas twit typically targets a particular embarrassing fact or failure; the verb now sounds dated.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用两个场景记：叫人 a twit 是“傻瓜”；twit someone about a mistake 是“拿失误挖苦人”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember two scenes: calling someone a twit labels them a fool; twitting someone about a mistake means teasing them over it.

etymology_story.zh: acetylcholine 是由既有化学名称 acetyl（乙酰基）和 choline（胆碱）组合而成的现代科学词，表示胆碱的乙酸酯。acetyl 的词源可追溯至表示“醋”的拉丁语 acetum，而 choline 的名称与表示“胆汁”的希腊语 cholē 有关。
etymology_story.en: Acetylcholine is a modern scientific compound of acetyl and choline, naming the acetate ester of choline. Acetyl ultimately traces to Latin acetum, meaning 'vinegar,' while choline is named from Greek cholē, meaning 'bile.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：acetyl（乙酰基）+ choline（胆碱）→ acetylcholine（乙酰胆碱），常缩写为 ACh。直接相关复合词有 acetylcholinesterase（乙酰胆碱酯酶）；相关基础词族包括 acetyl、acetylate（使乙酰化）、acetylation（乙酰化）、choline、cholinergic（胆碱能的）和 anticholinergic（抗胆碱能的），其中后几项属于相关化学或功能词族，并非都直接派生自 acetylcholine。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: acetyl + choline → acetylcholine, commonly abbreviated ACh. A directly related compound is acetylcholinesterase; associated base-word families include acetyl, acetylate, acetylation, choline, cholinergic, and anticholinergic, although these related chemical and functional terms are not all direct derivatives of acetylcholine.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有可随意替换的常用近义词：ACh 是同一物质的缩写；neurotransmitter（神经递质）是上位类别名称；choline（胆碱）是相关前体物质，并不等于乙酰胆碱。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There are no freely interchangeable everyday synonyms: ACh abbreviates the same substance, neurotransmitter names its broader functional category, and choline is a related precursor rather than another name for acetylcholine.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 结构记名称：乙酰基接上胆碱；功能记“神经信号的化学信使”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Read the structure in the name: an acetyl group attached to choline; remember its role as a chemical messenger for nerve signals.

etymology_story.zh: 表示颠动的动词 bobble 通常分析为 bob（上下动）加表示小幅或反复动作的历史后缀 -le，后来发展出接球不稳及相关失误义。表示装饰小球的名词与 bob 的“小团、小球”义有关，并进一步用于织物毛球和发圈。
etymology_story.en: The movement verb bobble is generally analyzed as bob, meaning to move up and down, plus the historical suffix -le, suggesting small or repeated action; it later developed senses involving mishandling a ball and making errors. The decorative-ball noun is connected with bob in its small rounded-object sense and extended to fabric pills and hair ties.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史上可分析为 bob + -le，但现代英语通常把 bobble 作为完整词基使用，不把所有词义都机械解释为“反复跳动”。常用形式：bobbles（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、bobbled（过去式及过去分词）、bobbling（现在分词）、bobbly（有小球状凸起的；起毛球的）；相关复合词有 bobble hat（绒球帽）和 bobblehead（摇头玩偶）。
morphology_enriched.en: Historically, bobble can be analyzed as bob + -le, but modern English generally uses it as a whole base, and not every sense should be mechanically interpreted as repeated bouncing. Usual forms are bobbles, bobbled, bobbling, and bobbly; related compounds include bobble hat and bobblehead.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fumble overlaps with the handling-error sense and emphasizes clumsiness; pompom denotes a fluffy decorative ball; pill denotes a fabric fiber ball and also means to develop such balls. Each matches a different sense of bobble rather than replacing it across all uses.

etymology_story.zh: 英语于17世纪从印地语 ḍuṅgrī 借入这个词，原指一种粗棉布；这一布名通常被认为与孟买的 Dongri 地名有关。后来，复数 dungarees 从布料名称转指用这种结实面料制成的裤装。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word in the seventeenth century from Hindi ḍuṅgrī, a coarse cotton cloth whose name is traditionally associated with Dongri in Bombay. The plural dungarees later came to mean trousers made from this durable material.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 dungaree 是不可再作常规词缀分析的借入词。主要形式与构词：dungaree（布料）→ dungarees（裤装，通常只用复数）；dungaree + clad → dungaree-clad（穿粗棉布工作服或背带裤的，复合形容词）。dungaree fabric 中 dungaree 是名词作定语，并非独立的形容词词义。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dungaree is a borrowed base without a productive internal root-and-affix breakdown. Its principal forms and formations are dungaree, the fabric; dungarees, the normally plural garment noun; and dungaree + clad → dungaree-clad, a compound adjective meaning dressed in dungaree clothing. In dungaree fabric, the word is an attributive noun rather than a separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: denim（牛仔布）强调一种结实的斜纹棉布，与 dungaree 的布料义接近；overalls 在美式英语中通常对应英式英语的 dungarees，指背带工装裤；jeans（牛仔裤）通常没有护胸和肩带，对应 dungarees 的部分美式用法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Denim names a durable cotton twill and overlaps with the fabric sense of dungaree. Overalls is the usual American equivalent of British dungarees with a bib and shoulder straps. Jeans normally lack a bib and straps and overlap with the older American trouser sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“耐磨的布”记到“耐磨的裤”：dungaree 是布，dungarees 是裤装。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the material into the garment: dungaree is the tough cloth; dungarees are the trousers.

etymology_story.zh: epidermal 由 epidermis（表皮）的词干加形容词后缀构成。epidermis 经后期拉丁语来自希腊语，其中 epi- 表示“在……之上”，derma 表示“皮肤”，原义即覆盖在外面的皮层。
etymology_story.en: Epidermal was formed by adding an adjective suffix to the stem of epidermis. Epidermis came through Late Latin from Greek, combining epi-, meaning upon, with derma, meaning skin, to name the outer covering.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：epidermis 的词干 epiderm- + -al（……的）→ epidermal。主要相关词形包括 epidermis（表皮；复数 epidermises 或 epidermides）、epidermal（表皮的）、epidermally（在表皮上；经表皮地）、epidermic（表皮的，较少见）；相关构词形式 epidermoid 表示“表皮样的”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: epiderm-, the stem of epidermis, + -al → epidermal. Principal related forms include epidermis, with plurals epidermises or epidermides; epidermal; epidermally, meaning on or through the epidermis; and the less frequent adjective epidermic. The related formation epidermoid means resembling the epidermis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: epidermic 与 epidermal 意义最接近，但较少见；cutaneous（皮肤的）可涉及整个皮肤，而不局限于表皮；dermal（真皮的；皮肤的）在严格解剖语境中常特指表皮下面的真皮，因此不能一概替换 epidermal。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Epidermic is the closest equivalent but is less frequent. Cutaneous concerns the skin generally rather than specifically its outermost layer. Dermal can mean relating to the skin, but in precise anatomical contexts it often refers to the dermis beneath the epidermis.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: epi- 在上，derm- 皮肤：位于皮肤最外面的，就是 epidermal 所指的表皮层。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Epi- means upon and derm- means skin: think of the layer sitting on the outside.

etymology_story.zh: masque 于16世纪从法语 masque 借入英语，与 mask 同源，早期用于指戴面具的娱乐活动，后来专指一种华丽的宫廷表演。现代美容行业也使用 masque 这一拼写，表示敷在面部或头发上的护理产品。
etymology_story.en: Masque entered English from French masque in the sixteenth century and shares its origin with mask; it developed from masked entertainment into the name of an elaborate court performance. Modern beauty usage also adopts the spelling masque for treatments applied to the face or hair.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 masque 是整体借入的词基，末尾 -que 不是后缀；复数为 masques。主要复合形式包括 court masque（宫廷假面剧）、face masque（面膜）和 hair masque（发膜）；mask、masked、masking 属于同源词 mask 的词族，并非由 masque 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, masque is a borrowed base; its final -que is not a suffix. The plural is masques, and common combinations include court masque, face masque, and hair masque. Mask, masked, and masking belong to the family of the related word mask rather than being direct derivatives of masque.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pageant emphasizes spectacle or ceremonial display without necessarily having the courtly form of a masque. Masquerade usually means an event whose participants wear masks or disguises rather than a scripted dramatic entertainment. Mask is generally interchangeable with masque in beauty usage, while the historical theatrical term normally retains masque.

etymology_story.zh: mort 来自古法语 mort（死亡），更早可追溯到拉丁语 mors，其宾格为 mortem。狩猎中宣告猎物死亡的号声因其用途而得名，这一意义如今主要保留在历史和专业狩猎语境中。
etymology_story.en: Mort comes from Old French mort, meaning death, ultimately from Latin mors, whose accusative form is mortem. The hunting call was named for the death it announced, and this sense now survives mainly in historical and specialist hunting contexts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中的独立词 mort 不再细分，复数为 morts，也没有常用的直接派生词。相关拉丁词根 mort- 表示“死”，见于 mortal（终有一死的）、mortality（死亡率；必死性）、immortal（不朽的）、immortality（不朽）和 mortuary（停尸房；丧葬的）；这些是词根亲属，并非由狩猎名词 mort 逐一派生。
morphology_enriched.en: The independent English word mort is not further segmented in ordinary modern usage; its plural is morts, and it has no common direct derivatives. The related Latin root mort-, meaning death, appears in mortal, mortality, immortal, immortality, and mortuary. These are root relatives rather than successive derivatives of the hunting noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hunting-horn call（狩猎号角声）是上位表达，可以传达多种信号；death signal（死亡信号）说明功能，但不限定使用号角；death knell（丧钟声）通常指钟声或某事终结的征兆，并非 mort 的准确替换词。该词没有常用的精确同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hunting-horn call is a broader term covering several signals. Death signal describes the function without specifying a horn. Death knell normally refers to a bell or figuratively to an approaching end, so it is not an exact substitute. Mort has no common exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联想 mortal 中表示“死”的 mort-：mort 是把“猎物已死”吹出来的号声。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Recall mort- in mortal: the mort is the horn call that announces death.

etymology_story.zh: pituitary 源自拉丁语 pituitarius（黏液的），其基础词 pituita 意为“黏液”。这一名称反映了早期关于该腺体将脑中黏液排向鼻腔的错误认识；后来其内分泌功能得到认识，旧名称仍保留下来。
etymology_story.en: Pituitary derives from Latin pituitarius, meaning relating to mucus, from pituita, mucus. The name reflects an early mistaken belief that the gland drained mucus from the brain toward the nose; it remained after the gland's endocrine functions became understood.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构词可分析为 pituit-（黏液）+ -ary（与……有关的）；现代英语通常将 pituitary 作为整体使用，名词义由 pituitary gland 缩略而来，复数为 pituitaries。主要相关专业词包括 hypopituitary（垂体功能低下的）、hyperpituitary（垂体功能亢进的）、hypopituitarism（垂体功能减退症）、hyperpituitarism（垂体功能亢进症）和 panhypopituitarism（全垂体功能减退症）。
morphology_enriched.en: The historical formation is pituit-, meaning mucus, + -ary, meaning relating to; modern English generally treats pituitary as a whole word. The noun is shortened from pituitary gland, with the plural pituitaries. Principal related technical formations include hypopituitary, hyperpituitary, hypopituitarism, hyperpituitarism, and panhypopituitarism.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pituitary gland 是名词 pituitary 的完整形式；hypophysis 是同一器官的专业解剖学名称；hypophyseal 是与形容词 pituitary 对应的专业形容词。前两者指器官，后者表示“与该器官有关的”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pituitary gland is the full form of the noun pituitary. Hypophysis is the technical anatomical name for the same organ. Hypophyseal is a technical equivalent of the adjective pituitary: the first two name the organ, while the third describes something related to it.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 Teuton 源自拉丁语族名 Teutones 或 Teutoni，最初指曾与罗马人交战的古代条顿部族成员。后来这个名称被扩大用于日耳曼人，尤其是德国人；这种泛称如今已经过时。
etymology_story.en: English Teuton comes from the Latin ethnic names Teutones or Teutoni, originally referring to an ancient people who fought the Romans. The name was later extended to Germanic peoples, especially Germans, but this broader usage is now dated.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 Teuton 是不可再作实用拆分的族名词干，复数为 Teutons。词族包括 Teuton + -ic → Teutonic（条顿人的；日耳曼的）、Teutonic + -ally → Teutonically（以日耳曼式方式）；Teutonism（日耳曼特征或表达方式）较少见。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Teuton is an ethnic-name base without a useful smaller morphological division; its plural is Teutons. Its family includes Teuton + -ic → Teutonic, Teutonic + -ally → Teutonically, and the less common Teutonism, meaning a Germanic characteristic or expression.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: German（德国人）是现代中性称谓；Germanic（people）（日耳曼人或日耳曼诸民族）覆盖范围更广；Teuton 在历史语境中可专指古代条顿人，泛指德国人时则显得陈旧，有时带刻板印象。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: German is the normal neutral modern term; Germanic people covers a broader ethnic and linguistic grouping. Teuton can specifically identify a member of the ancient Teutones, while its broader use for a German sounds dated and may carry stereotypes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 Teuton 与 Teutonic 成对记：先是古代族名，后来扩大为日耳曼人的旧称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pair Teuton with Teutonic: an ancient people's name later became an older label for Germans.

etymology_story.zh: untrammelled 由否定前缀 un- 与 trammel 的过去分词构成，十八世纪已有使用。trammel 原指一种捕鱼网，后来引申为束缚或妨碍，因此 untrammelled 表示摆脱限制。
etymology_story.en: Untrammelled was formed from the negative prefix un- and the past participle of trammel, with use recorded in the eighteenth century. Trammel originally named a fishing net and later came to mean a restraint or hindrance, so untrammelled describes freedom from restrictions.

morphology_enriched.zh: un-（不）+ trammel（束缚）+ -ed（分词词尾）→ untrammelled（不受束缚的）；英式拼写通常双写 l，美式通常写 untrammeled。相关词形包括 trammel（网；束缚；限制）、trammels（束缚；限制）、trammelled／trammeled、trammelling／trammeling；untrammelled 通常作形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Un- meaning 'not' + trammel meaning 'restrain' + the participial ending -ed → untrammelled. British spelling normally doubles the l, while American spelling normally uses untrammeled. Related forms include the noun and verb trammel, plural trammels, trammelled/trammeled, and trammelling/trammeling; untrammelled normally functions as an adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: unrestricted 强调没有明确限制；unfettered 强调摆脱束缚；unbridled 强调缺乏控制，常带批评意味。untrammelled 较正式，强调没有外在约束或阻碍，褒贬取决于语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Unrestricted emphasizes the absence of explicit limits; unfettered emphasizes freedom from restraints; unbridled suggests a lack of control and is often critical. Untrammelled is relatively formal and stresses the absence of external constraints or obstacles, with approval or criticism supplied by context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: trammel 原是网：un- 把网解开，行动便不受束缚。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A trammel was a net: un- removes the net, leaving movement unrestricted.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在十九世纪借入法语 doctrinaire；这个名称曾用于法国复辟时期的一派政治人物，后来发展出拘泥理论、不顾实际的贬义。它与法语 doctrine 同源，最终可追溯至拉丁语 doctrina，意为教导或学说。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed doctrinaire from French in the nineteenth century; the name was associated with a political group during the French Restoration before developing its critical sense of rigid attachment to theory. It belongs to the same family as French doctrine, ultimately from Latin doctrina, meaning teaching or doctrine.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是法语借词，可按 doctrin-（与 doctrine“学说”相关的词干）+ 法语后缀 -aire 理解，不宜把 -aire 当作现代英语中可自由使用的普通后缀。词族包括 doctrine（学说）、doctrinal（教义的；学说的）、doctrinally（在教义上）、doctrinairism（教条主义，较少见）；同源相关词还有 indoctrinate（灌输思想）、indoctrination（思想灌输）、indoctrinated 和 indoctrinating。
morphology_enriched.en: This French borrowing can be understood as doctrin-, the stem associated with doctrine, plus French -aire; -aire is not a freely productive ordinary English suffix here. The family includes doctrine, doctrinal, doctrinally, and the less common doctrinairism. Related words sharing the underlying source include indoctrinate, indoctrination, indoctrinated, and indoctrinating.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dogmatic 强调武断地把观点当作真理；ideological 强调受某种思想体系支配，本身不一定贬义；rigid 强调不愿改变，适用范围更广。doctrinaire 特指让理论凌驾于实际情况之上。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dogmatic emphasizes asserting opinions as unquestionable truth; ideological emphasizes commitment to a system of ideas and is not necessarily negative; rigid more broadly describes unwillingness to change. Doctrinaire specifically criticizes allowing theory to override practical circumstances.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 doctrine“学说”联想：学说一旦压过事实，就成了 doctrinaire。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with doctrine: when the doctrine outweighs the facts, the approach becomes doctrinaire.

etymology_story.zh: hacksaw 是十九世纪出现的英语复合词，由 hack“砍、切”和 saw“锯”组成，逐渐成为细齿金属切割锯的名称。后来该工具名称也转用为动词，表示用钢锯切割。
etymology_story.en: Hacksaw arose in nineteenth-century English as a compound of hack, meaning cut or chop, and saw, becoming the name of a fine-toothed saw used for metal. The tool name was subsequently also used as a verb meaning to cut with that tool.

morphology_enriched.zh: hack（砍切）+ saw（锯）→ hacksaw（钢锯）；名词通过零派生转为动词 hacksaw（用钢锯锯）。常用词形有复数及第三人称单数 hacksaws、现在分词 hacksawing、过去式 hacksawed，过去分词可用 hacksawed 或 hacksawn；相关复合表达有 hacksaw blade（钢锯条）和 hacksaw frame（钢锯架）。
morphology_enriched.en: Hack meaning 'cut or chop' + saw → the compound noun hacksaw; conversion without an added suffix produces the verb hacksaw. Forms include plural and third-person singular hacksaws, present participle hacksawing, past tense hacksawed, and past participles hacksawed or hacksawn. Related compounds include hacksaw blade and hacksaw frame.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: saw 是各种锯及锯切动作的总称；handsaw 强调手动操作，日常常指木工手锯；cut 是不限定工具的切割。hacksaw 明确指钢锯这种工具或使用它的动作，通常涉及金属。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Saw is the general term for the tool or cutting action; handsaw emphasizes manual operation and often refers to a woodworking saw; cut does not specify a tool. Hacksaw identifies the particular fine-toothed tool or the action of using it, usually on metal.

etymology_story.zh: hoar 源自古英语 hār，意思是灰白的或年老的。头发变白与霜的白色外观促成了相关用法，后来 hoar 也可作名词表示白霜；现代英语中这些独立用法主要见于文学语言。
etymology_story.en: Hoar comes from Old English hār, meaning grey, grey-haired, or old. The shared whiteness of ageing hair and frost supported its related uses, and hoar also became a noun for hoarfrost; these independent uses are now chiefly literary.

morphology_enriched.zh: hoar 是现代英语中不可再作实用拆分的词根；hoar + -y → hoary（灰白的；古老陈腐的），hoary 去 y 加 -iness → hoariness（灰白；陈腐），hoary 变 y 为 i 加 -ly → hoarily（灰白地；陈腐地，较少见）。复合词 hoar + frost → hoarfrost（白霜）。
morphology_enriched.en: Hoar is a modern English base without a useful smaller division. Hoar + -y → hoary, meaning greyish-white or old and overfamiliar; replacing the final y with -iness produces hoariness, and changing y to i before -ly produces the uncommon hoarily. Hoar + frost forms the compound hoarfrost.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hoary 比 hoar 更常见，既可指灰白，也可贬指陈腐；frosty 强调有霜或寒冷，也可形容态度冷淡；grey-haired 直指头发灰白，语气中性。hoar 带明显文学色彩，常联系白发、白霜与衰老。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hoary is more usual than hoar and can describe either greyish whiteness or something tediously old; frosty emphasizes frost or cold and can also describe an unfriendly manner; grey-haired neutrally describes hair colour. Hoar has a distinctly literary tone and commonly evokes white hair, frost, or age.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由表示“在、向”的 a- 与 stern（船尾）组合而成，并非始于17世纪。它在航海语境中既表示船尾或船后的位置，也表示朝船尾方向运动，进而表示船舶倒驶。
etymology_story.en: The word combines a-, meaning 'at' or 'toward,' with stern, and predates the seventeenth century. In nautical use, it describes both a position at or behind the stern and movement stern-first through the water.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：a-（在、向）+ stern（船尾）→ astern。现代英语中通常将其作为固定航海副词使用，没有常用的直接派生词；以 stern 为基础的相关词有 sternward/sternwards（向船尾）和 sternmost（最后部的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: a- ('at, toward') + stern → astern. In modern English it functions as an established nautical adverb with no common direct derivatives; related formations from stern include sternward/sternwards and sternmost.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: aft（在船尾或向船尾）通常指船体内部的后部位置或方向；abaft（在……后方）主要表示相对于船上某参照点的位置；backward（向后）是通用词，不限于航海。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Aft usually identifies a position or direction toward the rear within a vessel; abaft mainly locates something behind a reference point aboard; backward is a general term unrestricted to nautical contexts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 stern＝船尾：在船尾、在船后，或让船尾先走。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor everything to stern: at the stern, behind the stern, or moving stern-first.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在18世纪从法语 bivouac 借入该词，其更早来源是瑞士德语中表示“额外守卫、辅助夜间警戒”的词。词义从野外守卫及其驻地发展为临时营地，随后也用作表示临时宿营的动词。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed bivouac from French in the eighteenth century; its earlier source was a Swiss German term for an additional guard or auxiliary night watch. The meaning developed from an outdoor watch and its quarters to a temporary camp, and then also to the act of camping.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词中，bivouac 是不可再作常用词缀拆分的词基，名词可零派生为动词。词族及屈折形式：bivouacs（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、bivouacked（过去式及过去分词）、bivouacking（现在分词或动名词）、bivouacker（临时露营者）；接 -ed、-ing、-er 时通常在 c 后加 k。
morphology_enriched.en: Synchronically, bivouac is a base without a useful productive affix breakdown; its noun and verb are related by conversion. Family and inflected forms: bivouacs, bivouacked, bivouacking, and bivouacker; a k is normally inserted after c before -ed, -ing, and -er.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: camp（营地；露营）适用范围最广，可包括设施完善的营地；encampment（营地）较正式，常指军队或群体的驻地；encamp（扎营）强调建立营地，而 bivouac 更突出临时性和简陋的遮蔽条件。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Camp is the broadest noun or verb and can involve well-equipped accommodation; encampment is a more formal noun often used for military or group camps; encamp emphasizes establishing a camp, while bivouac particularly suggests a temporary stay with minimal shelter.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“野外守夜”记到“就地过夜”：一个词兼指临时营地和露宿动作。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect an outdoor night watch with staying out for the night: bivouac names both the temporary camp and the act.

etymology_story.zh: 该词源自古英语 hider，意为“到这里”，与 here（这里）同源。中古英语时期，其辅音和拼写逐渐发展为 th；现代主要保留于文学表达和 hither and thither 等固定短语中。
etymology_story.en: Hither descends from Old English hider, meaning 'to this place,' and is historically related to here. Its consonant and spelling developed into th during Middle English, and it now survives chiefly in literary expressions and phrases such as hither and thither.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 hither 作为整体词基，不宜机械拆成 here 加现代后缀。相关构词有 hither + to → hitherto（迄今）和 hither + -ward/-wards → hitherward/hitherwards（向这里，罕用）；thither（到那里）与 whither（到哪里）是历史上平行的方向副词，并非其派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat hither as a whole base in modern English rather than mechanically dividing it into here plus a modern suffix. Related formations include hither + to → hitherto ('until now') and hither + -ward/-wards → hitherward/hitherwards ('toward here,' rare); thither and whither are historically parallel directional adverbs, not derivatives of hither.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: here（这里；到这里）是现代日常用词，可表示位置，也可配合动作表示方向；this way（往这边）常用于指路或招呼，强调行进方向；hither 本身强调“到说话者这里”，语体带有文学或古风色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Here is the everyday modern word and can indicate either location or destination; this way commonly gives directions or calls someone over, emphasizing a route; hither specifically expresses movement toward the speaker's location and sounds literary or archaic.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 hither 记成“带箭头的 here”：这里 ← 到这里。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of hither as here with a movement arrow: toward here.

etymology_story.zh: 英语约在1600年前后借入拉丁语 invidiosus，其基础是 invidia（嫉妒、怨恨），更早与 invidere（以嫉妒的眼光看待）有关。词义由引起嫉妒或怨恨，发展为形容招致反感的不公平比较，以及容易得罪人的处境。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word around 1600 from Latin invidiosus, based on invidia ('envy, resentment') and ultimately related to invidere ('to look upon with envy'). Its meanings developed from arousing envy or resentment to describing objectionably unfair comparisons and situations likely to provoke ill will.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可按拉丁来源词干 invidi- + 形容词后缀 -ous 理解，但 invidi- 不是可自由使用的英语词根，开头 in- 也不是表示否定的前缀。常用词族：invidious（形容词）、invidiously（副词）、invidiousness（名词）；envy 与其历史同源，但不是它的现代派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: A learned analysis is the Latin-derived stem invidi- + adjectival -ous, but invidi- is not a freely usable English root, and the initial in- is not a negative prefix. The standard family consists of invidious, invidiously, and invidiousness; envy is historically related but is not a modern derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: unfair（不公平的）最宽泛，不一定强调他人的反应；discriminatory（歧视性的）突出依据群体身份等因素给予差别待遇；unenviable（令人不羡慕的、难堪的）强调处境不理想，而 invidious 尤其突出可能招致怨恨或批评。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Unfair is broad and need not emphasize anyone's reaction; discriminatory highlights unequal treatment based on factors such as group identity; unenviable describes an undesirable situation, whereas invidious particularly suggests the risk of resentment or criticism.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“怨恨”这一核心：不公平的比较招怨，难做的选择也招怨。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep resentment at the center: unfair comparisons breed it, and difficult choices can attract it.

senses.collocation_zh: 政治上的权力狂热；对妄自尊大的指责
senses.sentence_en: Critics saw his demand for absolute control as a sign of megalomania.
senses.sentence_zh: 批评者认为，他要求掌握绝对控制权，表现出了对权力的过度迷恋。

senses.meaning_zh: 夸大妄想〔传统心理学用语〕
senses.meaning_en: delusions of extraordinary greatness, power, or importance, in older psychological usage
senses.english_definition: In older psychological usage, megalomania is a state in which someone falsely believes they possess extraordinary greatness, power, or importance.
senses.collocation_en: suffer from megalomania; a case of megalomania
senses.collocation_zh: 患有夸大妄想；一例夸大妄想

senses.sentence_zh: 那份19世纪的记述将他认为自己统治着世界的信念称为夸大妄想。

etymology_story.zh: 英语在19世纪借入法语 mégalomanie，该词由源自希腊语、表示“巨大”的 megalo- 与表示“狂热、疯狂”的 -mania 组合而成。它最初用于描述对自身伟大或权势的妄想，后来也广泛用于批评极端自大和权力欲。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French mégalomanie in the nineteenth century, combining Greek-derived megalo- ('great, large') with -mania ('madness, obsession'). Originally used for delusions of personal greatness or power, it later gained broader use for extreme self-importance and hunger for power.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：megalo-（巨大、伟大）+ -mania（狂热、痴迷）→ megalomania。标准词族包括 megalomaniac（名词：妄自尊大者；形容词：妄自尊大的）、megalomaniacal（形容词：妄自尊大的）、megalomaniacally（副词：妄自尊大地）；另有较少见的形容词 megalomanic。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: megalo- ('great, large') + -mania ('obsession, madness') → megalomania. The standard family includes megalomaniac (noun and adjective), megalomaniacal (adjective), and megalomaniacally (adverb); megalomanic is a less common adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: grandiosity（夸大自我）突出对自身能力或地位的不切实际的高估；egotism（自我中心、自负）突出过度关注和谈论自己；narcissism（自恋）突出自我迷恋和对赞赏的需求，而 megalomania 更强调极端的伟大感与权力欲。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Grandiosity emphasizes an exaggerated estimate of one's abilities or status; egotism emphasizes excessive self-focus and self-promotion; narcissism emphasizes self-admiration and a need for admiration, while megalomania especially stresses extreme greatness and power.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: megalo-＝巨大，-mania＝痴迷：把“我很伟大”放大到失去分寸。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Megalo- means huge and -mania means obsession: imagine 'I am great' magnified beyond all proportion.

usage_note: 常含巧妙、隐蔽或欺骗意味；可以是较大策略中的一次具体计谋。

senses.meaning_zh: 为取得优势而采用的计谋；巧计
senses.meaning_en: a clever plan or trick used to gain an advantage
senses.english_definition: A stratagem is a clever plan, often involving deception, that you use to achieve something or gain an advantage.
senses.collocation_en: a clever stratagem; devise a stratagem
senses.collocation_zh: 巧妙的计谋；设计计谋
senses.sentence_en: Pretending to lose interest was a stratagem to get the seller to lower the price.
senses.sentence_zh: 假装失去兴趣是为了让卖家降价而采用的计谋。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语等欧洲语言传入英语，最终源于希腊语 stratēgēma，意为“将领的行动或计谋”，与 stratēgos“将领”有关。其意义后来从军事计谋扩展到一般竞争或交往中为取得优势而采用的巧计。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French and other European transmission routes, ultimately from Greek stratēgēma, meaning a general's action or device, related to stratēgos, 'general.' Its meaning broadened from military tricks to clever devices used to gain an advantage in other situations.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 stratagem 作为整体词基，不宜强行拆成可自由组合的英语词素。复数为 stratagems；少见派生词 stratagemic（计谋的）＝stratagem＋-ic。strategy（策略）、strategic（战略性的）、strategist（策略家）属于历史同源词群，并非直接由 stratagem 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, stratagem is normally treated as a whole base rather than split into productive English elements. Its plural is stratagems; the uncommon adjective stratagemic is formed with -ic. Strategy, strategic, and strategist belong to the historically related vocabulary group but are not direct derivatives of stratagem.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ruse（诡计）尤其强调欺骗；ploy（招数）强调为影响对方而采取的具体手段；tactic（战术、手段）可以完全不涉及欺骗。stratagem 强调经过巧妙设计、旨在取得优势的计谋。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A ruse particularly emphasizes deception; a ploy is a specific move intended to influence someone; a tactic need not involve deception at all. Stratagem emphasizes an ingenious plan designed to secure an advantage.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“将领出计”这一历史核心：从战场上的巧计，记到任何较量中的计谋。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a general devising a clever move: a battlefield trick becomes a stratagem in any contest.

etymology_story.zh: Technicolor 是20世纪初创立的彩色电影技术商标名，其中 Tech 是向麻省理工学院致意，部分创办人曾在那里求学。由于这种电影技术以浓艳色彩著称，该名称后来也被用于形容绚丽的色彩和格外鲜明的体验。
etymology_story.en: Technicolor originated as an early twentieth-century trademark for color motion-picture technology; Tech honored the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, where some of its founders had studied. Its association with rich screen colors later encouraged figurative uses for brilliant colors and exceptionally vivid experiences.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是专名式创制词，可识别出 Tech（历史上指向麻省理工学院）和 color（颜色），中间的 -ni- 不属于具有独立意义的常用英语词缀。相关形式包括小写的 technicolor，以及英式普通描写用法中的 technicolour；商标通常保留拼写 Technicolor。没有常用的规则派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: This is a coined proper name with recognizable elements Tech, historically referring to MIT, and color; the intervening -ni- is not a standard English affix with an independent meaning. Related forms include lowercase technicolor and British technicolour in ordinary descriptive use; the trademark normally retains Technicolor. There is no common productive family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: vivid（鲜明的）强调视觉或印象清晰强烈；vibrant（鲜艳活泼的）强调色彩富有生气；multicolored（多色的）只说明颜色种类多。形容词 Technicolor 还常带有老电影般浓艳、梦幻的联想；这些词不能替代其电影工艺专名义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Vivid emphasizes strong, clear colors or impressions; vibrant suggests lively, energetic color; multicolored simply means having several colors. The adjective Technicolor often adds an association with richly colored old films or dreamlike intensity; these alternatives do not replace its technical trademark meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象老电影突然亮起浓艳色彩：Technicolor 从彩色电影工艺，延伸到“鲜艳得像电影”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture an old movie bursting into rich color: Technicolor moves from a film process to anything vividly cinematic.

usage_note: 常修饰 criticism、analysis、comment，侧重表达直接、深刻、有力度，不只是语气大声。

senses.meaning_zh: 言辞或分析犀利有力、切中要害的
senses.meaning_en: expressed sharply and forcefully, with clear insight
senses.english_definition: A trenchant comment or analysis expresses a clear, forceful judgment that gets directly to the important issues.
senses.collocation_en: trenchant criticism; a trenchant analysis
senses.collocation_zh: 犀利的批评；切中要害的分析

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语借自古法语 trenchant，原是表示“切割”的动词的现在分词，具有“切割的、锋利的”之意。刀刃的锋利后来被比喻为言辞、批评和分析的犀利有力。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English from Old French trenchant, the present participle of a verb meaning 'to cut,' and originally meant cutting or sharp. The sharpness of a blade later became a metaphor for incisive, forceful language, criticism, and analysis.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 trenchant 作为整体形容词词基，其 -ant 结尾源于历史借词结构，不应机械拆成 trench＋-ant。常用派生词为 trenchantly（犀利有力地）＝trenchant＋-ly，以及 trenchancy（犀利、有力）＝将词尾 -ant 换为 -ancy；trenchantness（犀利）较少见。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats trenchant as a whole adjective base; its historical -ant ending should not be mechanically analyzed as English trench plus -ant. Its main derivatives are trenchantly, formed with -ly, and trenchancy, formed by replacing -ant with -ancy; trenchantness is less common.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: incisive（透彻犀利的）突出洞察力和准确性；pointed（尖锐的）强调评论具有明确针对性；caustic（刻薄尖酸的）强调讽刺和伤人。trenchant 兼具切中要害和表达有力的特点，但不必带有刻薄意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Incisive stresses penetrating insight and precision; pointed emphasizes a remark's direct relevance or critical target; caustic stresses biting sarcasm or harshness. Trenchant combines sharp insight with forceful expression without necessarily implying cruelty.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把评论想成刀锋：一刀切入要害，就是 trenchant。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Imagine a comment as a sharp blade: it cuts straight to the heart of the issue.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语已有 valaunce，指床或华盖边缘垂下的装饰布，其更早来源尚不确定，传统上有人将它与法国地名 Valence 联系起来。后来它也指窗帘顶部的短幔，并通过外形类比用于汽车下部的遮盖板。
etymology_story.en: Middle English valaunce referred to decorative fabric hanging from a bed or canopy; its deeper origin is uncertain, although a connection with the French place name Valence has traditionally been proposed. The word later covered short window draperies and, by analogy of shape and position, lower vehicle panels.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 valance 是不可作常规词缀分析的名词词基；复数为 valances。派生形容词 valanced（带装饰短幔的）由 valance 去掉词尾 e 后加 -ed 构成；没有常用的庞大派生词族。window valance、bed valance 和 front valance 是名词组合。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, valance is a noun base without a productive internal affix analysis; its plural is valances. The adjective valanced, meaning fitted with a valance, is formed by dropping final e and adding -ed. There is no extensive common derivative family; window valance, bed valance, and front valance are noun combinations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pelmet（窗帘盒、窗帘顶饰）尤用于英式英语，可指覆盖窗帘顶部装置的装饰结构；bed skirt（床裙）仅对应床下垂布义，常见于美式英语；drapery（帷幔）范围更广。valance 的织物义强调短幅、沿边缘垂挂，这些近义词不能直接替代其汽车义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pelmet, especially in British English, can denote a decorative structure covering curtain fittings; bed skirt corresponds only to the fabric hanging around a bed and is common in American English; drapery is much broader. The fabric sense of valance emphasizes a short hanging border; these alternatives do not directly replace its automotive sense.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember a short border hanging from an edge: above a window, around a bed, or below a car bumper.

etymology_story.zh: 该词于16世纪出现，由 way“道路”和 lay“放置、布置”构成，可能受到荷兰语或低地德语中类似表达的影响。它原指沿途设伏，后来也可用于较轻松的场景，表示突然拦住别人说话。
etymology_story.en: The word appeared in the sixteenth century as a compound of way, 'road,' and lay, 'place or set,' possibly influenced by similar Dutch or Low German expressions. It originally referred to ambushing someone along a route and later developed the milder sense of unexpectedly stopping someone for a conversation.

morphology_enriched.zh: way（道路）＋lay（布置、设下）→waylay，主要用作及物动词。第三人称单数为 waylays；过去式和过去分词均为 waylaid；现在分词为 waylaying。少见施事名词 waylayer（伏击者、拦截者）＝waylay＋-er。
morphology_enriched.en: Way, meaning a road or route, plus lay, meaning place or set, forms waylay, used primarily as a transitive verb. Its forms are waylays, waylaid for both past tense and past participle, and waylaying. The uncommon agent noun waylayer is formed with -er.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ambush（伏击）更明确强调隐蔽等待后的突然袭击；intercept（拦截）侧重在对方到达目的地之前将其截住，语气较中性；accost（贸然上前搭话）强调唐突或咄咄逼人的接近。waylay 的共同核心是在人行进途中突然拦住，既可指袭击，也可指攀谈。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ambush more explicitly involves a surprise attack from concealment; intercept neutrally emphasizes stopping someone before they reach their destination; accost emphasizes approaching someone boldly or intrusively. Waylay centers on unexpectedly stopping someone along their route, whether for an attack or a conversation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: way 是路，lay 是设下：在别人路上设个拦截点，就能记住“伏击”和“拦住攀谈”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Way is the route; lay suggests setting something in place: set an interception point on someone's route, for an ambush or a chat.

etymology_story.en: Bod is an informal shortening of body with a history extending back several centuries. It retains the physical meaning of body and also shares its use for a person, especially in informal British English.

morphology_enriched.zh: body（身体；人）截短为 bod，bod 本身没有可独立分析的现代前后缀；复数为 bods。来源词的常用词族包括 bodily（身体的；亲身地）、bodied（具有某种身体或形体的，常用于复合词）、bodiless（无形体的）、embody（体现；使具体化）、embodiment（体现；化身）和 disembodied（脱离身体的）；它们并非由 bod 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Bod is formed by clipping body and has no independently meaningful modern prefix or suffix; its plural is bods. Common relatives of the source word include bodily, bodied, bodiless, embody, embodiment, and disembodied; these are not direct derivatives of bod.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: body（身体）是中性通用词；physique（体格）侧重身体的结构、肌肉和外形；person（人）对应 bod 的指人义，但没有其随意、略带诙谐的语气。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Body is the neutral general term; physique emphasizes physical build, musculature, and appearance; person matches the human-reference sense of bod without its casual, slightly humorous tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: body 缩短成 bod：词变短，语气也更随意；既可说身体，也可借指人。

etymology_story.zh: dint 源自古英语 dynt，原意为“打击；一击”。by dint of 从“凭借打击的力量”发展为“凭借某种力量、努力或手段”，而“凹痕”义则指打击留下的结果。
etymology_story.en: Dint comes from Old English dynt, meaning a blow or stroke. By dint of developed from the force of blows into a broader expression for achieving something through effort or other means, while the dent sense names the mark a blow leaves.

morphology_enriched.zh: dint 在现代英语中是不可再拆分的基本词；同形名词和动词构成名动转换关系。屈折形式为 dints、dinted、dinting；dinted 可作分词修饰语，表示“有凹痕的”，没有常用的进一步派生词。by dint of 是固定表达，其中 dint 通常不变复数。
morphology_enriched.en: Dint is a morphologically simple modern word, with noun and verb uses related by conversion. Its inflected forms are dints, dinted, and dinting; dinted can function as a participial modifier meaning dented, and there are no common further derivatives. In the fixed expression by dint of, dint normally remains singular.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: through（通过）适用范围最广；by means of（借助）中性地指出所用方法或工具；by virtue of（由于；凭借）常强调身份、条件或某种特质，而 by dint of 常突出费力争取。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Through is the broadest equivalent; by means of neutrally identifies a method or instrument; by virtue of often points to status, circumstances, or a quality, whereas by dint of commonly emphasizes strenuous effort.

mnemonic_anchor.en: A blow supplies force and leaves a dent: by dint of means succeeding through that force or effort.

morphology_enriched.zh: drunk（喝醉的）+ -ard（表示具有某种特征的人，常含贬义）→ drunkard；复数为 drunkards。相关常用词族包括 drink（喝；饮料）、drinks、drank、drunk、drinking、drinker（饮酒者）、drunken（醉酒的）、drunkenly（醉醺醺地）和 drunkenness（醉酒状态）；drunkenness 来自 drunken，而非 drunkard。
morphology_enriched.en: Drunk + -ard, a suffix forming a person characterized by something, often disapprovingly, gives drunkard; its plural is drunkards. etymology_story.zh: fave 是 favorite／favourite 在20世纪形成的非正式缩略形式，流行文化和娱乐报道促进了它的传播。后来它又通过名动转换进入网络用语，表示把内容标为最爱、喜欢或收藏。
etymology_story.en: Fave developed in the twentieth century as an informal shortening of favorite or favourite, spreading through popular culture and entertainment writing. It later acquired a verb use online for marking content as a favorite, like, or saved item.

morphology_enriched.zh: favorite／favourite 截短并调整拼写为 fave；结尾的 e 帮助标示 /eɪ/，不是派生后缀。fave 可作名词、形容词和动词；相关形式有 faves、faved、faving。来源词族包括 favorite／favourite（最喜爱的人或事物；最喜爱的）、favoritism／favouritism（偏袒）和 favor／favour（好感；恩惠；偏爱）；这些不是由 fave 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Favorite or favourite is shortened and respelled as fave; the final e helps signal /eɪ/ and is not a derivational suffix. Fave functions as a noun, adjective, and verb, with the forms faves, faved, and faving. The source family includes favorite or favourite, favoritism or favouritism, and favor or favour; these are not direct derivatives of fave.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: favorite／favourite 是中性、适用范围更广的对应词；darling 指深受喜爱的人或事物，常突出群体的宠爱；like 作网络动词时通常指点赞，而 fave 也可能表示收藏，具体功能取决于平台。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Favorite or favourite is the neutral, more widely usable equivalent; darling describes someone or something especially cherished, often by a group; like as an online verb usually means registering approval, while fave can also involve saving an item, depending on the platform.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: favorite 缩成 fave：最爱的人、最爱的东西，以及把内容“标成最爱”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Shorten favorite to fave: your favorite thing, your favorite choice, or the action of marking something as a favorite.

etymology_story.zh: featherweight 把 feather“羽毛”和 weight“重量”组合起来，以羽毛的轻盈表示很轻的重量；它早期用于赛马负重，19世纪也用于拳击级别。后来该词扩展为“极轻的”，并借“分量不足”比喻能力、影响力或内容不足。
etymology_story.en: Featherweight combines feather and weight, using a feather's lightness as its image; early uses concerned racing weights, and boxing adopted the term in the nineteenth century. It later broadened to mean extremely light and, figuratively, lacking ability, influence, or substance.

morphology_enriched.zh: feather（羽毛）+ weight（重量）→ featherweight，是名词复合词，也可作形容词；名词复数为 featherweights，没有常用的后缀派生词。相关构词包括 featherlight（轻如羽毛的）以及 weight 构成的 lightweight（轻量级；轻的）、bantamweight（雏量级）、welterweight（次中量级）、middleweight（中量级）和 heavyweight（重量级）；这些是相关复合词，不是 featherweight 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Feather + weight forms the compound featherweight, which also functions as an adjective; its noun plural is featherweights, and it has no common suffix-derived forms. Related compounds include featherlight and the weight compounds lightweight, bantamweight, welterweight, middleweight, and heavyweight; these are related formations rather than direct derivatives of featherweight.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lightweight 可表示重量轻，也可比喻缺乏能力，但在运动中是另一个级别；featherlight 强调轻如羽毛，通常没有运动级别义；insubstantial 对应比喻义，强调内容、依据或重要性不足。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lightweight can mean physically light or figuratively lacking ability, but names a different sporting division; featherlight emphasizes extreme physical lightness and normally has no weight-division meaning; insubstantial matches the figurative sense of lacking content, support, or importance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 羽毛的重量：身体上很轻，是羽量级；比喻没分量，就是影响小、内容浅。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The weight of a feather suggests physical lightness, a light sporting division, and figuratively little influence or substance.

forms: 可数名词；动物一只螯可说 a pincer，两只为 pincers；工具钳常用复数 pincers。
family: pincers 钳子、双螯；pincer-shaped 钳状的。

morphology.text: pincer + shaped → pincer-shaped（钳状的）；这是复合形容词。pincer 整词作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 英语从古法语表示钳子的词借入，背后是表示夹、捏的动词；后来又用来称甲壳动物能够夹住东西的螯。

usage_note: 本课讲蟹、龙虾等动物的螯；pincer movement 是两路夹击的固定表达，工具义也常见于复数。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语传入英语，源头与古法语 pincier（夹、捏）有关，早期用于指夹持工具。后来它也用于动物的螯，并进一步以两颚合拢的形象表示两侧夹击。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French and is ultimately connected with Old French pincier, meaning to pinch, initially referring to a gripping tool. It later named animals' gripping claws and supplied the image of two sides closing together in a military attack.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 pincer 作为借入词整体识别，不宜机械拆成 pinc + -er。常用形式及相关构词：pincers（复数；也指钳子）、pincer-shaped（钳状的）、pincer movement（钳形包围行动）、pincer grip（拇指与另一手指相对夹取的动作）；形容词用法由名词转用而来。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, pincer is best treated as a borrowed base rather than mechanically divided into pinc + -er. Common forms and related constructions include pincers, the plural and the tool name; pincer-shaped; pincer movement; and pincer grip, a grasp between the thumb and another finger. The adjective develops from the noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: claw 泛指动物的爪或螯，不一定具有两部分相对夹合的结构；pliers 通常指用于夹持、弯折或剪切的钳子，而 pincers 尤其常用于拔钉；forceps 指镊子或医用钳，常用于精细操作。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Claw is a broader animal term and does not necessarily imply two opposing gripping parts. Pliers commonly grip, bend, or cut, whereas pincers are especially associated with pulling out nails. Forceps are instruments for precise gripping, particularly in medical work.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“两边合拢夹住”这一动作：工具是钳，动物的是螯，战术是夹击。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture two sides closing to grip: a tool's jaws, an animal's claw, or two attacking forces.

etymology.text: 17世纪英语借用拉丁语 trans（横过）和 sectus（切过的）造词；想象一刀横着切过去。

usage_note: transect 强调横着切过或穿过某物；通常直接接宾语，比一般的 cross 更书面。

senses.meaning_zh: 横切；横断；横穿

senses.english_definition: If something transects an area or structure, it passes across it or cuts through it.

senses.meaning_zh: 用于生态调查等的样线；样带

senses.english_definition: A transect is a line or narrow strip across an area along which researchers record plants, animals, or other features.

etymology_story.zh: transect 于17世纪进入英语，由拉丁语 trans（横过）与 secare（切）的分词词干 sect- 构成。其“横切”的基本含义后来发展出调查方法中的名词义，指横贯研究区域的样线或样带。
etymology_story.en: Transect entered English in the seventeenth century from Latin trans, meaning across, and sect-, the participial stem of secare, meaning to cut. Its basic idea of cutting across later developed into the survey noun for a sampling line or strip across an area.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词分析为 trans-（横过，在本词中表现为 tran-）+ sect（切的黏着词根）。词族包括 transects（动词第三人称单数或名词复数）、transected（过去式及过去分词）、transecting（现在分词）、transection（横断；横切术）；名词 transect 由动词转用，且重音前移。相关同根词有 section（部分；切面）和 dissect（解剖）。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure is trans-, meaning across and appearing here as tran-, plus the bound root sect, meaning cut. The family includes transects, transected, transecting, and transection, meaning a cutting across, especially a surgical division. The noun transect comes from the verb with stress shifted to the first syllable. Related root-family words include section and dissect.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cross 泛指横过，不强调切开；bisect 强调分成两部分，几何语境中常指等分；traverse 强调穿越某一区域或地形。transect 则常用于正式或技术语境，突出横向穿过或切断。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cross broadly means to go across without implying a cut. Bisect emphasizes division into two parts, often equal parts in geometry. Traverse emphasizes passage across an area or terrain. Transect is more technical and highlights a crosswise passage or division.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tran- 表示“横过”，sect 表示“切”：动词横切过去，名词沿横贯路线取样；动词重后，名词重前。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Across plus cut gives the verb; sampling along a line across an area gives the noun. Stress the second syllable for the verb and the first for the noun.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 troubadour 是整体借入的名词，不宜强行拆成英语词根和词缀。常用形式为复数 troubadours；troubadour-like（像行吟诗人的）是可按需构成的复合形容词，troubadour poetry（行吟诗人的诗歌）是名词修饰结构；本词没有常用的英语动词或副词派生形式。

etymology_story.en: English borrowed the nineteenth-century German term Antisemitismus, which gained currency in late nineteenth-century political campaigning as a supposedly racial label for existing hostility to Jews. Although its formation invokes the word Semitic, its historical and ordinary meaning specifically concerns prejudice or hostility against Jewish people.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可分析为 anti-（反对）+ Semit-（与 Semite、Semitic 有关的词干）+ -ism（思想、态度或实践）；整体词义已经固定，不能按字面扩展为反对所有使用闪米特语族语言的人。核心词族为 antisemite（反犹者）和 antisemitic（反犹的）；常见异体拼写有 anti-Semitism、anti-Semite、anti-Semitic。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be analyzed as anti-, meaning against, plus Semit-, the stem associated with Semite and Semitic, plus -ism, indicating an ideology, attitude, or practice. Its established meaning cannot be expanded literally to hostility toward all speakers of Semitic languages. Core family members are antisemite and antisemitic; spelling variants include anti-Semitism, anti-Semite, and anti-Semitic.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Anti-Jewish prejudice states the target of the prejudice most directly. Jew-hatred emphasizes intense hostility. Anti-Judaism usually emphasizes religious opposition to Judaism; it can overlap historically with antisemitism but is not identical to it.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Anti- signals opposition and -ism an attitude or ideology; remember the established whole-word meaning: prejudice, hostility, or discrimination against Jews.
