etymology_story.zh: 借自拉丁语 coitus，原义为“走到一起、结合”，源于 coire（共同前往、结合），由 co-（一起）与 ire（去）构成。这个表示结合的拉丁语名词也用于性交，英语沿用了其正式和医学意义。
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from Latin coitus, meaning 'a coming together or union,' from coire, formed from co-, 'together,' and ire, 'to go.' The Latin noun also referred to sexual union, and English adopted that formal and medical meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 coitus 是整体借词，不是由有生产力的英语词缀直接构成；历史上可分析为 co-（一起）+ it-（去的拉丁语词干）+ -us（拉丁语名词词尾）。主要同族形式有 coital（性交的）、coitally（以性交方式；少用）、precoital（性交前的）、postcoital（性交后的）；coition（性交；少用）是同源名词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats coitus as a whole loanword, not a productive English affix formation; historically, it contains co-, 'together,' it-, a Latin stem meaning 'go,' and the Latin noun ending -us. Related forms include coital, coitally, which is uncommon, precoital, and postcoital; coition is an uncommon cognate noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sexual intercourse（性交）是最直接、通用的正式对应表达；copulation（交配）更偏生物学，尤其常用于动物；sex（性行为）较日常，范围也可能比性交更广。coitus 的医学和学术色彩最明显。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sexual intercourse is the most direct general formal equivalent; copulation is more biological and is especially common when discussing animals; sex is more everyday and may cover a wider range of activities. Coitus has a distinctly medical or scholarly tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史词根逻辑：co- 一起 + it- 去 → 走到一起 → 身体结合。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical root logic: co-, together, plus it-, go, gives 'coming together' and then physical union.

etymology_story.zh: 来自法语 défrayer，意思是“支付费用、承担开支”，与 frais（费用）有关。英语保留了这一财务含义，通常以 cost、expenses 等表示费用的词作宾语。
etymology_story.en: From French défrayer, meaning 'to pay expenses,' related to frais, 'expenses.' English retained this financial meaning, typically using the verb with objects such as cost and expenses.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中应整体分析为 defray，不宜按 de- + fray（磨损；争斗）解释。屈折形式为 defrays、defrayed、defraying；派生词有 defrayal、defrayment（费用的支付）、defrayable（可予支付的）和 defrayer（付款者），这些派生形式均较少用。

Inflections are defrays, defrayed, and defraying; derivatives include defrayal and defrayment, meaning payment of expenses, defrayable, and defrayer, all of which are uncommon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pay（支付）用途最广，可接账单、金额或收款人；cover（足以支付；承担）强调资金能够负担某项支出；reimburse（报销；偿还）强调归还别人已经垫付的钱。defray 正式地强调承担费用，可以只承担其中一部分。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pay is the broadest term and can take a bill, amount, or recipient; cover emphasizes providing enough money for an expense; reimburse means paying someone back for money already spent. Defray formally emphasizes meeting an expense and can refer to only part of it.

etymology_story.zh: 由英语 fly 与 wheel 合成，其中 fly 与机械部件的快速旋转有关，wheel 意为“轮”。机械飞轮能够储存旋转能量并维持运动，这一特点后来发展出“持续积累动力、相互促进的循环”这一比喻义。
etymology_story.en: Formed from English fly and wheel, with fly referring to rapid revolving motion in machinery. Because a mechanical flywheel stores rotational energy and sustains motion, the word later acquired a figurative meaning involving accumulated momentum and reinforcing progress.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词为 fly + wheel → flywheel，是名词复合词，复数为 flywheels。没有常用的词缀派生词族；常见扩展组合有 flywheel effect（飞轮效应）、flywheel energy storage（飞轮储能）和 flywheel system（飞轮系统）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: fly + wheel → flywheel, a compound noun with the plural flywheels. There is no common affix-derived word family; established combinations include flywheel effect, flywheel energy storage, and flywheel system.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: inertia wheel（惯性轮）是强调转动惯性的近义技术表达；energy-storage rotor（储能转子）强调储能功能，但适用范围不完全相同；virtuous cycle（良性循环）可对应其正面的比喻义，强调良好结果相互促进，而 flywheel 更突出动力的积累和延续。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Inertia wheel is a near-equivalent technical expression emphasizing rotational inertia; energy-storage rotor emphasizes storage but does not have exactly the same scope. Virtuous cycle overlaps with the positive figurative sense, emphasizing mutually beneficial results, while flywheel highlights accumulating and sustained momentum.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Once a heavy wheel is spinning, its inertia keeps it going; reinforcing activities can build momentum the same way.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按学术词干 gnost-（知识、认知）+ -ic（与……有关的）理解；同一形式既作形容词，也作表示信徒的名词，名词复数为 Gnostics。主要同族词有 Gnosticism（诺斯替主义）、gnosis（灵性知识）和少用的 gnostically（以诺斯替主义方式）；agnostic（不可知论的；不可知论者）、agnosticism（不可知论）共享“知识”这一词根，但不是诺斯替宗教身份的简单反义词。
morphology_enriched.en: The learned structure is gnost-, 'knowledge or knowing,' plus -ic, 'relating to'; the same form functions as an adjective and as a noun for an adherent, with Gnostics as the noun plural. synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym. etymology_story.zh: 该词由希腊语源构词成分 histo- 和 pathology 组成：希腊语 histos 原指织物，后来借指由细胞构成的组织。词义因此是研究组织中疾病变化的学问。
etymology_story.en: The word combines the Greek-derived element histo- with pathology: Greek histos meant a woven fabric and later supplied a term for bodily tissue. The resulting word names the study of disease-related changes in tissues.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：histo-（组织）+ pathology（病理学）；pathology 内部可分析为 patho-（疾病）+ -logy（研究、学科）。常用词族：histopathologist（组织病理学家）、histopathological / histopathologic（组织病理学的）、histopathologically（从组织病理学角度）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: histo- (tissue) + pathology; pathology itself contains patho- (disease) + -logy (study or field of knowledge). Common family members: histopathologist, histopathological, histopathologic, and histopathologically.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tissue pathology（组织病理学）是接近的同义表达；histology（组织学）研究组织结构，范围不限于疾病；cytopathology（细胞病理学）侧重单个细胞或细胞群，与强调组织结构的 histopathology 有别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tissue pathology is a near-equivalent expression. Histology studies tissue structure more broadly, including healthy tissue. Cytopathology focuses on individual cells or cell groups, whereas histopathology also examines tissue architecture.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 组织像细胞织成的布：histo- 看这块“布”，pathology 看它哪里病了。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of tissue as fabric woven from cells: histo- identifies the fabric, and pathology investigates its disease.

etymology_story.zh: leaven 经古法语 levain 进入英语，最终源于拉丁语 levamen（使之轻松之物、缓解），与 levare（抬起、减轻）有关。它先指使面团膨起的发酵物，后来引申为能改变整体性质或增添活力的因素。
etymology_story.en: Leaven entered English through Old French levain, ultimately from Latin levamen, meaning relief or an alleviating substance, related to levare, 'to raise or lighten.' Its meaning expanded from a substance that raises dough to an influence that changes or enlivens a whole.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 leaven 是不可再作常用词缀拆分的词基，名词可直接转为动词。屈折与派生形式：leavens、leavened、leavening；leavened（发酵膨起的）、unleavened（未用发酵剂的）、leavening（发酵作用；发酵剂）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, leaven is a base without a productive internal affix division; the noun also functions as a verb through conversion. Inflected and derived forms include leavens, leavened, leavening, and unleavened; leavened and unleavened are adjectives, while leavening also names the process or agent.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: yeast（酵母）是 leaven 的一种，不能涵盖所有膨松剂；raising agent（膨松剂、起发剂）是较宽泛的烘焙术语；enliven（使活跃）接近其比喻动词义，但不一定带有“少量加入、影响整体”的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Yeast is one kind of leaven, rather than every possible raising agent. Raising agent is a broader baking term. Enliven matches the figurative verb, but does not necessarily suggest a small addition influencing a larger whole.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一小点让整体“发起来”：面团膨起，文章和气氛也能变活。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A little makes the whole rise: it lifts dough physically and lifts writing or conversation figuratively.

etymology_story.zh: 乐器名经法语 mandoline 传入英语，源于意大利语 mandolino，是 mandola（一种较大的同族拨弦乐器）的指小形式。厨房工具义沿用了法语 mandoline 的名称，英语中也保留 mandoline 这一拼法。
etymology_story.en: The instrument's name came through French mandoline from Italian mandolino, a diminutive of mandola, a larger related string instrument. The kitchen-tool sense also uses the French name mandoline, a spelling retained in English.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 mandolin 作为整体词基记忆，不把结尾 -in 当作能自由构词的英语后缀；其指小结构属于意大利语词源。词族：mandolins（复数）、mandolinist（曼陀林演奏者）、mandolinists（演奏者的复数）；mandoline 是相关借词形式，常用于厨房工具义。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, mandolin is treated as a whole base; its ending -in is not a productive English suffix, and the diminutive structure belongs to its Italian history. Family forms include mandolins, mandolinist, and mandolinists; mandoline is a related borrowed form commonly used for the kitchen tool.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 乐器义没有完全等同的常用同义词：lute（鲁特琴）是较宽泛的相关乐器名称，mandola（曼多拉琴）是同族中通常音域更低的乐器。厨房义可近似表达为 vegetable slicer（蔬菜切片器），但后者也包括其他结构的切片工具。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The instrument has no exact common synonym: lute is a broader related instrument term, and mandola names a usually lower-pitched relative. For the kitchen sense, vegetable slicer is a near-equivalent, but also covers slicing tools of other designs.

etymology_story.zh: metronome 经法语 métronome 进入英语，由希腊语 metron（度量、尺度）和 nomos（规则、法则）构成。这个名称表达的是用规则节拍来衡量并约束演奏速度。
etymology_story.en: Metronome entered English through French métronome, formed from Greek metron, 'measure,' and nomos, 'rule or law.' The name expresses the idea of regulating musical speed through a measured, regular beat.

morphology_enriched.zh: 词源构词可分析为 metro-（度量）+ -nome（规则），不能把这里的 metro- 理解为“地铁”；现代英语中通常将 metronome 作为完整词基。词族：metronomes（复数）、metronomic / metronomical（节拍器的；极有规律的）、metronomically（像节拍器一样有规律地）。
morphology_enriched.en: Its learned historical structure is metro- (measure) + -nome (rule); metro- here does not mean an underground railway. Modern English usually treats metronome as a complete base. Family forms include metronomes, metronomic, metronomical, and metronomically.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tempo keeper is a broader functional description covering a person or tool. A click track supplies preset rhythmic clicks for recording or performance. Timekeeper is broader still and need not refer to a musical device.

etymology_story.zh: palpitate 源于拉丁语 palpitare，意为扑动、颤动或急跳，与 palpare（轻触、抚摸）有关。英语保留了颤动的意思，并常用它描述人能明显感觉到的异常心跳。
etymology_story.en: Palpitate comes from Latin palpitare, meaning to flutter, tremble, or throb, related to palpare, 'to touch gently or stroke.' English retained the trembling sense and commonly uses the word for an unusually noticeable heartbeat.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可作学习性分析：palpit-（源于拉丁语的“扑动、跳动”词干）+ -ate（动词词尾）；palpit- 不是独立的现代英语单词。词族：palpitates、palpitated、palpitating，以及 palpitation（悸动；心悸），其复数 palpitations 常指阵阵心悸。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful learned analysis is palpit- (a Latin-derived stem meaning flutter or throb) + -ate (a verb ending); palpit- is not an independent modern English word. Family forms include palpitates, palpitated, palpitating, and palpitation; the plural palpitations commonly refers to episodes of noticeable heartbeat.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pound（怦怦猛跳）强调心跳有力；throb（搏动、抽痛）强调反复的脉动，也可描述疼痛；flutter（扑动、轻颤）强调轻快或不规则的颤动。palpitate 更正式，描述心跳时常带异常明显的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pound emphasizes forceful beating. Throb emphasizes repeated pulses and can also describe pain. Flutter suggests light, rapid, or irregular movement. Palpitate is more formal and, for the heart, often suggests an unusually noticeable beat.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把心跳想成胸口里扑动的小翅膀：扑扑颤动，就是 palpitate。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Imagine a tiny wing fluttering inside your chest: that noticeable flutter is the core image of palpitate.

etymology_story.zh: quicksand 可追溯到古英语，由表示“活的”的 quick 的早期形式与 sand“沙”组成。沙层仿佛会活动，因此得名，后来又比喻令人越陷越深的困境。
etymology_story.en: Quicksand goes back to Old English and combines an early form of quick, meaning 'alive', with sand. The apparently moving sand later became a metaphor for situations that draw people into deeper trouble.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代结构为 quick + sand，是复合名词；其中 quick 保留“活的、会动的”这一历史词义。主要形式有 quicksand 和复数 quicksands，后者尤其用于比喻义；没有常用的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern structure is quick + sand, a compound noun whose first element preserves the historical meaning 'alive or moving'. The main forms are quicksand and the plural quicksands, especially in figurative use; there are no common direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: quagmire 指松软泥沼，也常比喻复杂难解的困境；bog 通常指泥炭质湿地；morass 指沼泽，也可指混乱复杂的局面。quicksand 特指不稳定的饱水沙层，比喻时突出越挣扎越难脱身。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Quagmire means soft, boggy ground or a complicated predicament; bog usually refers to wet, peaty land; morass means a swamp or a confusing situation. Quicksand specifically involves unstable, water-saturated sand and figuratively emphasizes being drawn further into difficulty.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: quick 古义是“活的”：仿佛会动的沙 → 流沙 → 越陷越深的困境。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Quick once meant 'alive': seemingly living sand → quicksand → trouble that pulls you deeper.

etymology_story.zh: sloop 借自荷兰语 sloep，原指一种小船。英语中它成为一种帆装类型的名称；历史海军术语 sloop 或 sloop-of-war 的范围更广，并不一定指单桅船。
etymology_story.en: Sloop was borrowed from Dutch sloep, a word for a small boat. In English it became the name of a sailing rig, although the historical naval terms sloop and sloop-of-war could describe vessels with other mast arrangements.

morphology_enriched.zh: sloop 在现代英语中是不可再作常用词根词缀拆分的借词；复数为 sloops。相关复合词有 sloop-rigged“采用单桅纵帆装的”和 sloop-of-war“历史上的一类小型军舰”，后者复数为 sloops-of-war。
morphology_enriched.en: Sloop is a borrowed base word with no productive internal root-and-affix breakdown in modern English; its plural is sloops. Related compounds include sloop-rigged, meaning fitted with a sloop rig, and sloop-of-war, a historical category of small warship, with the plural sloops-of-war.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sailboat 是“帆船”的上位词；cutter 通常指前帆配置不同、常带多面前帆的单桅帆船；yacht 按休闲或竞赛用途分类，可以是帆船或机动艇。sloop 主要按桅杆与帆装结构命名。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sailboat is the general category; cutter usually describes a single-masted sailing vessel with a different headsail arrangement, commonly using multiple headsails; yacht describes a leisure or racing vessel and may be powered by sails or an engine. Sloop primarily identifies the mast and sail arrangement.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Attach sloop to one silhouette: one mast, a mainsail behind it, and a headsail ahead.

etymology_story.zh: smut 属于表示污点、污垢的日耳曼语词族，与德语 Schmutz“污垢”等词相关。它从黑色污物扩展到植物上的黑色病斑，又由“脏”的评价引申为淫秽言语或内容。
etymology_story.en: Smut belongs to a Germanic family of words for stains and dirt, with relatives such as German Schmutz. Its associations with black dirt extended to dark fungal growth on plants, while the evaluative idea of 'dirtiness' produced the sense of obscene material or talk.

morphology_enriched.zh: smut 是现代英语中的基本词，名词可直接转作动词。主要形式为 smuts、smutted、smutting；smut + -y → smutty“淫秽的；沾有黑污的”，加后缀时双写 t；进一步有 smuttier、smuttiest、smuttily“淫秽地”和 smuttiness“淫秽；污秽”。
morphology_enriched.en: Smut is a base word in modern English, and the noun also functions as a verb by conversion. Main forms include smuts, smutted, and smutting; smut + -y gives smutty, meaning obscene or marked with black dirt, with the final t doubled. Further forms include smuttier, smuttiest, smuttily, and smuttiness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 色情义中，pornography 通常指旨在引起性兴奋的露骨内容，obscenity 强调淫秽冒犯性，smut 常带轻蔑色彩，也包括下流笑话和言谈；污物义中，soot 专指不完全燃烧产生的黑色烟灰，并不能替代其他词义中的 smut。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: In the sexual sense, pornography usually means explicit material intended to arouse, obscenity emphasizes offensive indecency, and smut is often dismissive and also covers dirty jokes or talk. In the dirt sense, soot specifically means black combustion residue and cannot replace smut in its other meanings.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“黑脏”一条线：物上的黑污、庄稼的黑粉、言语里的“脏”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the idea of dark dirt: black marks on things, dark spores on crops, and 'dirty' words.

etymology_story.zh: strobe 是 stroboscope“频闪观测仪”的缩略形式；后者由源自希腊语 strobos“旋转”的成分和表示观察仪器的 -scope 构成。早期装置用于观察周期性运动，缩略词后来广泛用于频闪照明。
etymology_story.en: Strobe is a shortened form of stroboscope, formed from an element based on Greek strobos, meaning 'whirling', and -scope, indicating an instrument for viewing. Early instruments helped observers examine periodic motion, and the shortened word later became widely used for flashing lights.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代 strobe 是 stroboscope 的截短词，名词可直接转作动词；屈折形式有 strobes、strobed、strobing。相关词族有 stroboscope“频闪观测仪”、stroboscopy“频闪观测法”、stroboscopic“频闪的”和 stroboscopically“以频闪方式”；复合词有 strobe light“频闪灯”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern strobe is a clipping of stroboscope and also functions as a verb by conversion; its inflected forms are strobes, strobed, and strobing. The related family includes stroboscope, stroboscopy, stroboscopic, and stroboscopically; a common compound is strobe light.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: flash 可指一次闪光或闪光装置；flashing light 泛指闪烁的灯，不限定闪烁频率；flicker 指轻微或不规则地闪动。strobe 突出短促、周期性重复的闪光，常产生动作被分割的视觉效果。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Flash can mean a single burst of light or a flash device; flashing light is a broad term without a particular flashing rate; flicker suggests slight or irregular changes in light. Strobe emphasizes brief, regularly repeated flashes, often creating an interrupted-motion effect.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“观察旋转”想到“连续闪光”：每闪一下，就像给运动截取一帧。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect viewing rotation with repeated flashes: each flash captures another frame of movement.

etymology_story.en: Timpani was borrowed from Italian as the plural of timpano, ultimately tracing through Latin tympanum to Greek tympanon, meaning 'drum'. English retained the Italian plural to name the tunable drums used in orchestras.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是保留意大利语屈折形式的借词：词干 timpan- + 单数词尾 -o → timpano；词干 timpan- + 复数词尾 -i → timpani。现代英语通常使用复数 timpani；timpanist“定音鼓演奏者”由词干加 -ist 构成，复数为 timpanists；相关英语名称为 kettledrum“定音鼓”。
morphology_enriched.en: This borrowing preserves Italian inflection: the stem timpan- + singular -o gives timpano, while timpan- + plural -i gives timpani. Modern English normally uses the plural timpani; timpanist, meaning a player of these drums, adds -ist to the stem and has the plural timpanists. Kettledrum is a related English name.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: kettledrums 是最接近的同义词，名称突出锅形鼓身；drums 是涵盖各种鼓的上位词；percussion 指打击乐器或打击乐声部，范围更广。timpani 特指定音鼓，通常成组配置并可调至明确音高。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Kettledrums is the closest synonym and highlights the bowl-shaped bodies; drums is the broader category; percussion refers to a much wider family of instruments or an orchestral section. Timpani specifically names drums that are normally grouped together and tuned to definite pitches.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture bowl-shaped drums with adjustable pitch; the Italian ending -i reminds you that they usually come as a group.

etymology_story.zh: 这个词的历史词根来自拉丁语 venter（腹部）和 loqui（说话），字面意象是“用腹部说话的人”。早期人们曾把这种仿佛来自体内或别处的声音与神秘力量联系起来，后来该词主要指运用声音错觉的表演者。
etymology_story.en: Its historical roots are Latin venter, meaning 'belly,' and loqui, meaning 'to speak,' giving the image of a 'belly-speaker.' Voices apparently coming from within the body or elsewhere were once associated with supernatural powers; the word later became chiefly a term for an entertainer.

morphology_enriched.zh: 古典词素分析：ventri-（腹部）+ loqu-（说话）+ -ist（从事者）；这些词根在现代英语中不能独立成词。主要词族：ventriloquism、ventriloquy（腹语术），ventriloquial、ventriloquistic（腹语的），ventriloquize／ventriloquise（表演腹语）。
morphology_enriched.en: Classical combining elements: ventri- 'belly' + loqu- 'speak' + -ist 'practitioner'; the roots do not function as independent modern English words. Principal family members include ventriloquism and ventriloquy, the art; ventriloquial and ventriloquistic, describing the art; and ventriloquize/ventriloquise, to perform it.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: A puppeteer operates puppets without necessarily using ventriloquism; an impressionist imitates other people's voices or mannerisms; a voice actor supplies a character's voice. These roles overlap with ventriloquist, but none specifically requires the illusion that the voice comes from elsewhere.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经后期拉丁语借入希腊语 apotheōsis，原指“使人成为神”，与 theos（神）同源。它从实际的尊奉为神，延伸为极度推崇，进而表示某种品质或成就的最高体现。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word through Late Latin from Greek apotheōsis, meaning 'making someone a god,' ultimately related to theos, 'god.' Its meaning extended from literal deification to supreme glorification and then to the highest embodiment of a quality or achievement.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常将 apotheosis 作为整体借词；历史上可追溯至希腊语 apo- + theō-（使成为神）+ -sis（行为或过程），不能把 apo- 机械译成“离开”来解释全词。主要词族：apotheosize／apotheosise（神化；极度推崇），apotheotic（神化的；极致的）；复数为 apotheoses。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats apotheosis as a whole borrowed word. Historically, it reflects Greek apo- + theō- 'make divine' + -sis 'action or process'; translating apo- mechanically as 'away' does not explain the whole word. Principal family members are apotheosize/apotheosise, to deify or glorify, and apotheotic, relating to deification or supreme achievement; the plural is apotheoses.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Deification directly denotes making or treating someone as a god. Epitome emphasizes the embodiment of characteristic qualities without necessarily implying supreme excellence. Pinnacle emphasizes the highest point of achievement or development rather than a perfect embodiment.

etymology_story.zh: 这个医学名称借自德语 Atherosklerose，由表示“粥”的希腊语 athērē 和表示“硬化”的希腊语词素构成。“粥”形容斑块中软烂的脂质物质，“硬化”则描述受累动脉壁的病理变化。
etymology_story.en: This medical term was borrowed from German Atherosklerose and combines Greek elements meaning 'gruel' and 'hardening.' The gruel image refers to the soft fatty material within plaques, while hardening describes pathological changes in the affected artery walls.

morphology_enriched.zh: 医学构词公式：ather/o（粥样脂质物；粥样斑块）+ scler/o（硬）+ -osis（病理状态），也可分析为 athero- + sclerosis（硬化）。主要词族：atherosclerotic（动脉粥样硬化的）；相关同根医学词包括 atheroma（粥样斑块）、atheromatous（粥样斑块的）、atherogenesis（粥样斑块形成）和 atherogenic（促粥样斑块形成的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Medical word-building formula: ather/o 'gruel-like fatty material or plaque' + scler/o 'hard' + -osis 'pathological condition'; it can also be analyzed as athero- + sclerosis 'hardening.' The principal derivative is atherosclerotic. Related words sharing the ather- element include atheroma, a fatty plaque; atheromatous, relating to such plaques; atherogenesis, plaque formation; and atherogenic, promoting plaque formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: arteriosclerosis（动脉硬化）是动脉壁增厚、变硬和弹性下降的较宽泛概念，atherosclerosis 是其中以粥样斑块为特征的一类；atheromatosis（粥样斑块形成或广泛存在）强调斑块病变；atheroma（粥样斑块）指病变本身，而不是整个疾病过程。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Arteriosclerosis is the broader category of arterial thickening, hardening, and loss of elasticity; atherosclerosis is a form characterized by fatty plaques. Atheromatosis emphasizes the formation or widespread presence of these lesions. Atheroma names a plaque or lesion rather than the entire disease process.

etymology_story.zh: coed 起源于19世纪美国英语，是 coeducational 或 coeducation 的缩略形式。它既用来描述男女共同接受教育，也曾特别用作这类院校中女学生的称呼；后来形容词义扩展到男女共同参与的活动和团体。
etymology_story.en: Coed arose in nineteenth-century American English as a shortening of coeducational or coeducation. It described education for both sexes and also became a label specifically for female students at such institutions; its adjectival use later extended to mixed groups and activities.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词关系：co-（共同）+ education（教育）→ coeducation（男女同校教育）；coeducation + -al → coeducational（男女同校的）；缩略为 coed，也写作 co-ed。相关词族：coeducationally（以男女同校的方式）；名词复数为 coeds。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: co- 'together' + education → coeducation; coeducation + -al → coeducational; shortening produces coed, also written co-ed. The related adverb is coeducationally, meaning in a coeducational manner; the noun plural is coeds.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: coeducational（男女同校的）较正式，主要描述教育机构或教育制度；mixed（男女混合的）在英式英语中常用于学校，也可用于其他群体；female student（女学生）对应 coed 的旧名词义，本身不说明学校是否男女同校。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Coeducational is more formal and primarily describes educational institutions or systems. Mixed commonly describes schools in British English and can also describe other groups. Female student corresponds to the dated noun sense of coed but does not itself specify whether an institution admits both sexes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: co“共同”+ ed“教育”：男女一起上学；形容词再扩展为男女一起参加。
mnemonic_anchor.en: co 'together' + ed 'education': men and women learn together, then participate together more broadly.

etymology_story.zh: 这个词由 dis- 与 favour 构成，favour 经古法语来自拉丁语 favor，意为“好感、支持”。由“缺乏好感或支持”，发展出不赞成、失宠，以及动词中给予较少支持或不利待遇的含义。
etymology_story.en: The word combines dis- with favour, which came through Old French from Latin favor, meaning 'goodwill or support.' The absence or reversal of goodwill developed into disapproval and loss of favour, and into the verbal senses of withholding support or treating less advantageously.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词公式：dis-（否定；相反）+ favour（好感；支持）→ disfavour；名词和动词同形。动词变化：disfavours、disfavoured、disfavouring；美式对应拼写为 disfavor、disfavors、disfavored、disfavoring。基础词族包括 favour、favourable、favourably、unfavourable、unfavourably。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: dis- 'negation or reversal' + favour 'goodwill or support' → disfavour, used as both noun and verb. Verb forms are disfavours, disfavoured, and disfavouring; American spellings are disfavor, disfavors, disfavored, and disfavoring. The base family includes favour, favourable, favourably, unfavourable, and unfavourably.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: disapproval（不赞成）侧重负面评价；dislike（不喜欢）侧重个人感受；disadvantage（不利处境；使处于不利地位）侧重实际待遇或后果。disfavour 可以兼指态度上的不认可和支持、待遇上的不利。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Disapproval emphasizes a negative judgment; dislike emphasizes personal feeling; disadvantage emphasizes an adverse position or the act of creating one. Disfavour can cover both an unfavourable attitude and reduced support or less favourable treatment.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dis- 逆转 favour“青睐”：不再青睐，就是不赞成、失宠或受到不利待遇。
mnemonic_anchor.en: dis- reverses favour: goodwill disappears, producing disapproval, lost support, or less favourable treatment.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 expungere，意为“用点标记删去”，由 ex-（向外）和 pungere（刺、点）构成。古代抄写时可用点标示应删除的文字，后来词义扩展为彻底删除或抹去。
etymology_story.en: Expunge comes from Latin expungere, meaning to mark for deletion with dots, formed from ex- meaning out and pungere meaning to prick. The practice of marking unwanted writing with dots developed into the broader meaning of removing or erasing something completely.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 expunge 为基础词，不宜把历史词根 pung- 当作可自由使用的现代词素。屈折变化：expunges、expunged、expunging；词族：expungement（删除；记录清除）、expunction（删除，较正式）、expunger（删除者或删除工具）、expungable（可删除的）、unexpunged（未被删除的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, expunge functions as the base; its historical root pung- is not a freely usable modern morpheme. Inflections: expunges, expunged, expunging. Family: expungement and the more formal expunction, both meaning removal; expunger, a person or tool that removes something; expungable, capable of being removed; and unexpunged, not removed.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: delete（删除）侧重移除文字或数据；erase（擦除）强调使痕迹消失；expunge（彻底抹去）更正式，尤其常用于记录，也可用于记忆。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Delete focuses on removing text or data; erase emphasizes making marks or traces disappear; expunge is more formal and especially associated with records, though it can also refer to memories.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史逻辑：给文字点上删除记号 → 从记录中彻底抹去。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical hook: mark unwanted words with dots, then remove them completely.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语已有 instep，由 in 和 step 构成，当时就用于指脚部的这一位置。它延续为上部脚背的名称，并引申指鞋子覆盖该处的部分。
etymology_story.en: Instep is recorded in Middle English as a formation from in and step, already referring to this part of the foot. It retained that anatomical meaning and also came to describe the corresponding part of a shoe.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可识别为 in + step，但应整体记忆为“脚背”，不能按两个成分直接推导词义。复数：insteps；较少见的派生形式：instepped（具有某种脚背的），常见于 high-instepped（脚背高的）和 low-instepped（脚背低的）等复合形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: The components in + step remain recognizable, but instep should be learned as a whole meaning the upper part of the foot. Plural: insteps. The uncommon derivative instepped occurs chiefly in compound adjectives such as high-instepped and low-instepped.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Top of the foot is an everyday near-equivalent; dorsum of the foot is the anatomical term and can cover a broader area; arch refers to the foot's curved supporting structure and is related but not interchangeable.

etymology_story.zh: Lint 可追溯至中古英语中表示亚麻或亚麻纤维的词，与 linen（亚麻布）有历史联系，后来指敷伤口的软质材料和松散的织物绒屑。计算机用法源于名为 lint 的代码检查工具，并进一步产生了“检查代码”的动词用法。
etymology_story.en: Lint goes back to a Middle English word for flax or flax fibers, historically related to linen, and later referred to soft wound-dressing material and loose textile fibers. Its computing use comes from the code-checking tool named lint, whose name also became a verb.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代 lint 是基础词，无需拆分。形容词：lint + -y → linty（有绒屑的），比较级 lintier，最高级 lintiest；名词：lintiness（绒屑多的状态）。计算机词族：lints、linted、linting，以及 lint + -er → linter（代码静态检查工具）；常见复合形式：lint-free（无绒屑的）、lint roller（粘毛滚筒）、lint filter（绒屑过滤网）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern lint is a simple base. Adjective: lint + -y → linty, with lintier and lintiest; noun: lintiness, the state of being linty. Computing forms include lints, linted, and linting; lint + -er gives linter, a static code-checking tool. Common compounds include lint-free, lint roller, and lint filter.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 纤维义：fluff（绒毛）更强调轻软蓬松，fuzz（细绒毛）也可指附着表面的短毛，lint 尤指脱落并聚集的织物纤维。计算机义：check（检查）范围最广，analyze（分析）不限于查错，lint 专指按照规则对代码作静态检查。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For fibers, fluff emphasizes softness and lightness, while fuzz can include short fibers attached to a surface; lint especially means shed textile fibers. In computing, check is broad and analyze need not involve error detection, while lint specifically means checking code statically against rules.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 衣服上找细小绒屑；代码里找细小问题。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Find tiny fibers on clothes; find tiny problems in code.

senses.meaning_zh: 谄媚的；卑躬屈膝的；过分顺从的
senses.meaning_en: excessively eager to please or obey someone, especially someone powerful
senses.english_definition: If you describe someone as obsequious, you disapprove of how excessively they try to please or obey someone who has power or influence.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 obsequiosus（顺从的），与 obsequi（顺从、迎合）有关，其中 sequi 意为“跟随”。英语中的词义由顺从发展为带贬义的过分服从、讨好权势者。
etymology_story.en: Obsequious comes from Latin obsequiosus, meaning compliant, related to obsequi, to comply with or accommodate, and ultimately to sequi, to follow. In English, the meaning developed from obedience into disapproving descriptions of excessive submission and eagerness to please.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可将 obsequious 作为形容词基础词记忆，词尾 -ous 是形容词后缀，但 obsequi- 不是独立英语词。词族：obsequious + -ly → obsequiously（谄媚地）；obsequious + -ness → obsequiousness（谄媚；卑躬屈膝）；另有较少见的相关名词 obsequience（过分顺从）。
morphology_enriched.en: Learn obsequious as the adjective base: -ous is an adjective suffix, but obsequi- is not an independent English word. Family: obsequious + -ly → obsequiously, in an excessively submissive manner; obsequious + -ness → obsequiousness, excessive submissiveness. The related noun obsequience is uncommon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: servile（奴颜婢膝的）强调有失尊严的服从；sycophantic（阿谀奉承的）强调为谋利而奉承权势者；fawning（讨好献媚的）强调外露、殷勤的讨好表现。Obsequious 兼有过分顺从和急于取悦之意。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Servile emphasizes degrading submission; sycophantic emphasizes flattering influential people for advantage; fawning emphasizes conspicuous displays of eager affection or approval. Obsequious combines excessive compliance with eagerness to please.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“跟随”记到“事事顺从”，再到“顺从得失去尊严”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow → comply with every wish → become excessively submissive.

senses.meaning_zh: 黑曜石；通常呈黑色的天然火山玻璃
senses.meaning_en: natural volcanic glass, usually dark, formed when lava cools rapidly
senses.english_definition: Obsidian is a natural volcanic glass that forms when lava cools rapidly and is usually black or another dark color.
senses.collocation_en: an obsidian blade; an obsidian arrowhead

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 obsidianus，这是 Obsianus 的变体；后者与罗马作者老普林尼记载的 Obsius 有关，据记载他在埃塞俄比亚发现了类似的石料。这个名称后来用于指天然形成的火山玻璃。
etymology_story.en: Obsidian comes from Latin obsidianus, a variant of Obsianus, a name associated with Obsius, whom Pliny the Elder credited with finding a similar stone in Ethiopia. The name subsequently became the term for naturally occurring volcanic glass.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代 obsidian 是整体借词，不应按 ob-、sid-、-ian 强行拆解；词尾 -ian 在这里不是现代英语中自由添加的人物或地域后缀。没有常用的日常派生词；可构成 obsidian-like（像黑曜石的）等形式，也常作名词前置修饰语，如 obsidian blade（黑曜石刀刃）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern obsidian is a whole borrowed word and should not be forced into ob-, sid-, and -ian; its ending is not a freely added modern suffix referring to a person or place. It has no common everyday derivatives, though obsidian-like is a transparent formation, and the noun often modifies another noun, as in obsidian blade.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: volcanic glass（火山玻璃）是上位词，范围比 obsidian 更广；pitchstone（松脂岩）也是火山玻璃，但通常含水更多并呈松脂光泽；flint（燧石）虽也能打制成锋利工具，却是富含二氧化硅的沉积岩，并非黑曜石。后两者是相关材料名称，不能作为严格同义词互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Volcanic glass is the broader category containing obsidian; pitchstone is another volcanic glass, generally with more water and a resinous luster; flint can also be shaped into sharp tools but is a silica-rich sedimentary rock. Pitchstone and flint are related material terms rather than interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Lava cools rapidly into natural glass: picture dark obsidian with sharp broken edges.

usage_note: 正式医学词；常与疾病名或相关形容词连用，说明针对哪种疾病的预防。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经近代拉丁语进入英语，源于希腊语 prophylaxis，意为“预先防护”，与 prophylassein“预先守护”有关。原本“提前防守”的概念后来成为医学中预防疾病及牙科预防性清洁的术语。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through modern Latin from Greek prophylaxis, meaning advance protection, related to prophylassein, to guard beforehand. The idea of guarding in advance developed into a medical term for disease prevention, including preventive dental cleaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常作为完整的医学名词使用；按希腊语来源可分析为 pro-（预先）＋ phylax-/phylact-（守护），不宜把 -is 当作可自由使用的现代英语后缀。主要词族包括 prophylactic（预防性的；预防用品）、prophylactically（预防性地）；相关复合词有 chemoprophylaxis（化学预防）和 immunoprophylaxis（免疫预防）。表示多次或多项预防性处置时可用复数 prophylaxes。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, prophylaxis is generally treated as a complete medical noun; its Greek elements are pro- (beforehand) and phylax-/phylact- (guarding), rather than a productive English suffix -is. Its main word family includes prophylactic (preventive; a preventive agent or device) and prophylactically (preventively); related compounds include chemoprophylaxis and immunoprophylaxis. The plural prophylaxes is used when individual preventive procedures or interventions are counted.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: prevention（预防）适用范围最广；preventive treatment（预防性治疗）明确指医疗干预；dental cleaning（洁牙）只对应牙科义。prophylaxis 是较专业的医学术语，强调疾病发生前或风险出现后的预防措施。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Prevention is the broadest term; preventive treatment explicitly refers to medical intervention; dental cleaning corresponds only to the dental sense. Prophylaxis is a technical medical term emphasizing measures taken to prevent disease, sometimes after exposure to a risk.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pro-＝提前，守护＝设防：疾病到来前先设一道防线。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think pro- meaning beforehand plus guarding: put up a defense before disease develops.

etymology_story.en: Rickshaw is a shortened English form of Japanese jinrikisha, whose elements mean person, power, and vehicle. It originally named a two-wheeled passenger vehicle pulled by a person and later extended to similar pedal-powered and motorized vehicles.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 rickshaw 是整体借词，不能拆成有意义的英语词根和词缀；其来源形式为日语 jin（人）＋ riki（力）＋ sha（车）。复数为 rickshaws；常见相关复合表达有 cycle rickshaw（脚踏三轮客车）、auto-rickshaw（机动三轮客车）和 rickshaw puller（人力车夫），没有常用的独立派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Rickshaw is a borrowed whole word in modern English, with no meaningful English root-and-affix breakdown; its source is Japanese jin (person) + riki (power) + sha (vehicle). The plural is rickshaws; common related compounds include cycle rickshaw, auto-rickshaw, and rickshaw puller. There are no common independent derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: jinrikisha（人力车）是较少见的旧式称呼，通常指人拉的车辆；pedicab（脚踏三轮客车）专指脚踏式；auto-rickshaw（机动三轮客车）专指机动式。rickshaw 的具体动力形式取决于地区和上下文。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Jinrikisha is a less common older term, usually for the hand-pulled vehicle; pedicab specifically means a pedal-powered passenger vehicle; auto-rickshaw specifically means a motorized version. The exact type meant by rickshaw depends on regional usage and context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从日语“人＋力＋车”记住原型：靠人的力量拉动的车。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember its Japanese source: person + power + vehicle, originally a vehicle moved by human effort.

senses.meaning_zh: 以豪侠姿态冒险或打斗；耀武扬威
senses.meaning_en: To behave or fight in a bold, flamboyant, adventurous way.
senses.english_definition: If someone swashbuckles, they behave or fight in a bold, showy way, like a sword-fighting adventurer.

etymology_story.zh: swashbuckle 是从较早的 swashbuckler 逆构而来的动词；swashbuckler 结合了 swash“猛击、发出响声”和 buckler“小圆盾”，原指挥剑敲盾、虚张声势的人。后来这一形象发展为小说和电影中大胆潇洒的剑侠或冒险者。
etymology_story.en: Swashbuckle was back-formed from the older noun swashbuckler, which combines swash, to strike noisily, with buckler, a small shield, originally describing a swaggering swordsman. The image later developed into the bold, flamboyant adventurer familiar from fiction and film.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中可把 swashbuckle 作为动词词干，接 -s、-ed、-ing，形成 swashbuckles、swashbuckled、swashbuckling。主要词族为 swashbuckler（豪侠；剑侠；剑侠冒险作品）和 swashbuckling（豪侠式的；大胆冒险的，也可作名词指此类行为）；历史构词方向是 swashbuckler → swashbuckle，而不是先有动词再加 -er。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, swashbuckle functions as a verb stem taking -s, -ed, and -ing: swashbuckles, swashbuckled, and swashbuckling. Its main family includes swashbuckler (a flamboyant adventurer or an adventure story or film) and swashbuckling (boldly adventurous, or such behavior). Historically, swashbuckler produced swashbuckle by back-formation, rather than the verb producing the noun with -er.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: swagger（大摇大摆、神气活现）侧重姿态；bluster（虚张声势、气势汹汹地说话）侧重言语和威吓；strut（趾高气扬地走）侧重步态。swashbuckle 更有舞剑冒险的戏剧感，不一定带贬义；实际使用中 swashbuckling 和 swashbuckler 比动词原形更常见。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Swagger emphasizes an ostentatiously confident manner; bluster emphasizes noisy, threatening talk; strut emphasizes a self-important way of walking. Swashbuckle adds theatrical sword-fighting adventure and need not be disapproving; swashbuckling and swashbuckler are more usual than the base verb.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经拉丁语 tiara 源于希腊语 tiara，最初指古代波斯等地的头饰，包括王者佩戴的冠帽。英语后来用它指教皇的礼仪冠，以及正式场合佩戴的冠状珠宝头饰。
etymology_story.en: The word came through Latin tiara from Greek tiara, originally referring to headdresses associated with ancient Persia and neighboring peoples, including royal headwear. In English it came to denote the pope's ceremonial crown and a jeweled ornamental headpiece worn on formal occasions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 tiara 是不可进一步拆分的借词；复数为 tiaras。tiara ＋ -ed → tiaraed（戴着冠状头饰的）是少见的形容词；常见相关表达为 bridal tiara（新娘冠饰）和 papal tiara（教皇三重冠），没有常用的动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Tiara is an unanalyzable loanword in modern English; its plural is tiaras. Tiara + -ed produces the uncommon adjective tiaraed, meaning wearing a tiara. Common related expressions include bridal tiara and papal tiara; there are no common verb or adverb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: diadem（王冠、冠状头饰）是较正式或文学性的称呼；crown（王冠）范围更广，常象征君权；coronet（小冠、贵族冠）常与贵族等级有关。tiara 在日常现代用法中通常指正式场合佩戴的珠宝冠饰，不必象征统治权。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Diadem is a formal or literary term for a crown or ornamental headband; crown is broader and often symbolizes sovereignty; coronet is a small crown commonly associated with noble rank. In ordinary modern usage, tiara usually means a jeweled headpiece for formal occasions and need not imply ruling power.

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自法语 trapèze“梯形”，其名称联系着吊杆、两侧绳索及上方支撑构成的几何轮廓。它经拉丁语 trapezium 追溯到希腊语 trapezion，原意为“小桌子”。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from French trapèze, meaning trapezium, with reference to the outline formed by the bar, its ropes, and the support above. Through Latin trapezium, it goes back to Greek trapezion, meaning a small table.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 trapeze 通常作为完整借词记忆；复数为 trapezes。trapeze 去掉末尾不发音的 e 再加 -ist，形成 trapezist（空中秋千演员，较少见）；更常见的表达是 trapeze artist。trapezium（梯形）和 trapezoid（梯形；具体几何含义因英美用法而异）是同源相关词，不是由英语 trapeze 直接派生而来。
morphology_enriched.en: Trapeze is generally treated as a complete loanword in modern English; its plural is trapezes. Dropping its final silent e and adding -ist gives trapezist, a less common term for a trapeze performer; trapeze artist is more usual. Trapezium and trapezoid are related words of the same origin, with geometrical meanings that vary between British and American usage, rather than direct derivatives of English trapeze.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: aerial bar（空中吊杆）是描述性近义表达；swing（秋千）通常带有供人坐的座板；flying trapeze（飞行空中秋千）是用于腾空、接抛等表演的特定形式。trapeze 的核心是供杂技演员抓握或悬挂身体的横杆，没有完全通用的日常单词近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Aerial bar is a descriptive near-equivalent; swing usually suggests a suspended seat; flying trapeze names a particular form used for airborne releases and catches. A trapeze is fundamentally a bar that acrobats grip or hang from, and it has no exact everyday single-word synonym.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语 triptyque 追溯至希腊语 triptykhos，意为“三折的”，其中 tri- 表示“三”，后半部分与“折叠”有关。它原指三折式板面，后来用于三联画，并引申为由三个相关部分构成的作品。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through French triptyque from Greek triptykhos, meaning “threefold,” combining tri-, “three,” with an element associated with folding. From a threefold arrangement of panels, its meaning developed into a three-panel artwork and then a creative work in three related parts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 tri-（三）+ -ptych（联板、折板），但整体属于借入词；复数为 triptychs。相关同源构词有 diptych（二联画）和 polyptych（多联画），它们不是 triptych 的派生词；triptych-like（三联画式的）是可自由构成的复合形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern form can be analyzed as tri- (“three”) + -ptych (“panel or fold”), although the word was borrowed as a whole; its plural is triptychs. Related formations include diptych and polyptych, which are not derivatives of triptych; triptych-like is a freely formed compound adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: three-panel painting（三联画）是直白的描述性近义表达；altarpiece（祭坛画或祭坛装饰）强调宗教用途，不限三块；trilogy（三部曲）强调三部相对独立但相关的作品，而 triptych 更突出三个部分并置形成的整体。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Three-panel painting is a plain descriptive equivalent; altarpiece identifies a religious function and need not have three panels; trilogy usually consists of three relatively independent related works, whereas triptych emphasizes three parts presented as a unified composition.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Tri- means “three”; connect -ptych with folded panels: three linked panels make one work.

etymology_story.zh: 该词的历史与法语 étui（小盒、工具盒）及其复数形式有关：英语中的早期借入形式逐渐缩短，产生了 tweeze、tweezes 等形式。名称由盛放小工具的盒子转指其中的小镊子，后来形成 tweezers。
etymology_story.en: The word's history involves French étui, meaning a small case, and its plural form; shortened English forms included tweeze and tweezes. The name shifted from a case holding small instruments to the pincers inside it, eventually developing into tweezers.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形式可识别为 tweezer + -s，但通常以复数工具名 tweezers 使用；一把说 a pair of tweezers，多把说 pairs of tweezers。相关词族有 tweeze（用镊子夹取或拔除）、tweezes、tweezed、tweezing；动词 tweeze 是从较早的工具名称逆向形成的，不宜把 tweezers 的历史简单写成 tweeze + -ers。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern form contains tweezer + -s, but tweezers normally functions as a plural tool noun: one tool is a pair of tweezers, and several are pairs of tweezers. The related verb family is tweeze, tweezes, tweezed, and tweezing; tweeze arose by back-formation from an earlier instrument name, so tweeze + -ers does not accurately explain the word's history.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: forceps（钳、镊）多用于医疗或技术语境，范围更广；pincers（钳子）通常更大、夹持力更强；tongs（夹钳、夹子）常用于夹取食物或热物。tweezers 特指适合精细夹取的小型工具。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Forceps is a broader medical or technical term; pincers usually suggests a larger tool with a stronger grip; tongs commonly handle food or hot objects. Tweezers specifically suggests a small tool for precise gripping.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 两条细臂，轻轻一捏，夹住细小物；把 a pair of tweezers 整体记成“一把镊子”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Two slender arms pinch something tiny; remember a pair of tweezers as one complete tool.

meaning: 颤音；音高轻微而快速波动的效果

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；ˈ 后的音节承重音，ˌ 表示次重音。

forms: 通常不可数，指不同颤音效果时可用复数 vibratos。
family: vibrate 振动；vibration 振动

morphology.text: vibrato 作为独立词素记忆；vibrato + -phone → vibraphone（颤音琴，缩合时词尾发生变化）。

etymology.text: 从意大利语 vibrato 借入英语，意大利语形式承接拉丁语 vibrare“振动”的分词；把它想成一个音轻轻颤动。

usage_note: 音乐用语，重点是音高的轻微周期变化；tremolo 通常指音量的波动或快速重复奏音。

senses.pos: n. 通常作不可数名词
senses.meaning_zh: 颤音；演唱或演奏时音高轻微、快速而有规律的波动
senses.meaning_en: A slight, rapid, regular variation in musical pitch.
senses.english_definition: Vibrato is a musical effect in which a singer or player makes the pitch of a sustained note rise and fall slightly and rapidly.
senses.collocation_en: sing with vibrato; a wide vibrato
senses.collocation_zh: 用颤音演唱；音高波动幅度较大的颤音
senses.sentence_en: She used a gentle vibrato on the final note.
senses.sentence_zh: 她在最后一个音上运用了轻柔的颤音。

etymology_story.zh: 英语直接借用意大利语 vibrato，其本义为“振动的”，是 vibrare（振动）的过去分词，最终源于拉丁语 vibrare。这个表示振动的词在音乐中专指持续音的轻微、规律性音高波动。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Italian vibrato, meaning “vibrated,” the past participle of vibrare, ultimately from Latin vibrare, “to vibrate.” In music, this idea of vibration became the slight, regular fluctuation in the pitch of a sustained note.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 vibrato 是整体借入的音乐名词，不宜把 -ato 当作可自由使用的英语后缀。需要计数时复数可用 vibratos；同源词族包括 vibrate（振动）、vibration（振动）、vibrating（振动的）、vibratory（振动的）、vibrational（振动的）和 vibrator（振动器）；vibraphone（颤音琴）是相关构词，不能分析成 vibrato 直接加 -phone。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, vibrato is a musical noun borrowed as a whole; -ato is not a freely productive English suffix. When a countable use is needed, the plural is vibratos; the related root family includes vibrate, vibration, vibrating, vibratory, vibrational, and vibrator. Vibraphone is a related formation, not a direct combination of vibrato and -phone.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: quaver（声音的颤抖）可表示因紧张或虚弱产生的不稳定声音，不一定是有意的技巧；tremolo（震音）通常涉及音量的快速变化或音的快速重复；trill（颤音）是在两个不同音高之间快速交替。vibrato 则是围绕一个音高的小幅连续波动。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Quaver can describe an unsteady voice caused by nervousness or weakness rather than deliberate technique; tremolo usually involves rapid changes in loudness or rapid repetition; trill alternates rapidly between two distinct pitches. Vibrato is a small, continuous fluctuation around one pitch.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联系 vibrate“振动”：让一个长音的音高轻轻上下颤动。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with vibrate: the pitch of one held note gently wavers up and down.

meaning: 天使向马利亚报喜（基督教事件）

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；ˈ 后的音节承重音，ˌ 表示次重音。

forms: 宗教事件或节日名称通常用单数 the Annunciation；一般“宣布”义可有复数 annunciations。
family: annunciate 宣告；announcement 宣布

morphology.text: annunciate + -ion → annunciation（报喜；词尾去 e），可借“宣告消息”的结构记住宗教义。

etymology.text: 中古英语经盎格鲁法语、古法语借入拉丁语 annuntiatio“宣告”；在基督教传统中专指天使带来的报喜消息。

usage_note: 指宗教事件或节日时通常大写 Annunciation；这里教宗教义，普通的宣布更常用 announcement。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语和法语传入，源自拉丁语 annuntiatio（宣告），与 annuntiare（传达消息、宣告）有关。原本一般性的“宣告”在基督教语境中专门指向马利亚报喜，继而也指纪念这一事件的节日及描绘它的艺术作品。
etymology_story.en: The word entered through Middle English and French from Latin annuntiatio, “announcement,” related to annuntiare, “to bring news or announce.” In Christian usage, the general idea of an announcement became specifically Gabriel's message to Mary, then also the commemorative feast and artistic depictions of the event.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族关系可写为 annunciate（宣告）去词尾 e + -ion → annunciation（宣告）；大写 Annunciation 表示特定的宗教事件、节日或相关艺术题材。词族包括 annunciate、annunciates、annunciated、annunciating、annunciation、annunciator（信号显示器、通告装置）和 annunciatory（宣告的）；announce、announcement 是同源相关词。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern word-family relationship is annunciate, with final e removed, + -ion → annunciation; capitalized Annunciation names the specific religious event, feast, or artistic subject. The family includes annunciate, annunciates, annunciated, annunciating, annunciation, annunciator, and annunciatory; announce and announcement are related cognate words.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: announcement（宣布、通告）是一般用语；proclamation（正式宣告）强调公开和权威性；Annunciation 专指这一基督教报喜事件及其相关节日或艺术表现，前两个词不能直接替代这一专名。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Announcement is the general word for making news known; proclamation suggests a formal, public, authoritative declaration. Annunciation specifically names this Christian event and its associated feast or artistic representation, so the general terms are not interchangeable with the proper name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联系 announce“宣告”：大写的 Annunciation，是向马利亚宣告耶稣将诞生的消息。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with announce: the capitalized Annunciation announces to Mary that Jesus will be born.

etymology_story.zh: 该词在中古英语中出现，源自古法语 baubel，意为“玩具、小玩意”；更早的来源并不确定。词义由玩物发展为价值不高的装饰品，后来也用于圣诞装饰球，并比喻华而不实的荣誉或地位标志。
etymology_story.en: The word appeared in Middle English from Old French baubel, meaning a toy or trinket; its earlier origin is uncertain. Its meaning developed from a plaything to an inexpensive ornament, later including Christmas-tree balls and, figuratively, showy honors or symbols of status.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 bauble 是不可再作实用拆分的单纯词，不能按 baub + -le 理解；复数为 baubles。它没有常用的标准派生词族；bauble-like（像小饰物的）是可自由构成的复合形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, bauble is a simple lexical base with no useful productive division into baub + -le; its plural is baubles. It has no common established family of derivatives; bauble-like is a freely formed compound adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: trinket（廉价小饰物）与 bauble 最接近，常指小首饰；ornament（装饰物）是中性词，不暗示廉价；knick-knack（小摆设）通常指家中陈列的小装饰品。bauble 更突出闪亮、花哨或价值有限。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Trinket is the closest synonym and often refers to inexpensive jewelry; ornament is neutral and does not imply low value; knick-knack usually means a small decorative object displayed in a home. Bauble more strongly suggests glitter, showiness, or limited value.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“玩具”到“饰物”：外表闪亮，小巧好看，实际价值不高。
mnemonic_anchor.en: From toy to ornament: small and shiny, pleasing to look at, but worth little.

senses.sentence_zh: 她的研究带领读者走进医学史中那些鲜为人知却引人入胜的领域。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在中古英语中由表示“旁侧、次要”的 by 与表示“道路”的 way 组合而成，最初指偏离主路的小路。后来，“偏离主干道路”的空间意象被用于知识领域，表示冷僻的分支或细节。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in Middle English from by, meaning 'at the side' or 'secondary,' and way, meaning 'road.' The image of a route away from the main road later developed into a figurative meaning: an obscure branch or detail of a subject.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：by（旁侧、次要）+ way（道路）→ byway；复数为 byways。该词没有常用的直接派生词；highway（公路）、pathway（小径）和 roadway（车行道）属于共享 way 的相关复合词，并非 byway 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: by ('secondary' or 'at the side') + way ('road') → byway; plural: byways. There are no common direct derivatives; highway, pathway, and roadway are related compounds sharing way, rather than derivatives of byway.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lane（狭窄道路）强调路窄，未必偏僻；back road（僻静支路）强调避开主要交通路线；side road（支路）强调从主路分出。byway 通常兼有僻静、少人通行的意味，语体略带文学色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lane emphasizes narrowness without necessarily implying remoteness; back road suggests a route away from major traffic; side road emphasizes branching off a main road. Byway usually suggests a quiet, little-traveled route and has a slightly literary tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: by“在旁边”+ way“道路”：主路旁的小路，也是知识主干旁的冷僻分支。
mnemonic_anchor.en: By means 'at the side': a byway runs beside the main route, literally on the map or figuratively through a subject.

usage_note: 偏文学、旧式用语，常形容人的外貌；日常更常说 attractive 或 good-looking，并非 come 的副词。

etymology_story.zh: comely 源自古英语 cȳmlic，意为“美丽的、秀美的”，经中古英语演变为现代形式。它保留了形容容貌好看的含义，但在现代英语中逐渐带有文学或古雅色彩。
etymology_story.en: Comely descends from Old English cȳmlic, meaning 'beautiful' or 'lovely,' through Middle English forms. It has retained its meaning of physical attractiveness while becoming literary or old-fashioned in modern English.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 comely 作为整体词干识记，不应拆作 come + -ly；词尾 -ly 在这里不表示它是副词。词族：comelier（更秀美的）、comeliest（最秀美的）、comeliness（秀美，comely + -ness，y 变 i）、uncomely（不雅观的）、uncomeliness（不雅观）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, treat comely as a whole stem rather than come + -ly; its ending does not make it an adverb. Family: comelier, comeliest, comeliness (comely + -ness, with y changing to i), uncomely, and uncomeliness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pretty（漂亮的）常强调精巧、悦目的美；beautiful（美丽的）赞美程度通常更强，适用范围更广；attractive（有吸引力的）表达更中性，也可涉及气质。comely 主要形容外貌，语气古雅而含蓄。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pretty often suggests delicate, pleasing looks; beautiful usually expresses stronger admiration and has wider application; attractive is more neutral and may include personal appeal. Comely focuses on physical appearance in a restrained, old-fashioned register.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 comely 连到 comeliness“秀美”：古典肖像里那种端正、清秀的好看。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect comely with comeliness: the graceful good looks of someone in an old portrait.

senses.meaning_en: Capable of being transmitted between people or other hosts.

senses.meaning_en: Capable of being expressed or conveyed to someone else.
senses.english_definition: An idea, feeling, or experience is communicable if you can convey it to another person.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语及拉丁语传统传入英语，源头是晚期拉丁语 communicabilis“可分享、可传达的”，与 communicare“分享、使共同拥有”同源。它既用于能够传达的思想或体验，也用于能够在宿主之间传播的疾病。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French and Latin transmission, ultimately from Late Latin communicabilis, 'capable of being shared or communicated,' related to communicare, 'to share or make common.' It came to describe both conveyable ideas or experiences and diseases that can pass between hosts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族分析：communic-（与分享、传达有关的词干）+ -able（能够被……的）→ communicable；它与 communicate 对应，但不是简单保留 communicate 全词再加 -able。主要词族：communicate（交流）、communication（交流；传播）、communicative（健谈的；交流性的）、communicator（交流者）、communicability（可传达性；可传播性）、noncommunicable（非传染性的）、incommunicable（无法传达的）、incommunicability（不可传达性）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern family analysis: communic- (the stem associated with sharing or conveying) + -able ('capable of being') → communicable. It corresponds to communicate but is not formed by simply retaining the whole verb and adding -able. Principal family members: communicate, communication, communicative, communicator, communicability, noncommunicable, incommunicable, and incommunicability.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: transmissible（可传播的）强调能够从一处或一个宿主传到另一个；contagious（有传染性的）通常强调经接触或近距离接触传染；conveyable（可传达的）对应思想、信息等的非疾病义。communicable 的疾病义涵盖直接及间接传播，不限于接触传染。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Transmissible emphasizes the ability to pass between places or hosts; contagious typically emphasizes spread through contact or close proximity; conveyable matches the nonmedical sense involving ideas or information. Communicable covers direct and indirect disease transmission, rather than contact transmission alone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: communic- 的核心是“传递、分享”：思想能传达，疾病也能传播。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The communic- family centers on passing something on: ideas can be communicated, and infections can be transmitted.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；ˈ 后的音节承重音，ˌ 表示次重音。

family: cybernetics 控制论；cybernetically 从控制论角度

etymology.text: 来自控制论术语 cybernetics 这一词族，词根承接希腊语 kybernētēs“舵手”；像舵手根据船的偏向不断调节方向。

usage_note: 强调反馈、通信和调节；不等于泛指互联网的 cyber，也不必然指机器人。

etymology_story.zh: cybernetic 属于 cybernetics“控制论”词族；其希腊语源头与 kybernētēs“舵手”及 kybernan“掌舵、治理”有关。维纳在1948年确立了 cybernetics 的现代学科用法，以掌舵比喻依靠通信和反馈实现控制，后来该形容词也扩展到人机结合的科幻技术。
etymology_story.en: Cybernetic belongs to the cybernetics family, ultimately connected with Greek kybernētēs, 'steersman,' and kybernan, 'to steer or govern.' Norbert Wiener established the modern disciplinary use of cybernetics in 1948, connecting steering with control through communication and feedback; the adjective later extended to fictional technologies combining bodies and machines.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族结构：cybernet-（控制论词干）+ -ic（形容词后缀）→ cybernetic；cybernetics 表示“控制论”。主要词族：cybernetically（以控制论方式）、cyberneticist／cybernetician（控制论专家）。cyber- 是同源并进一步发展的构词成分，常用于计算机或网络相关词汇，但这些词并非都由 cybernetic 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern family structure: cybernet- (the cybernetics stem) + -ic (adjective suffix) → cybernetic; cybernetics names the discipline. Principal family members include cybernetically and cyberneticist/cybernetician. The related combining form cyber- developed broader computer and network associations, but words containing it are not all direct derivatives of cybernetic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: feedback-controlled（由反馈控制的）突出具体调节机制；bionic（仿生的；以机电装置增强身体的）常用于人工器官或能力增强；robotic（机器人的）强调机器人及其动作或装置。cybernetic 的核心是信息反馈与控制，其科幻义还可涉及身体与机器的结合。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Feedback-controlled highlights the regulating mechanism; bionic often describes artificial body parts or enhanced physical abilities; robotic concerns robots and their mechanisms or movements. Cybernetic centers on information, feedback, and control, with an extended science-fiction use for integration between bodies and machines.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“舵手”：发现偏航→接收反馈→调整方向，就是 cybernetic 的控制逻辑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a steersman: detect a deviation, receive feedback, and correct the course—the central cybernetic loop.

senses.meaning_zh: 二层拼合宝石；由两层材料黏合制成的宝石
senses.meaning_en: A composite gemstone made by joining two layers of material.
senses.english_definition: In jewelry, a doublet is a stone made by joining two layers, often with a thin gemstone layer attached to a supporting base.
senses.collocation_en: an opal doublet; a doublet stone
senses.collocation_zh: 二层拼合欧泊；二层拼合宝石

etymology_story.zh: doublet 在中古英语时期借自古法语 doublet，由 double“双重的”加小称后缀构成，早期服装义与双层或加衬的衣物有关。后来，“双重、成对”的概念也体现在词源学、光学、光谱学和宝石学等领域的专门用法中。
etymology_story.en: Doublet entered Middle English from Old French doublet, formed from double with a diminutive suffix; its early clothing sense was associated with doubled or padded garments. The idea of doubleness or pairing also appears in its specialized uses in etymology, optics, spectroscopy, and gemology.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可识别结构为 double（双重、成对）与历史后缀 -et 的组合，但 doublet 整体借自法语，不宜把“去 e 加 -et”当作普遍适用的现代构词规则。直接词形：doublet、doublets；相关词族包括 double（双倍的；加倍）、doubly（双倍地）、doubling（加倍）和 triplet（三个一组；三联体），其中 triplet 是平行构词，并非 doublet 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The recognizable structure links double ('twofold' or 'paired') with historical -et, but doublet was borrowed as a whole from French; 'drop e and add -et' should not be treated as a general modern formation rule. Direct forms: doublet and doublets. Related vocabulary includes double, doubly, doubling, and the parallel formation triplet, which is not a derivative of doublet.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: jacket（短上衣）是服装义的上位词，不限定历史时期或贴身款式；pair（一对）泛指两个相关事物，不带 doublet 常见的专业含义；composite stone（拼合宝石）涵盖多种层数，doublet 则明确为两层。各义所属领域不同，不能用同一个近义词全部替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Jacket is a broader term for the garment sense and does not specify period or fit; pair describes two associated things without doublet's usual technical specificity; composite stone includes constructions with different numbers of layers, whereas a doublet has two. These substitutes apply to different senses and are not interchangeable across them.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 double“双”：衣服联想双层，谱线联想双线，透镜和宝石联想两个元件或两层，同源词联想“一源两形”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor everything to double: doubled cloth, paired spectral lines, two lens elements, two gemstone layers, or two word forms from one source.

meaning: 被认为带有女性气质的（形容男性，常含贬意）

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；ˈ 后的音节承重音，ˌ 表示次重音。

forms: 形容词，通常不变形；比较可用 more / most effeminate。
family: effeminately 被认为女性化地；effeminateness 被认为女性化的特质

morphology.text: effeminate 作为独立词素记忆；effeminate + -ly → effeminately（以被认为女性化的方式）。

etymology.text: 源自拉丁语 effeminatus，为 effeminare 的分词形式，其词根 femina 意为“女人”；英语沿用了将男性气质女性化的旧式评价。

usage_note: 带有性别刻板印象，形容男性时常有贬意；阅读时识别说话者态度，不宜用来随意评价他人。feminine 适用范围更广。

senses.meaning_zh: 被认为具有女性气质的（用于男性，常含贬意或刻板印象）
senses.meaning_en: Describing a man whose appearance or behavior is considered traditionally feminine, often disapprovingly.
senses.english_definition: If someone describes a man as effeminate, they mean that he looks or behaves in ways traditionally associated with women, usually expressing disapproval.
senses.collocation_en: an effeminate voice; effeminate mannerisms
senses.collocation_zh: 被认为女性化的嗓音；被认为女性化的举止
senses.sentence_en: He disliked being called effeminate simply because he spoke softly.
senses.sentence_zh: 他不喜欢别人仅仅因为他说话轻柔，就说他女性化。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 effeminatus，即 effeminare“使女性化”的过去分词，其中 femina 意为“女人”。英语沿用了这一词语对男性外表和行为的传统评价，因此它常带有贬意和性别刻板印象。
etymology_story.en: It comes from Latin effeminatus, the past participle of effeminare, meaning “to make feminine,” ultimately based on femina, “woman.” English retained its traditional judgment about male appearance and behavior, giving it frequent disapproving and stereotypical associations.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 effeminate 作为整体借入的形容词记忆，不宜机械拆解为几个独立英语词。词族包括 effeminately（以被认为女性化的方式）、effeminacy（男性被认为具有女性气质的特征）和较少见的 effeminateness（女性化特征）；effemination（使女性化）也有使用，但较罕见。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, effeminate is best treated as a borrowed adjective rather than mechanically divided into independent English elements. Its family includes effeminately, the noun effeminacy, the less common noun effeminateness, and the rare noun effemination, meaning the process of making feminine.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: feminine（女性气质的）通常较中性，也可用于男性；womanly（具有成熟女性特质的）常带肯定意味；unmanly（被认为缺乏男子气概的）是更宽泛的贬义评价。effeminate 专门把男性的某些特征评价为女性化，通常含贬意。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Feminine is generally more neutral and can describe men as well as women; womanly often positively suggests qualities associated with mature women; unmanly is a broader disapproving judgment about failing masculine expectations. Effeminate specifically characterizes a man's traits as feminine, usually negatively.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住与 feminine 共有的 fem-：核心联想是“女性特征”，而 effeminate 常指男性被如此评价。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect fem- with feminine: the central idea is feminine traits, with effeminate usually applying that judgment to a man.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；ˈ 后的音节承重音，ˌ 表示次重音。

forms: 本卡名词复数 fibs；同形动词过去式及过去分词 fibbed，现在分词 fibbing，第三人称单数 fibs。
family: fibber 撒小谎的人

morphology.text: fib + -er → fibber（撒小谎的人，双写 b）；fib 本身作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 17世纪初英语已有名词 fib“小谎话”，后来又用作“撒小谎”的动词；记住这是比 lie 口气轻一些的日常说法。

usage_note: 可数，常说 tell a fib；通常将谎言说得较轻，不表示这件事一定无害。动词可说 fib about something。

senses.meaning_zh: 小谎话；无关紧要的谎言
senses.meaning_en: A small, relatively unimportant lie.
senses.english_definition: A fib is a lie about something relatively unimportant, especially one regarded as causing little harm.

etymology_story.zh: fib 在早期现代英语中已用作“小谎话”，后来也用作动词“撒小谎”。其更早来源不确定，可能与旧词 fibble-fabble“胡说、闲扯”有关，但这一联系不能视为定论。
etymology_story.en: Fib was used in early modern English for a small lie and later also became a verb. Its earlier origin is uncertain; a connection with the older expression fibble-fabble, meaning nonsense or idle talk, has been suggested but is not established.

morphology_enriched.zh: fib 是可独立使用的词基，名词与动词形式相同。fib + -s → fibs（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）；加元音开头的后缀时双写 b：fibbed（过去式、过去分词）、fibbing（现在分词、动名词）、fibber（撒小谎的人），其复数为 fibbers。
morphology_enriched.en: Fib is a free base used as both a noun and a verb. Adding -s gives fibs, either the plural noun or the third-person singular verb; the final b doubles before vowel-initial suffixes in fibbed, fibbing, and fibber, whose plural is fibbers.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lie（谎言；撒谎）是最宽泛的说法，可指严重欺骗；white lie（善意的谎言）强调避免伤害他人的动机；untruth（不实之言）较正式，也不一定明确强调故意欺骗。fib 语气较轻、较口语化，但不一定出于善意。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lie is the broadest term and can involve serious deception; a white lie is specifically intended to spare someone's feelings; untruth is more formal and does not always explicitly imply deliberate deception. Fib is informal and minimizes the seriousness of a lie without necessarily implying a kind motive.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 fib 记成“小谎”：a fib 是一个小谎，to fib 就是撒小谎。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor fib to “a little lie”: a fib names it, and to fib means to tell it.

meaning: 任性固执的；不肯听劝的

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；ˈ 后的音节承重音，ˌ 表示次重音。

morphology.text: head（头脑、主意）+ strong（强硬的）→ headstrong（主意强硬、不肯听劝的）。

etymology.text: 中古英语由 head 和 strong 组合，早已用来形容一意孤行的人；可联想脑子里的主意太硬，别人的劝告进不去。

usage_note: 通常含批评，强调坚持己见、不听劝；determined 可以褒义地表示有决心。

senses.meaning_zh: 任性固执的；一意孤行的；不肯听劝的
senses.meaning_en: Determined to do what one wants despite advice or objections.
senses.english_definition: If someone is headstrong, they insist on doing what they want and are unwilling to listen to other people's advice.

etymology_story.zh: headstrong 是中古英语时期形成的复合词，由 head“头”与 strong“强的”组成。其历史意象与难以驾驭、执意向前有关，后来稳定用于形容不肯受劝告约束的人。
etymology_story.en: Headstrong is a Middle English compound of head and strong. Its historical imagery involves being difficult to control and determined to press ahead, developing into the familiar description of someone who resists advice.

morphology_enriched.zh: head（头；此处可联想自己的意志）+ strong（强的）→ headstrong。相关派生词为 headstrongly（任性固执地）和 headstrongness（任性固执），二者均不如形容词常见；比较级和最高级通常用 more headstrong、most headstrong。
morphology_enriched.en: Head + strong forms the compound adjective headstrong, with head suggesting one's own will as a memory aid. Related derivatives are headstrongly and headstrongness, both less common than the adjective; comparison normally uses more headstrong and most headstrong.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: stubborn（固执的）泛指不肯改变想法或做法；obstinate（顽固的）更强调面对劝说仍不改变；wilful（任性的，美式拼写 willful）强调明知他人反对仍按自己的意愿行事。headstrong 尤其突出急于照自己的主意行动、不肯听劝。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Stubborn broadly describes resistance to changing one's mind or behavior; obstinate emphasizes continued resistance to persuasion; wilful, spelled willful in American English, emphasizes deliberately following one's wishes despite opposition. Headstrong particularly suggests pushing ahead with one's own plans and rejecting advice.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: head + strong：自己的主意太“强”，别人的劝告进不去。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Head + strong: your own ideas push so strongly that other people's advice cannot get in.

senses.meaning_zh: 易怒的；脾气暴躁的
senses.meaning_en: Easily angered; quick-tempered.
senses.english_definition: Someone who is irascible becomes angry very easily.

etymology_story.zh: irascible 经法语或直接从晚期拉丁语 irascibilis 借入，后者源于拉丁语 irasci“发怒”，进一步关联 ira“愤怒”。词义一直围绕“容易发怒”，英语中通常用于较正式的人物性格描写。
etymology_story.en: Irascible entered English through French or directly from Late Latin irascibilis, based on Latin irasci, “to become angry,” ultimately related to ira, “anger.” It has retained the meaning “easily angered” and is typically used in relatively formal descriptions of character.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是借入词，可按拉丁来源的词干 irasc-（发怒）+ -ible（具有某种可能性或倾向的）理解，但 irasc- 不能在现代英语中独立使用。词族包括 irascibly（易怒地）、irascibility（易怒；暴躁）和较少见的 irascibleness（易怒）；irascible 变为 irascibility 时，词尾 -ible 对应 -ibility。
morphology_enriched.en: This borrowed word can be analyzed as the Latin-derived stem irasc-, “become angry,” plus -ible, indicating capacity or tendency, although irasc- is not an independent modern English word. Its family includes irascibly, irascibility, and the less common irascibleness; the ending -ible corresponds to -ibility in irascibility.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: irritable（易烦躁的）可指疲劳等造成的暂时状态，未必发展为明显愤怒；hot-tempered（脾气急躁的）强调容易突然发火；choleric（易怒的）较书面，常描述习惯性的暴躁。irascible 通常强调一个人容易被激怒的性格倾向。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Irritable can describe temporary annoyance caused by factors such as tiredness, without overt anger; hot-tempered emphasizes a tendency to flare up suddenly; choleric is literary and often describes habitual bad temper. Irascible usually emphasizes a person's disposition to become angry easily.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: irasc- 表示“发怒”，-ible 提示“容易如此”：一点就怒。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Irasc- points to anger, and -ible suggests readiness: ready to get angry at the slightest spark.

morphology.text: litmus 作为独立词素记忆；litmus + -like → litmus-like（像石蕊的），-like 表示“像……的”。

etymology.text: 中古英语已有 lit-mose 这类形式，名称中的后半部分与日耳曼语表示“苔、地衣”的词相关；石蕊染料正是取自某些地衣。

usage_note: 石蕊遇酸呈红、遇碱呈蓝；litmus test 也可比喻检验某种品质的关键标准。

senses.meaning_zh: 石蕊；从某些地衣中提取的酸碱指示染料
senses.meaning_en: A dye obtained from certain lichens and used to indicate acidity or alkalinity.
senses.english_definition: Litmus is a dye that turns red in acidic conditions and blue in alkaline conditions and is used to test substances.
senses.collocation_en: litmus paper; litmus solution
senses.collocation_zh: 石蕊试纸；石蕊溶液

senses.meaning_zh: 检验标准；试金石（主要用于 litmus test）
senses.meaning_en: A revealing test or criterion, chiefly in the expression litmus test.
senses.english_definition: A litmus test is a situation or question that clearly reveals someone's attitude or shows whether something meets an important standard.
senses.collocation_en: a litmus test of commitment; a political litmus test
senses.collocation_zh: 检验承诺是否坚定的试金石；检验政治立场的标准

etymology_story.zh: litmus 一般被追溯到中古荷兰语 litmoes，并与斯堪的纳维亚语言中表示“颜色、染料”和“苔”的成分相联系，反映了这种染料取自地衣的历史。由于石蕊通过变色显示酸碱性，litmus test 后来引申为能揭示真实情况或立场的检验。
etymology_story.en: Litmus is generally traced to Middle Dutch litmoes and linked with Scandinavian elements meaning “color or dye” and “moss,” reflecting the dye's origin in lichens. Because its color change reveals acidity or alkalinity, litmus test later developed the figurative meaning of a revealing test of a situation or position.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 litmus 是不可再作常规英语构词拆分的借入词，通常作不可数名词。它没有常用的后缀派生词；主要构词形式是复合结构，如 litmus paper（石蕊试纸）、litmus solution（石蕊溶液）和 litmus test（石蕊检验；试金石），其中 litmus 作名词定语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, litmus is a borrowed word with no productive internal English breakdown and is normally an uncountable noun. It has no common suffix-derived family; its main formations are compounds such as litmus paper, litmus solution, and litmus test, in which litmus functions as a noun modifier.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: indicator（指示剂）是上位词，范围比石蕊广；比喻义中的 touchstone（试金石）强调衡量品质或价值的标准，acid test（严峻而关键的检验）强调决定性的实际考验。litmus test 尤其强调通过某个问题、事件或反应迅速辨明性质或立场。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Indicator is a broader category rather than an exact synonym for the dye. For the figurative expression, touchstone emphasizes a standard for judging quality or value, while acid test emphasizes a decisive practical challenge; litmus test particularly suggests a question, event, or response that readily reveals a quality or position.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 石蕊遇酸变红、遇碱变蓝：颜色揭示性质，因此 litmus test 就是“让真实情况显出来的检验”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Litmus turns red in acid and blue in alkali: its color reveals a property, so a litmus test reveals what something or someone is really like.

etymology.text: 英语先在17世纪用名词 miff 表示一阵不快，后来发展出“使人不悦”的动词；可记住它常是小小的冒犯。

senses.meaning_zh: 使略感恼火；使有些不悦，常用被动形式

etymology_story.zh: miff 在17世纪初已用作名词，表示一阵不悦，后来也用作动词，表示使人略感恼怒。其确切来源不明，可能是模仿不满情绪的表现性造词。
etymology_story.en: Miff was used as a noun for a fit of displeasure by the early seventeenth century and later became a verb meaning to annoy slightly. Its exact origin is uncertain, though it may be an expressive formation suggesting displeasure.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 miff 是不可再拆分的词基。屈折形式：miffs、miffed、miffing；miffed 也常作形容词，表示“略感恼火的”。它没有常用的进一步派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, miff is an indivisible base. Its inflected forms are miffs, miffed, and miffing; miffed is also commonly used as an adjective meaning slightly annoyed. There is no widely used larger family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: annoy（使恼火）适用范围最广；irritate（使烦躁）常强调持续或反复的刺激；offend（冒犯）更强调伤害感情或自尊。miff 较口语化，通常只表示轻微的不悦。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Annoy is the broadest term; irritate often suggests persistent or repeated aggravation; offend emphasizes hurt feelings or wounded pride. Miff is informal and usually describes only mild displeasure.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 miff 联想成受了小冒犯后轻轻“哼”一声：有点不高兴，还没大发雷霆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Associate miff with a small huff after a slight: mildly offended, without becoming furious.

etymology_story.zh: minaret 经法语 minaret 和土耳其语 minare，最终源自阿拉伯语 manāra，意为“灯塔、灯台或宣礼塔”。这个词的历史意象从高处的光源延伸到清真寺旁用于宣礼的高塔。
etymology_story.en: Minaret came through French minaret and Turkish minare from Arabic manāra, meaning a lighthouse, beacon, or minaret. Its historical imagery connects an elevated source of light with the tower used for the call to prayer.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 minaret 是整体借入的名词，不宜按英语词缀硬拆。词族：minarets（复数）；minaret + -ed → minareted（带宣礼塔的），其中 -ed 表示“具有……的”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, minaret is a borrowed noun rather than a transparent combination of English roots and affixes. Its family includes the plural minarets and minaret + -ed → minareted, meaning furnished with a minaret or minarets.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tower（塔）是上位词，不说明宗教用途；turret（小塔）通常指建筑上的小型塔楼；steeple（教堂尖塔）通常属于基督教教堂。它们都不能完全替代专指清真寺宣礼塔的 minaret。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tower is a general term without a religious function; turret usually means a small tower forming part of a building; steeple usually belongs to a Christian church. None is an exact substitute for minaret.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“灯塔式高处标志”的历史意象：清真寺旁高高的宣礼塔。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep the historical beacon image in mind: a high, visible tower beside a mosque.

etymology_story.zh: scabbard 由中古英语经盎格鲁法语传入，通常被认为可追溯至表示“刀刃”和“保护”的日耳曼语成分，不过具体来源仍有不确定之处。其核心含义一直是包住并保护刀刃的套。
etymology_story.en: Scabbard entered Middle English through Anglo-French and is generally traced to Germanic elements associated with a blade and protection, although the precise derivation is uncertain. Its central meaning has remained a covering that encloses and protects a blade.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 scabbard 是不可按常用英语词素再拆分的词基，不应拆成 scab + bard。词族包括 scabbards（复数）、scabbarded（装有剑鞘的或已入鞘的）和较少用的 scabbardless（无鞘的）；另有少见的动词用法 scabbard，意为“把刀剑收入鞘中”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, scabbard is an indivisible base, not scab + bard. Its family includes the plural scabbards, scabbarded meaning equipped with a scabbard or placed in one, and the uncommon scabbardless meaning without a scabbard; a rare verb scabbard means to put a blade into its scabbard.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sheath（鞘、套）范围更广，可指刀鞘及其他保护套；case（盒、套）只是泛称；holster（枪套）通常用于手枪。scabbard 尤其让人想到剑或长刀的鞘。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sheath is broader and can cover knives or other objects; case is a general word for a protective container; holster usually holds a handgun. Scabbard particularly suggests the covering for a sword or other long blade.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of a blade's protective coat: the sword wears a scabbard.

etymology_story.zh: stillborn 出现于16世纪末，由 still“静止的、无声的”和 born“出生的”组合而成，其中 still 委婉地表达没有生命。后来它被用于比喻尚未发展或实施便已失败的计划等事物。
etymology_story.en: Stillborn appeared in the late sixteenth century as a compound of still, meaning motionless or silent, and born, with still euphemistically suggesting lifelessness. It later acquired a figurative sense for plans and other undertakings that fail before they can develop.

morphology_enriched.zh: still（静止、无声）+ born（bear 表示“生育”时的过去分词形式）→ stillborn。相关词族：stillbirth（死产；死产婴儿）及其复数 stillbirths；stillborn 本身没有常用的比较级或最高级形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Still, meaning motionless or silent, + born, the birth-related past participle of bear, → stillborn. Related forms are stillbirth, meaning a birth without signs of life or a baby born dead, and its plural stillbirths; stillborn has no usual comparative or superlative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: born dead（出生时已死亡）最接近字面义；abortive（未成功的）强调尝试未能达到目的；nonviable（无法存活或不可行的）强调缺乏继续生存或成功的条件。比喻义 stillborn 特别强调还没真正开始便已失败。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Born dead closely matches the literal meaning; abortive describes an attempt that fails to achieve its purpose; nonviable emphasizes an inability to survive or succeed. Figurative stillborn particularly suggests failure before an undertaking properly begins.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: still“静止无声”+ born“出生”：出生便无生命；引申为计划一开始便无发展机会。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Still + born: lifeless at birth, then figuratively without a chance to develop from the outset.

etymology_story.zh: tambourine 经法语 tambourin 传入，后者是 tambour“鼓”的小称形式，原有“小鼓”的意思。英语中这个名称后来主要用于框边装有金属响片、可以摇动或敲击的铃鼓。
etymology_story.en: Tambourine came through French tambourin, a diminutive of tambour, meaning drum. In English, the name came to refer chiefly to the frame instrument fitted with metal jingles and played by shaking or striking it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 tambourine 通常作为整体借词学习；历史上可联系法语 tambour“鼓”和小称形式 tambourin，不应把 -ine 当作这里可自由使用的英语后缀。词族：tambourines（复数）；tambourine 去词尾 e + -ist → tambourinist（铃鼓演奏者，较少用），日常更常说 tambourine player（铃鼓演奏者）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tambourine is best treated as a whole borrowed word; historically it is related to French tambour, meaning drum, and its diminutive tambourin, rather than a productive English suffix -ine. Its family includes tambourines and tambourinist, formed by dropping final e before -ist; the everyday expression is tambourine player.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: frame drum（框鼓）是较宽泛的乐器类别，不一定装有响片；hand drum（手鼓）泛指用手敲击的鼓；timbrel（铃鼓）是较古旧、常见于宗教或历史语境的近义名称。tambourine 的典型特征是框边的金属响片。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Frame drum names a broader instrument category and does not necessarily imply jingles; hand drum broadly describes a drum played with the hands; timbrel is an older near-equivalent often found in religious or historical contexts. Metal jingles around the frame are characteristic of a tambourine.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“小鼓”的历史含义联想：一手拿着，摇一下便叮当响。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with the historical idea of a little drum: hold it in one hand and shake it to make the jingles ring.

etymology_story.zh: transceiver 是20世纪将 transmitter（发射器）和 receiver（接收器）缩合而成的词。它最初用于无线电设备，后来也用于其他同时具备发送和接收功能的通信设备。
etymology_story.en: Transceiver was coined in the twentieth century by blending transmitter and receiver. Originally associated with radio equipment, it later came to describe other communication devices that combine transmitting and receiving functions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：transmitter + receiver → transceiver，属于缩合词，不能简单分析为 trans- 加上独立词根 ceiver。复数：transceivers；相关基础词族：transmit（发送）、transmitter（发射器）、transmission（传输），以及 receive（接收）、receiver（接收器）、reception（接收）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: transmitter + receiver → transceiver, a blend rather than a straightforward combination of trans- and an independent root ceiver. Plural: transceivers. Related source-word families include transmit, transmitter, transmission, receive, receiver, and reception.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: transmitter-receiver（收发机）直接说明两项功能，与 transceiver 最接近；two-way radio（双向无线电设备）专指可双向通信的无线电设备；walkie-talkie（对讲机）进一步限定为便携式设备。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Transmitter-receiver is the closest equivalent and explicitly names both functions; two-way radio specifically denotes equipment for two-way radio communication; walkie-talkie refers more narrowly to a portable handheld device.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 transmitter 和 receiver 合成一个词，也把“发”和“收”装进同一台设备。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Combine transmitter and receiver in one word, just as the device combines sending and receiving.

meaning: 精神失常的；情绪失控的

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；ˈ 后的音节承重音，ˌ 表示次重音。

forms: 本卡是形容词；动词原形 unhinge，过去式及过去分词 unhinged，现在分词 unhinging。
family: unhinge 使失常；hinge 铰链

morphology.text: un-（解除）+ hinge（铰链）+ -ed → unhinged（像脱离铰链般失去稳定，情绪失控的）。

etymology.text: 英语 unhinge 原指把门从铰链上卸下，随后比喻使人失去精神上的稳定；其分词形容词发展为 unhinged。
