etymology_story.zh: testator 最终源自拉丁语 testator，与 testari（作证、正式声明、立遗嘱）有关。这一词源把遗嘱看作对本人意愿作出的正式声明，英语沿用了其法律含义。
etymology_story.en: Testator ultimately comes from Latin testator, related to testari, meaning to bear witness, make a formal declaration, or make a will. The legal meaning treats a will as a formal declaration of someone's wishes.

morphology_enriched.zh: testator 是借入的法律名词，可从历史构词上联系 testat-（作出声明、立遗嘱）与施事后缀 -or；不能理解为现代英语 test（测试）+ -ator。相关词族：testators（复数）、testatrix（传统女性称谓）、testatrices（其传统复数）、testate（留有有效遗嘱的）、intestate（未留有效遗嘱的）、testacy（留有有效遗嘱的状态）、intestacy（未留有效遗嘱的状态）、testament（遗嘱）、testamentary（遗嘱的、有关遗嘱的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Testator is a borrowed legal noun, historically associated with testat-, referring to declaring or making a will, and the agent suffix -or; it is not modern English test plus -ator. Its related family includes testators; testatrix, the traditional female term; testatrices, its traditional plural; testate, having left a valid will; intestate, without a valid will; testacy and intestacy, the corresponding states; testament, a will; and testamentary, relating to a will.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: will-maker 是通俗、性别中立的对应表达；testatrix 是传统上专指女性立遗嘱人的法律称谓，而 testator 现也可作性别中立用语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Will-maker is the plain-language, gender-neutral equivalent. Testatrix is the traditional legal term specifically for a woman, whereas testator can also be used without specifying gender.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联系 testament（遗嘱）：testator 就是作出这份正式意愿声明的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with testament: the testator is the person making that formal statement of wishes.

etymology_story.zh: polythene 是 polyethylene 的缩合形式，主要用于英国英语。polyethylene 的名称由 poly-（许多）和 ethylene（乙烯）组成，表示由许多乙烯分子聚合而成的材料。
etymology_story.en: Polythene is a contracted form of polyethylene, used chiefly in British English. Polyethylene combines poly-, meaning many, with ethylene, identifying a material formed by polymerizing many ethylene molecules.

morphology_enriched.zh: poly-（许多）+ ethylene（乙烯）→ polyethylene → 缩合为 polythene；不宜把 -thene 当作独立的现代英语词根。相关术语：polyethylene、polyethene（聚乙烯的同义名称）、PE（缩写）、ethylene/ethene（乙烯）、polymer（聚合物）、polymerization/polymerisation（聚合）。polythene bag 中 polythene 作名词定语，并不因此构成独立的常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Poly- meaning many + ethylene → polyethylene → contracted polythene; -thene should not be treated as an independent modern English root. Related terms include polyethylene and polyethene, equivalent names; PE, the abbreviation; ethylene/ethene, the starting compound; polymer; and polymerization/polymerisation. In polythene bag, polythene functions as a noun modifier rather than establishing a separate common adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: polyethylene 与 polythene 指同一种材料，前者更具国际通用性；polyethene 是与 ethene 命名相对应的同义名称；plastic（塑料）是更宽泛的上位词，不能精确限定为聚乙烯。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Polyethylene denotes the same material and is more internationally widespread. Polyethene is an equivalent name corresponding to ethene. Plastic is a broader category and does not specifically identify polyethylene.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: poly-＝许多：许多乙烯单元连成链，成为聚乙烯塑料。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Poly- means many: many ethylene units join into chains to make the plastic.

etymology_story.zh: 职业名 tanner 在中古英语中已有使用，与 tan（鞣皮）及法语同源词有关；传统鞣皮常使用含单宁的树皮。tan 后来发展出皮肤晒成棕褐色的含义，由此产生美黑产品的名称以及形容词比较级 tanner。
etymology_story.en: The occupational noun tanner was established in Middle English and is related to tan and corresponding French forms; traditional tanning often used tannin-rich bark. Tan later developed the sense of skin becoming brown, leading to the cosmetic noun and the adjective's comparative form tanner.

morphology_enriched.zh: 职业名和产品名：tan（鞣制；使皮肤呈棕褐色）+ -er（从业者或起相应作用的东西）→ tanner。形容词比较级：tan + -er（更……）→ tanner；两种构词均双写末尾 n。相关词族：tan、tans、tanned、tanning、tanners、tannest（tan 的最高级）、tannery（制革厂）、tanneries（其复数）、self-tanner（自助美黑产品）、self-tanning（自助美黑的）、suntan（晒黑；晒成的肤色）、suntanned（晒黑的）。
morphology_enriched.en: For the occupational and product nouns, tan + -er, meaning a worker or something producing an effect, → tanner. For the comparative adjective, tan + comparative -er → tanner; both formations double the final n. Related forms include tan, tans, tanned, tanning, tanners, tannest, tannery, tanneries, self-tanner, self-tanning, suntan, and suntanned.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: leatherworker（皮革工匠）范围更广，还包括用成品皮革制作物品的人；self-tanner 对应美黑产品义，明确指无需日晒即可产生效果的产品；browner 对应比较级义，但可描述任何东西颜色更棕，不限于肤色。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Leatherworker is broader and includes people who make goods from finished leather. Self-tanner matches the cosmetic sense and explicitly indicates an effect produced without sun exposure. Browner overlaps with the comparative adjective but can describe the colour of anything, not just skin.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先看 -er 的作用：tan + 从业者＝鞣皮匠；tan + 产品＝美黑剂；tan + 比较级＝晒得更黑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Read the job of -er: a tanning worker, a tanning product, or the comparative meaning more tan.

senses.meaning_zh: 胎儿；胎体，指胚胎期之后、出生之前的发育个体

etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 fetus，意为“生育、繁殖；后代、幼体”。foetus 是后来形成的传统异体拼写，现代主要用于英式英语；fetus 是美式英语及许多医学文献中的常用拼写。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin fetus, meaning the bearing of young or offspring. Foetus is a later traditional spelling used chiefly in British English; fetus is usual in American English and many medical publications.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，foetus 通常作为整体词基处理，不宜把 -us 当作可自由使用的英语后缀。构词时常用 foet- 或 foeto-：foet- + -al → foetal（胎儿的），foetal + -ly → foetally（在胎儿阶段）；其他常见相关词有 foetoscopy（胎儿镜检查）、foetoplacental（胎儿与胎盘的）、foetomaternal（胎儿与母体的）、foeticide（杀胎）和 foetotoxicity（胎儿毒性）。这些词通常都有相应的 fet-／feto- 拼写。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, foetus is generally treated as a whole base; -us is not a freely productive English suffix here. Related formations use foet- or foeto-: foet- + -al gives foetal, and foetal + -ly gives foetally. Other established relatives include foetoscopy, foetoplacental, foetomaternal, foeticide, and foetotoxicity, generally with corresponding fet- or feto- spellings.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fetus 是同一个词的另一种拼写，含义相同；embryo 指较早的胚胎阶段，并非严格同义词；unborn baby 是日常说法，通常指人类胎儿，语气更具个人和情感色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fetus is an alternative spelling with the same meaning. Embryo refers to an earlier developmental stage and is not an exact synonym. Unborn baby is an everyday expression, usually for a human foetus, with a more personal or emotional tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心锚点：尚未出生的后代；foetal 就是“胎儿的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor: offspring before birth; foetal means relating to the foetus.

senses.meaning_zh: 下方的；较低的；地下的，常用于文学或幽默表达
senses.meaning_en: Lower, beneath something else, or underground, especially in literary or humorous language.
senses.english_definition: The nether parts or regions of something are its lower parts or the areas beneath it.
senses.collocation_en: the nether regions; the nether world

etymology_story.zh: 经中古英语 nether 继承自古英语 niþera，意为“较低的、下面的”，与古英语表示“向下”的词有关。原本的空间含义后来延伸到地下世界，也用于幽默地指身体下部。
etymology_story.en: Middle English nether continues Old English niþera, meaning lower or situated below, related to an Old English word for downward. Its spatial meaning later extended to the underworld and to humorous references to the lower body.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，nether 是整体形容词，不能分析为 net + her；其历史上的比较含义已固定在词内。主要相关形式为 nether + world → netherworld（冥界；隐秘或不光彩的世界）；nethermost（最下面的）属于较少见的文学用词，nether 本身没有常用的现代动词或副词派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, nether is a whole adjective, not net + her; its historical comparative meaning is built into the word. Its principal relative is nether + world → netherworld, meaning the underworld or a hidden, sometimes disreputable sphere. Nethermost is a less common literary form meaning lowest; nether has no usual modern verb or adverb derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lower 是中性的“较低的”；underlying 强调位于某物之下，也可指潜在原因；subterranean 专指地表以下。nether 的文学色彩或幽默意味更强。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lower is the neutral term for a lower position. Underlying emphasizes being beneath something and can also describe hidden causes. Subterranean specifically means below the earth's surface. Nether has a more literary or humorous flavor.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心锚点：下面那一层；netherworld 就是想象中位于下方的世界。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor: the layer below; the netherworld is imagined as the world underneath.

senses.meaning_en: The inactive precursor protein that is activated to form plasmin.
senses.english_definition: Plasminogen is a protein in blood that can be changed into plasmin, an enzyme that breaks down fibrin in blood clots.

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代生化术语，由 plasmin（纤溶酶）与表示前体或生成来源的构词成分 -ogen 组成。plasmin 的名称与 plasma（血浆）有关；整个名称表达的是“能够生成纤溶酶的前体”。
etymology_story.en: This modern biochemical term combines plasmin with -ogen, a formative indicating a precursor or source of something. Plasmin is named in relation to plasma, and plasminogen therefore identifies the precursor from which plasmin is formed.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可分析为 plasmin + -ogen，也可展开为 plasmin + 连接元音 -o- + -gen；在本词中，整体表示纤溶酶的前体。主要相关术语包括 plasmin（纤溶酶）、plasminogen activator（纤溶酶原激活剂）、plasminogen activation（纤溶酶原激活）和 antiplasmin（抗纤溶酶）；这些相关术语并非全部直接派生自 plasminogen。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure is plasmin + -ogen, also analyzable as plasmin + linking -o- + -gen; here the whole formation names the precursor of plasmin. Principal related terms include plasmin, plasminogen activator, plasminogen activation, and antiplasmin. These are related biochemical terms, not all direct derivatives of plasminogen.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: profibrinolysin 是较旧的同义名称；plasmin precursor 是说明性的等义表达；zymogen（酶原）是上位词，泛指无活性的酶前体。plasmin 则是激活后的纤溶酶，不能与 plasminogen 混用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Profibrinolysin is an older synonymous name. Plasmin precursor is a descriptive equivalent. Zymogen is the broader category of inactive enzyme precursors. Plasmin is the activated enzyme and must not be confused with plasminogen.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心锚点：plasmin 是酶，plasminogen 是等待激活的酶原。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor: plasmin is the enzyme; plasminogen is its precursor waiting to be activated.

etymology_story.zh: 副词 infra 直接借自拉丁语 infrā，意为“在下面”，在正式写作中用于指向文档后面的内容。技术口语中的名词 infra 则是 infrastructure 的截短形式，属于另一条现代构词路径。
etymology_story.en: The adverb infra was borrowed directly from Latin infrā, meaning below, and is used in formal writing to point to later material. The informal technical noun is a separate modern clipping of infrastructure.

morphology_enriched.zh: 副词 infra 在现代英语中通常作为整体处理，没有常用的屈折或派生形式；技术名词则为 infrastructure → infra 的截短词。同形前缀 infra- 表示“在……以下”，见 infra- + red → infrared（红外线的）和 infra- + sonic → infrasonic（次声的）；这些是前缀构词，不能据此给独立词 infra 增加形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: The adverb infra is normally treated as a whole word in modern English and has no usual inflected or derived forms; the technical noun is clipped from infrastructure. The matching prefix infra- means below, as in infra- + red → infrared and infra- + sonic → infrasonic. These prefixed formations do not establish an adjective use for the independent word infra.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 副词义：below 是更通用、更自然的“在下文”；later in this document 明确指本文后面的内容；supra 意为“见上文”，是反义对应词。名词义：infrastructure 是完整、中性的形式；IT infrastructure 更明确限定为信息技术基础设施。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the adverb, below is the more general and natural alternative, while later in this document makes the reference explicit. Supra is its opposite, pointing backward. For the noun, infrastructure is the full neutral form, while IT infrastructure specifically identifies information-technology systems.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心锚点：读到 infra，就把视线往文档下方移；技术语境里则把它展开为 infrastructure。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor: infra tells your eyes to move down the document; in technical conversation, expand it to infrastructure.

etymology_story.zh: wellie，也拼作 welly，是 Wellington boot 的口语昵称形式；这种靴子的名称来自第一代威灵顿公爵，早期款式为皮靴，后来常指橡胶防水靴。表示“力气、动力”以及“用力踢”的用法，与靴子和用脚使劲的联想有关。
etymology_story.en: Wellie, also spelled welly, is an informal nickname for a Wellington boot, named after the first Duke of Wellington; the original leather style was later associated with waterproof rubber boots. The meanings involving force, power, and hard kicking are associated with boots and vigorous use of the foot.

morphology_enriched.zh: Wellington 截短后加昵称式后缀 -ie／-y → wellie／welly；这里的 well- 不是副词 well（好）。名词复数为 wellies；动词由名词转类而来，常见屈折形式为 wellies、wellied、wellying。相关形式包括 Wellington boot（威灵顿靴）和 wellie boot（长筒雨靴）；没有常用的专属形容词或副词派生。
morphology_enriched.en: A shortened form of Wellington takes the familiar suffix -ie or -y to produce wellie or welly; well- here is not the adverb well. The noun plural is wellies. The verb arises by conversion from the noun and commonly inflects as wellies, wellied, and wellying. Related expressions include Wellington boot and wellie boot; there are no usual dedicated adjective or adverb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 雨靴义：Wellington boot 是完整名称，rubber boot 强调材质，rain boot 强调防雨用途且常见于美式英语。力气义：effort 强调投入的努力，force 强调施加的力量，power 强调动力或输出。动词义：kick 是中性词，boot 常指用脚踢，belt 在这里强调猛力踢出。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For footwear, Wellington boot is the full name, rubber boot emphasizes material, and rain boot emphasizes wet-weather use and is common in American English. For exertion, effort emphasizes application, force emphasizes physical strength, and power emphasizes output. For the verb, kick is neutral, boot suggests kicking with the foot, and belt emphasizes a very forceful kick.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心锚点：穿上雨靴，用脚使劲；一双 wellies，给它 some wellie，再 wellie 一脚。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor: boots on, foot down—wear wellies, give it some wellie, or wellie the ball.

meaning: 古怪糊涂的；有点疯癫的

etymology.text: 英语的“古怪糊涂”义常联系 dote（糊涂、痴迷）一词的历史用法；另一个“多点的”义由 dot 加 -y 形成。用语境区分这两个来源线索。

etymology_story.zh: 表示“糊涂、古怪”的 dotty 见于19世纪，通常与 dote 的“糊涂、痴迷”等历史含义联系起来。“布满圆点”的 dotty 则由 dot 加 -y 构成，不宜用这一构词直接解释“古怪”义。
etymology_story.en: Dotty meaning 'eccentric or confused' is recorded in the nineteenth century and is commonly associated with historical senses of dote involving confusion or excessive fondness. The separate meaning 'covered with dots' transparently combines dot and -y and should not be used to explain the eccentricity sense.

morphology_enriched.zh: 圆点义：dot（圆点）+ -y（具有……的）→ dotty，末尾辅音 t 双写；古怪义在现代英语中宜整词识记。直接词族：dotty、比较级 dottier、最高级 dottiest、dottily（古怪地）、dottiness（古怪；糊涂）；圆点相关词有 dot、dotted、dotting；另可联系 dote、doting、dotingly，但这些不是现代英语中由 dotty 直接派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: For the spotted sense, dot + -y forms dotty, with the final t doubled; the eccentricity sense is best learned as a whole modern word. Its direct family includes dotty, dottier, dottiest, dottily, and dottiness; dot-related forms include dot, dotted, and dotting. Dote, doting, and dotingly provide a separate historical connection rather than direct modern derivatives of dotty.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: eccentric 强调行为或习惯异于常人，不一定糊涂；batty 与“古怪、疯癫”义接近，同属非正式用语；dotted 对应“有圆点的”这一独立词义，通常更中性。dotty about 则可用 crazy about 表达。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Eccentric emphasizes unusual habits without necessarily suggesting confusion; batty is a similarly informal word for slightly crazy; dotted matches the separate spotted sense and is usually more neutral. For dotty about, crazy about is a close equivalent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 分两条记：dot + -y＝有圆点；古怪义联想 dote 的“糊涂、痴迷”，dotty about＝痴迷于。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep two tracks: dot + -y means 'having dots'; connect eccentric dotty with dote, and learn dotty about as 'extremely fond of'.

etymology_story.zh: verity 经中古英语 verite，借自盎格鲁诺曼语及古法语的相关形式，最终源于拉丁语 veritas（真实、真理），其基础是 verus（真实的）。它既可表示“真实这一性质”，也可指一条被认为恒久成立的道理，后者常用复数 verities。
etymology_story.en: Verity entered Middle English as verite through Anglo-Norman and Old French forms, ultimately from Latin veritas, 'truth', based on verus, 'true'. It can denote truth as a quality or an enduring truth, with the latter meaning frequently appearing in the plural verities.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中主要作为完整借词识记；可用历史词干 ver-（真）+ -ity（性质、状态）辅助分析，但不是现代自由词根的常规拼接。直接形式：verity → verities；同源词族包括 veritable、veritably、verify、verifies、verified、verifying、verification、verifiable、unverifiable、veracity、veracious、veraciously，不能把它们都视为由 verity 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, verity is primarily a borrowed whole word; historical ver- 'true' + -ity 'quality or state' offers a useful analysis rather than a freely productive modern formation. Its direct plural is verities. Related Latin-root words include veritable, veritably, verify, verifies, verified, verifying, verification, verifiable, unverifiable, veracity, veracious, and veraciously; these are not all direct derivatives of verity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: truth 最通用，既可指事实真相，也可指道理；truism 指明显到几乎不值得说的道理，常有“老生常谈”意味；axiom 指作为推理基础而被接受的公理或原则。verity 更庄重，常强调道理的根本性与恒久性。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Truth is the broad everyday term; a truism is so obviously true that stating it may seem unhelpful; an axiom is a principle accepted as a basis for reasoning. Verity is more elevated and often suggests a fundamental, enduring truth.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ver-＝真：verity 是“真实或真理”，verify 是“核实是否真实”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the shared 'true' element: a verity is a truth, and to verify is to establish that something is true.

etymology_story.zh: cholangitis 是由希腊语来源的医学构词成分组成的术语：cholē 表示“胆汁”，angeion 表示“容器、管道”，-itis 表示“炎症”。这些成分组合后，名称直接表达“胆汁管道的炎症”。
etymology_story.en: Cholangitis is a medical formation using Greek-derived elements: cholē means 'bile', angeion means 'vessel', and -itis denotes inflammation. Together, they identify inflammation of the ducts that carry bile.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代医学构词：cholangi/o（胆管）+ -itis（炎症）→ cholangitis；后缀以元音开头，因此连接元音 o 省略。直接相关形式有 cholangitic（胆管炎的）；同一组合形式构成的术语包括 cholangiography（胆管造影）、cholangiogram（胆管造影图）、cholangioscopy（胆管镜检查）、cholangiocyte（胆管上皮细胞）和 cholangiocarcinoma（胆管癌），这些是同词干术语，不是 cholangitis 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern medical formation: cholangi/o 'bile duct' + -itis 'inflammation' → cholangitis; the combining vowel o is omitted before the vowel-initial suffix. A directly related adjective is cholangitic. Terms sharing the combining form include cholangiography, cholangiogram, cholangioscopy, cholangiocyte, and cholangiocarcinoma; these are related formations, not direct derivatives of cholangitis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bile duct inflammation 是准确、易懂的释义性近义表达；biliary tract inflammation（胆道炎症）范围可能更宽，并非在所有语境中都与 cholangitis 完全等同。cholangitis 本身表示炎症，不应自动等同于“胆管感染”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bile duct inflammation is an accurate plain-language equivalent. Biliary tract inflammation can have a broader scope and is not interchangeable in every context. Cholangitis denotes inflammation and should not automatically be treated as a synonym for bile duct infection.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cholangi-＝胆管，-itis＝炎症：胆管＋发炎＝胆管炎。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cholangi- identifies the bile ducts; -itis identifies inflammation: inflamed bile ducts.

etymology_story.zh: biff 在19世纪英语中出现，通常被认为是模仿突然击打声的拟声词。它先后用来表示“一记重击”和“猛击”，在部分北美非正式用法中又扩展为“失手、搞砸或摔倒”。
etymology_story.en: Biff appeared in nineteenth-century English and is generally regarded as an imitation of the sound of a sudden blow. It came to name a blow and the action of striking, with some North American informal uses extending to botching an attempt or taking a fall.

morphology_enriched.zh: biff 是独立的拟声词词基，现代英语中不再拆分；名词与动词形式相同。词形包括名词复数或动词第三人称单数 biffs、过去式及过去分词 biffed、现在分词 biffing；biff + -er → biffer（猛击者；用力击球的人，较少见）。
morphology_enriched.en: Biff is an independent sound-symbolic base with no further modern morphological breakdown; the same form serves as a noun and a verb. Its forms include biffs, biffed, and biffing. Biff + -er produces the less common biffer, a hard hitter.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: punch 明确指用拳头击打；whack 强调有力的一击，不限于拳头；botch 对应“搞砸”义，强调做得不好，通常不表示摔倒。biff 的击打义带有鲜明的口语和拟声色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Punch specifically involves the fist; whack emphasizes a forceful hit with a hand or another object; botch matches the failure sense and usually does not imply falling. In its striking sense, biff has a distinctly informal, sound-imitating flavor.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 听到“biff!”就想到“砰，一下重击”；运动中 biff it，再联想失手摔了一下。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hear 'biff!' as the sound of a hard hit; in sports, biff it can suggest a failed move ending in a tumble.

etymology_story.zh: Geordie 原是人名 George 的昵称，后来成为纽卡斯尔及泰恩赛德居民的地域称呼，并进一步指当地的方言和口音。关于这一昵称为何专指当地居民，存在不同历史解释，不宜把其中某一种当作确定事实。
etymology_story.en: Geordie began as a familiar form of the personal name George and later became a regional name for people from Newcastle and Tyneside, then for their speech. Several historical explanations compete to explain that regional association, so no single popular story should be presented as certain.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可分析为 George 的昵称词干 Geord- + 昵称后缀 -ie，但 George → Geord- 属于约定俗成的昵称变化，并非现代通用拼写规则。居民称呼的复数为 Geordies；表示方言时通常不可数，形容词用法不发生词形变化；常见相关组合有 Geordie accent、Geordie dialect、Geordie speaker。首字母通常大写。
morphology_enriched.en: Geordie can be analyzed as the nickname stem Geord-, associated with George, plus the familiar-name suffix -ie; George → Geord- is a conventional nickname formation rather than a productive spelling rule. The plural for people is Geordies; the dialect name is normally uncountable, and the adjective is invariant. Related combinations include Geordie accent, Geordie dialect, and Geordie speaker. The initial capital is normally retained.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Newcastle native 是指人的明确释义性表达，但比某些用法中的 Geordie 地域范围窄；Tynesider 指泰恩赛德居民，与 Geordie 常有重合；Northumbrian 的地域或方言范围不同，不能直接互换。Geordie 还可指口音、方言，这一点不能由居民称呼在所有语境中替代。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Newcastle native is a clear equivalent for a person, though geographically narrower than some uses of Geordie; Tynesider often overlaps with Geordie as a name for a resident. Northumbrian has a different geographical or linguistic scope and is not directly interchangeable. Geordie also names an accent or dialect, which resident labels cannot replace in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the naming chain: George's nickname Geordie → people around Newcastle → their accent and dialect.

senses.english_definition: If you collocate things, you put them together in a particular arrangement or location.
senses.collocation_en: collocate words; collocate facilities
senses.collocation_zh: 把词语组合在一起；将设施集中设置
senses.sentence_en: The proposal would collocate the two facilities on a single site.
senses.sentence_zh: 该提案将把这两处设施集中设在同一个地点。

senses.meaning_zh: 搭配词；与某词惯常共同出现的词
senses.meaning_en: a word that frequently occurs with a particular word
senses.english_definition: A collocate of a word is another word that is frequently used with it.
senses.collocation_en: a frequent collocate; verb collocates
senses.collocation_zh: 高频搭配词；动词搭配词
senses.sentence_en: 'Commit' is a frequent collocate of 'crime'.
senses.sentence_zh: commit 是 crime 的一个高频搭配词。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 collocare（放在一起）的分词词干 collocat-，其中 col- 表示“共同”，locare 表示“放置”。英语中的一般“共同放置”义后来发展出语言学上的“词语惯常共现”义。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from collocat-, the participial stem of Latin collocare, meaning 'to place together', formed from col- 'together' and locare 'to place'. The general idea of placing things together later developed into the linguistic meaning of words habitually occurring together.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为黏着词干 colloc- + -ate，但不能把 loc 当作可独立使用的现代英语词；col- + loc- 的解释属于历史构词。常用词族：collocates、collocated、collocating；collocation（搭配）、collocations、collocational（搭配的）、collocationally（从搭配角度）；较专门的相关形式有 collocability（搭配能力）和 collocable（可搭配的）。名词 collocate 与动词同形，但末音节通常弱读。
morphology_enriched.en: A modern analysis recognizes the bound stem colloc- plus -ate; loc is not an independent modern English word, and the col- + loc- analysis is historical. The usual family includes collocates, collocated, collocating, collocation, collocations, collocational, and collocationally; more specialized forms include collocability and collocable. The noun collocate has the same spelling as the verb but usually has a reduced final syllable.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: co-occur（共现）只说明共同出现，不一定构成惯常搭配；go with（与……搭配）更口语化；combine（组合）强调结合，未必涉及使用频率。名词义可用 lexical partner（词汇搭配伙伴）解释。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Co-occur means to appear together without necessarily forming a habitual combination; go with is a less technical alternative; combine emphasizes joining rather than frequency of use. For the noun, lexical partner is a useful explanatory equivalent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “共同放置”→ 词语常待在一起 → 惯常搭配。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Placed together → words that regularly stay together → habitual word partners.

forms: 可数名词；复数 publicans。

morphology.text: public（联系 public house“酒馆”）+ -an（人）→ publican（酒馆经营者）；现代职业义用这条线索记忆。

etymology.text: 英语较早的 publican 经中古英语和法语联系拉丁语 publicanus（税吏）；后来酒馆老板义与 public house 这一酒馆名称相联系，形成今天常见的英国用法。

senses.meaning_en: a person who owns or manages a pub, chiefly in British usage
senses.english_definition: A publican is someone who owns or manages a pub.

senses.meaning_zh: （古罗马及《圣经》语境中的）税收承包人；税吏
senses.meaning_en: a tax contractor or tax collector in ancient Roman or biblical contexts
senses.english_definition: In accounts of ancient Rome or in older Bible translations, a publican is someone who contracts to collect public revenue or collects taxes.
senses.collocation_en: a Roman publican; publicans and sinners
senses.collocation_zh: 古罗马税收承包人；税吏与罪人
senses.sentence_en: In older English Bible translations, Matthew is described as a publican.
senses.sentence_zh: 在较早的英语《圣经》译本中，马太被称为税吏。

etymology_story.zh: 较早的“税收承包人、税吏”义经法语源自拉丁语 publicanus，后者与 publicus（公共的、国家的）有关。十八世纪出现的英国“酒馆经营者”义与 public house（酒馆）这一名称相联系。
etymology_story.en: The older tax-related meaning came through French from Latin publicanus, related to publicus, meaning 'public' or 'of the state'. The British meaning 'pub keeper', recorded from the eighteenth century, developed through association with public house.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代通常把 publican 作为完整职业名词使用：publican + -s → publicans。public + -an 可作记忆性分析，但它并非现代英语中简单、透明的“公共的 + 人”派生；public、publicly、publicity、publicize 与其历史词根相关，却不是由 publican 派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, publican normally functions as a complete occupational noun: publican + -s gives publicans. Public + -an can serve as a memory aid, but the word is not a straightforward modern formation meaning 'public person'; public, publicly, publicity, and publicize share its historical root but are not derivatives of publican.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pub landlord／pub landlady（酒馆经营者）与现代职业义接近，并区分性别；licensee（持牌经营者）强调持有经营许可证，范围不限于酒馆；tax collector（税吏）对应其历史或《圣经》义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pub landlord or pub landlady closely matches the modern occupational meaning and specifies gender; licensee emphasizes legal authorization and can refer to other licensed businesses; tax collector matches the historical or biblical meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: public house 是酒馆，publican 是经营酒馆的人；历史义则联系国家税收。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A public house has a publican; the older meaning connects the word with public revenue.

forms: 材料或蛋白质总称通常不可数；不同类型可用 gliadins。
family: antigliadin 抗麦醇溶蛋白的；gluten 面筋蛋白

morphology.text: anti-（抗）+ gliadin → antigliadin（抗麦醇溶蛋白的）；gliadin 整词作为独立词素记忆，不按日常词硬拆。

etymology.text: 英语 gliadin 联系意大利语 gloiodina，这个蛋白名称由十九世纪研究者 Taddei 创造；用小麦面筋中的一种蛋白来记，不把名字中的字母当作日常英语词根。

usage_note: 食品科学和生化术语，指小麦面筋中的一种蛋白；不是小麦中的糖，也不等于面筋全部成分。

translation: 实验室从小麦样本中分离出了麦醇溶蛋白。
scenario: 食品实验室研究小麦中的蛋白成分。

senses.meaning_zh: 麦醇溶蛋白；麦胶蛋白，构成小麦面筋的一类蛋白质
senses.meaning_en: a class of wheat proteins that form part of gluten and dissolve in aqueous alcohol
senses.english_definition: Gliadin is a type of protein found in wheat that forms part of gluten and can dissolve in a mixture of alcohol and water.
senses.collocation_en: gliadin proteins; anti-gliadin antibodies
senses.collocation_zh: 麦醇溶蛋白类蛋白质；抗麦醇溶蛋白抗体
senses.sentence_en: The researchers extracted gliadin from wheat flour using an alcohol solution.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员用醇溶液从小麦粉中提取了麦醇溶蛋白。

etymology_story.zh: 这个名称形成于十九世纪欧洲对小麦面筋的研究，词源最终联系希腊语中表示“胶、黏性物质”的词。它后来成为面筋中一类蛋白质的专门名称。
etymology_story.en: The name emerged from nineteenth-century European research on wheat gluten and ultimately relates to Greek words for glue or a sticky substance. It became the technical name for a class of proteins within gluten.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代以 gliadin 为完整科学词干，不宜硬拆成日常英语词根；词尾 -in 符合许多蛋白质名称的形式。相关形式：gliadins（不同种类的麦醇溶蛋白）、anti-gliadin／antigliadin（抗麦醇溶蛋白的）；α-gliadin、γ-gliadin、ω-gliadin 表示不同类别。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats gliadin as a complete scientific base rather than a transparent combination of everyday roots; its ending -in follows a common pattern in protein names. Related forms include gliadins for different types, anti-gliadin or antigliadin, and class names such as α-gliadin, γ-gliadin, and ω-gliadin.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有通用且完全等义的英语近义词。prolamin（醇溶谷蛋白）是其所属的更大蛋白质类别；gluten（面筋蛋白）包含麦醇溶蛋白与其他组分；glutenin（麦谷蛋白）是面筋中的另一类主要蛋白，不能与 gliadin 混用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no widely used exact English synonym. Prolamin names the broader protein class to which gliadin belongs; gluten contains gliadin alongside other components; glutenin is another major class of gluten proteins and is not interchangeable with gliadin.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“胶”的历史意象，联想到黏性面筋中的一种蛋白。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The historical glue image points to a protein within sticky wheat gluten.

meaning: 指示功能；依语境确定所指的现象
aliases: 指示功能；依语境确定所指的现象
依语境确定所指的现象

pronunciation.note: ˈ 标出主重音；按完整单词连读。

forms: 语言学抽象名词，通常不可数。
family: deictic 指示的；deictically 以指示方式

morphology.text: 希腊语 deik-（显示、指出）+ -sis（动作或过程）→ deixis（指示）；现代英语把它作为独立术语整词记忆。

etymology.text: 英语借自古希腊语 deixis（指点、指示），源于 deiknymi（我显示、我指出）；联想说话人指着某处说“这里”。

usage_note: 语言学术语。here、now、I 等表达的具体所指依赖说话时间、地点或说话人；单看词本身往往无法确定所指。
sentence: The teacher used the word here to introduce deixis.
translation: 老师用 here 这个词来介绍指示功能。
scenario: 语言课堂比较不同说话人使用 here 时指向的地点。
cloze: The teacher used the word here to introduce _____.
collocation:
spatial deixis 空间指示
temporal deixis 时间指示
context_hint: The reference shifts when the speaker changes.
hint: The reference shifts when the speaker changes.

teaching.translation: 关于指示功能的讲座说明了 tomorrow 为什么每天所指的日期都不同。

senses.meaning_zh: 指示；词语的所指依说话人、时间、地点等语境确定的现象
senses.meaning_en: reference whose interpretation depends on the context of an utterance
senses.english_definition: Deixis is the use of words such as 'I', 'here', and 'now' whose reference depends on who is speaking and on the situation in which they are used.
senses.collocation_en: spatial deixis; temporal deixis
senses.collocation_zh: 空间指示；时间指示
senses.sentence_en: The words 'here' and 'there' are common examples of spatial deixis.
senses.sentence_zh: here 和 there 这两个词是空间指示的常见例子。

etymology_story.zh: 借自古希腊语 deixis（显示、指示），与表示“显示、指出”的动词 deiknymi 同源。英语语言学沿用“指出”的意象，指通过说话情境确定人、时间、地点等所指的机制。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Ancient Greek deixis, meaning 'showing' or 'pointing', and is related to deiknymi, 'I show' or 'I point out'. Linguistics retains this pointing image for reference to people, times, places, and other features interpreted through the speaking situation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语把 deixis 作为整体术语使用；历史上可联系 deik-（显示、指出）与希腊语动作名词后缀 -sis，但这不是现代英语中的能产拆分。核心词族：deictic（指示的）、deictically（以指示方式）、non-deictic／nondeictic（非指示的）；deictic 采用相关的希腊语词干形式，不能机械地写成 deixis + -ic。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats deixis as a whole technical term; historically, it connects with deik- 'show, point' and the Greek action-noun ending -sis, rather than a productive modern English combination. Its core family includes deictic, deictically, and non-deictic or nondeictic; deictic uses a related Greek stem form rather than a mechanical deixis + -ic construction.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: indexicality（索引性）与之高度重叠，但在某些理论中范围更广；context-dependent reference（依赖语境的指称）是便于理解的解释性近义表达；reference（指称）是上位概念，也包含不依赖当前说话情境的指称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Indexicality overlaps strongly with deixis but can have a broader scope in some theories; context-dependent reference is a useful explanatory near-equivalent; reference is the broader category and also includes reference that does not depend on the immediate speaking situation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 像手指一样的词：谁说、何时说、在哪里说，决定它指什么。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Words that point: who speaks, when, and where determine what they refer to.

meaning: 难以根除的祸患；问题层出不穷的局面

forms: 可数名词；复数 hydras。另有水螅义及神话专名 Hydra。
family: hydralike 像九头蛇般的；hydra-headed 多头的，问题层出的

morphology.text: hydra + -like → hydralike（像九头蛇般难缠的）；hydra 整词作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 英语借用希腊神话 Hydra 的形象：砍掉一个头又长出新头；因此用小写 hydra 比喻解决一处又冒出另一处的祸患。

usage_note: 本卡学比喻义，常见 a hydra of problems。神话怪物名 Hydra 大写；泛指难缠除患或水螅时小写。

scenario: 处理一个腐败环节时，调查人员发现还有多个互相牵连的环节。

senses.sentence_en: The investigation revealed a hydra of corruption stretching across several departments.
senses.sentence_zh: 调查揭露了一个蔓延至多个部门、盘根错节的腐败祸患。

etymology_story.zh: 经拉丁语源自希腊语 hydra（水蛇），与表示“水”的词 hydōr 同源；神话中的 Hydra 因断头后又生新头而著名。这个形象产生了“难以根除的祸患”义，而水螅的名称也呼应其触手外形与再生能力。
etymology_story.en: The word came through Latin from Greek hydra, 'water snake', related to hydōr, 'water'; the mythical Hydra was famous for growing new heads after losing them. This image produced the figurative meaning of a persistent evil, while the freshwater animal's name also evokes its tentacles and regenerative ability.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代 hydra 是完整词干，不应拆成 hydro- + -a。复数为 hydras，也可见学术性复数 hydrae；相关构词有 hydra-headed（多头的；问题层出不穷的）、hydralike／hydra-like（水螅似的；多头怪似的）以及相关科学词 hydroid（水螅状的；水螅类动物）。Hydra 用于神话专名和生物属名时首字母大写。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern hydra is a complete base, not a combination of hydro- and -a. Its plural is hydras, with hydrae also used in scholarly contexts; related formations include hydra-headed, hydralike or hydra-like, and the scientific word hydroid. Hydra is capitalized as the mythological name and as a biological genus name.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: freshwater polyp（淡水水螅体）可解释其动物义，但 polyp 本身范围更广；scourge（严重祸患）强调危害，未必暗示解决后又复发；intractable problem（棘手难题）强调难以处理，而 hydra 特别突出问题不断分枝、再生。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Freshwater polyp can explain the animal sense, although polyp itself is broader; scourge emphasizes serious harm without necessarily implying recurrence; intractable problem emphasizes difficulty, while hydra particularly suggests multiplying or regenerating difficulties.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 砍一头，又长新头：既联想水螅再生，也记住祸患难除。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cut off one head and more appear: connect regeneration with a problem that keeps returning.

pronunciation.note: ˈ 标出主重音；按完整单词连读。

forms: 可数名词；复数常用 lacunae，也可用 lacunas。
family: lacunar 有空隙的；lacunae 空缺（复数）

morphology.text: lacuna + -ar → lacunar（有空隙的）；派生时去掉末尾 a，lacuna 整词作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 英语借自拉丁语 lacuna（坑、空洞、缺口）；把纸页上少掉的一块文字想成知识中的一个小坑。

usage_note: 正式书面用语，可指文本、记录或知识中的缺漏；医学中还可指小腔隙，本卡学习缺失部分义。

translation: 缺失的一页在手稿中留下了一处空缺。
scenario: 整理旧手稿时发现中间缺了一页内容。

a lacuna in our knowledge 知识中的空白
context_hint: Something is missing from that year in the records.
hint: Something is missing from that year in the records.

senses.meaning_zh: 文字、知识或论述中的空缺；缺漏
senses.meaning_en: A gap or missing part in a text, body of knowledge, or argument.
senses.english_definition: A lacuna is a gap where something is missing from a text, an account, or someone's knowledge.

senses.meaning_zh: 腔隙；陷窝，尤指骨或软骨组织中的小腔
senses.meaning_en: A small cavity in tissue, especially bone or cartilage.
senses.english_definition: In anatomy, a lacuna is a small space within a tissue, such as a cavity containing a bone cell.
senses.collocation_en: osteocyte lacunae; lacunae in cartilage

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自拉丁语 lacuna，原指坑、凹陷或空洞，与 lacus（湖、水池）有关。具体的“空洞”后来引申为文字、记录或知识中的“缺漏”，解剖学则保留了小腔隙的空间含义。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Latin lacuna, meaning a pit, hollow, or cavity, related to lacus, meaning a lake or pool. The physical hollow developed into a figurative gap in texts, records, or knowledge, while anatomy retained the spatial meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 lacuna 是整体借入的名词，不宜硬拆为常用英语词根与词缀。学术构词使用词干 lacun-：lacun- + -ar → lacunar（腔隙的）；lacun- + -ary → lacunary（有缺漏的）；lacun- + -ose → lacunose（多孔隙的；有缺漏的）；lacunar + -ity → lacunarity（空隙性；空隙度）。名词复数为 lacunae，也可用 lacunas。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, lacuna is a borrowed base rather than a transparent combination of everyday English morphemes. Learned formations use lacun-: lacun- + -ar → lacunar, relating to cavities; lacun- + -ary → lacunary, containing gaps; lacun- + -ose → lacunose, full of cavities or gaps; lacunar + -ity → lacunarity, the property or degree of gappiness. The plural is lacunae or lacunas.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gap（空白、间隙）最通用，也可指实体之间的距离；omission（遗漏）强调被省去或漏掉的内容；hiatus（中断、间断）强调时间或连续过程中的断裂。lacuna 更正式，常指文本或知识体系中本应有内容的位置出现空缺。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gap is the broadest term and can describe physical separation; omission emphasizes something left out; hiatus emphasizes a break in time or continuity. Lacuna is more formal and often identifies missing material within a text or body of knowledge.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 lacuna 想成知识表面上的一个“小坑”：有结构，却缺了一块内容。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a little hollow in the surface of knowledge: the structure is there, but one piece is missing.

senses.meaning_zh: 在本页背面；见反面

senses.english_definition: If information is overleaf, it is on the other side of the sheet you are reading.

senses.sentence_zh: 填写此表前，请先阅读本页背面的说明。

etymology_story.zh: overleaf 由 over 与 leaf 组合而成，leaf 在这里使用“纸张的一张、书的一叶”这一历史悠久的含义。整个词表示把这一叶翻过去后，在它背面看到内容。
etymology_story.en: Overleaf combines over with leaf in its long-established sense of a sheet of paper or a leaf of a book. It directs the reader to turn that leaf over and look at its reverse.

morphology_enriched.zh: over（翻到另一面）+ leaf（一张纸、一叶书页）→ overleaf（在本页背面），是复合副词，无常用屈折变化或标准派生词。相关表达有 turn over（翻过来）、turn the page（翻页）和 on the reverse（在背面）；它们是相关短语，并非 overleaf 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Over, indicating movement to the other side, + leaf, a sheet of paper, → overleaf, a compound adverb. It has no ordinary inflections or established common derivatives. Related expressions include turn over, turn the page, and on the reverse; these are associated phrases rather than derivatives of overleaf.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: on the reverse（在背面）较正式；on the back（在背面）更口语化，适用对象也不限于纸张。overleaf 专用于引导读者查看当前纸张的背面，不能笼统等同于 on the next page（在下一页）。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: On the reverse is relatively formal; on the back is more conversational and can refer to objects other than paper. Overleaf specifically directs the reader to the reverse of the current sheet and is not a general equivalent of on the next page.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: leaf 是一张纸；把它翻过去（over），答案就在背面。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A leaf is a sheet: turn it over, and the information is on the back.

pronunciation.note: ˈ 标出主重音；按完整单词连读。

forms: 通常不可数；不同磷酸化事件可用 phosphorylations。
family: phosphoryl 磷酰基；phosphorylate 使磷酸化

morphology.text: phosphoryl（磷酰基）+ -ation（过程）→ phosphorylation（磷酸化过程）。

etymology.text: 现代科学英语由 phosphoryl 加过程名词后缀 -ation 形成；phosphoryl 的名称联系 phosphorus（磷），后者经拉丁语来自希腊语“带来光的”。先抓住“加上含磷基团的过程”。

senses.meaning_zh: 磷酸化；向分子中引入磷酸基团的过程
senses.meaning_en: The addition of a phosphate group to a molecule.
senses.english_definition: Phosphorylation is a chemical process in which a phosphate group is added to a molecule, often changing its activity or storing energy.
senses.collocation_en: protein phosphorylation; oxidative phosphorylation
senses.collocation_zh: 蛋白质磷酸化；氧化磷酸化
senses.sentence_en: Phosphorylation of the protein changes its activity.

etymology_story.zh: phosphorylation 是现代科学英语中与 phosphorylate（使磷酸化）对应的过程名词，其构词基础 phosphoryl（磷酰基）与 phosphorus（磷）有关。phosphorus 经拉丁语源自希腊语 phōsphoros，意为“带来光的”，但 phosphorylation 的现代含义是加入磷酸基团，并非发光。
etymology_story.en: Phosphorylation arose in scientific English as the process noun corresponding to phosphorylate, built on phosphoryl, a chemical term related to phosphorus. Phosphorus comes through Latin from Greek phōsphoros, meaning light-bringing, although phosphorylation itself means adding a phosphate group rather than producing light.

morphology_enriched.zh: phosphoryl（磷酰基）+ -ate（构成动词）→ phosphorylate（使磷酸化）；phosphorylate 去掉末尾 e，再加 -ion → phosphorylation（磷酸化）。主要词族包括 phosphorylates（动词第三人称单数）、phosphorylated（已磷酸化的；过去式及过去分词）、phosphorylating（正在使磷酸化；现在分词）、dephosphorylate（使去磷酸化）、dephosphorylation（去磷酸化）、autophosphorylation（自磷酸化）、hyperphosphorylation（过度磷酸化）和 hypophosphorylation（磷酸化不足）。
morphology_enriched.en: Phosphoryl, a chemical group name, + verbal -ate → phosphorylate; remove the final e and add -ion → phosphorylation. Major family members include phosphorylates, the third-person singular verb; phosphorylated, the past tense, past participle, and an adjective; phosphorylating, the present participle; dephosphorylate and dephosphorylation, removing a phosphate group and the corresponding process; autophosphorylation, self-phosphorylation; hyperphosphorylation, excessive phosphorylation; and hypophosphorylation, reduced phosphorylation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: phosphate addition（添加磷酸基团）是直接的解释性近义表达；phosphate-group transfer（磷酸基团转移）强调基团从供体转移到受体的机制，适用于许多磷酸化反应，但不能在所有语境中完全替换 phosphorylation。该术语没有常用的日常英语单词近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Phosphate addition is a direct explanatory equivalent. Phosphate-group transfer emphasizes movement from a donor to an acceptor and describes many phosphorylation reactions, but it is not interchangeable with phosphorylation in every context. There is no common everyday single-word synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“磷酸基团 + 加上去 + 过程”：给分子接上一个磷酸基团。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think phosphate group + attach + process: a molecule gains a phosphate group.

etymology_story.zh: draughtsman 由 draught 与 man 组成；draught 属于与 draw（拉、画）相关的本土词族，历史上可指绘出的图样或起草的文本。这些含义分别发展出技术制图者、擅长绘画的人和法律文本起草人的用法。
etymology_story.en: Draughtsman combines draught with man; draught belongs to the native word family associated with draw and historically referred to a drawing or a drafted text. These meanings underlie its uses for a technical drawing professional, a skilled artist, and a drafter of legal documents.

morphology_enriched.zh: draught（图样；草稿）+ 连接成分 -s- + man（人）→ draughtsman。复数为 draughtsmen；draughtsman + -ship → draughtsmanship（制图或素描技艺）。相关复合词有 draughtswoman（女性制图员或绘画者）、draughtswomen（其复数）、draughtsperson（不标明性别的制图员）和 draughtspeople（其复数）。美式对应形式通常为 draftsman、draftsmen 和 draftsmanship。
morphology_enriched.en: Draught, a drawing or draft, + linking -s- + man → draughtsman. Its plural is draughtsmen; draughtsman + -ship → draughtsmanship, skill in technical or artistic drawing. Related compounds include draughtswoman and its plural draughtswomen, and gender-neutral draughtsperson and its plural draughtspeople. The usual American counterparts are draftsman, draftsmen, and draftsmanship.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: drafter（制图员；起草人）是常见的性别中性表达，也可用于技术和法律语境；illustrator（插画家）侧重为书刊等制作说明性图画；designer（设计师）侧重构思形式、功能或结构，职责通常超出准确绘图。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Drafter is a common gender-neutral alternative in technical and legal contexts; illustrator emphasizes pictures made to explain or accompany material; designer emphasizes devising form, function, or structure, with responsibilities extending beyond accurate drawing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 draw 抓住“画出、拟出”：画图样的人，也可以是拟法律文本的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with draw: a person who draws up a picture, a plan, or a legal text.

etymology_story.zh: 英语从南非荷兰语借入 springbok，其组成部分对应荷兰语 springen（跳）和 bok（公山羊；用于一些羚羊名称）。这个名称描写了跳羚醒目的跃起动作；动物名称后来也成为南非体育代表身份的称号，尤其用于国家橄榄球队。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed springbok from South African Dutch, combining elements corresponding to Dutch springen, to jump, and bok, a male goat or an element in antelope names. The name describes the animal's conspicuous leaps and later became a designation for South African sporting representatives, especially the national rugby union team.

morphology_enriched.zh: 源语言中的 spring（跳）+ bok（公山羊；羚羊名称成分）→ springbok；在现代英语中通常作为完整借词使用，其中 bok 不是普通英语中自由使用的“羚羊”词根。动物义复数可用 springbok 或 springboks；球队及队员义通常写作 Springbok、Springboks。无常用标准派生词；springbokkie 是相关的南非语指小形式，也用于一种分层小杯酒的名称。
morphology_enriched.en: In the source language, spring, jump, + bok, a male goat or an element in antelope names, → springbok. Modern English generally treats it as a complete loanword; bok is not an ordinary productive English base meaning antelope. The animal plural is springbok or springboks; the sporting forms are normally capitalized Springbok and Springboks. There are no common standard derivatives; the related Afrikaans diminutive springbokkie is also used for a layered alcoholic shot.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: antelope（羚羊）是包含跳羚在内的上位名称，不能精确替换物种名；gazelle（瞪羚）指外形和习性相近的一类羚羊，但与跳羚并非同一物种。体育义中 South African rugby international（南非橄榄球国脚）可作解释性近义表达。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Antelope is a broader category that includes the springbok, rather than an exact species synonym; gazelle names similar antelopes but is not the same species. In the sporting sense, South African rugby international is an explanatory near-equivalent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: spring 抓住“弹跳”：一只像弹簧一样跃起的羚羊；大写时联想到南非橄榄球队。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let spring suggest a bouncing leap: an antelope that springs into the air; with a capital letter, connect it with South African rugby.

etymology.text: 由古法语 lancete（小矛，lance 的指小形式）经中古英语 launcet 传入；想象尖头小矛，就能记住这件细小器械。

senses.meaning_zh: 采血针；柳叶刀
senses.meaning_en: a small pointed instrument for puncturing skin or making small incisions
senses.english_definition: A lancet is a small, sharp medical instrument used to prick the skin or make a small cut.
senses.collocation_en: a sterile lancet; a blood lancet
senses.collocation_zh: 无菌采血针；采血针
senses.sentence_en: The nurse used a sterile lancet to collect a drop of blood.

senses.meaning_zh: 尖拱窄窗；柳叶形尖拱
senses.meaning_en: a tall, narrow window with a pointed top, or its pointed arch
senses.english_definition: In architecture, a lancet is a narrow window with a sharply pointed top, or an arch of that shape.
senses.collocation_en: a lancet window; a lancet arch
senses.collocation_zh: 尖拱窄窗；柳叶形尖拱
senses.sentence_en: Three lancet windows lit the small chapel.
senses.sentence_zh: 三扇尖拱窄窗为这座小礼拜堂提供了采光。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语借自古法语 lancete，即 lance（矛）的指小形式，原有“小矛”之意。细小尖刀因形似矛尖而得名，建筑中的尖拱窄窗也因相似的尖长轮廓而沿用这一名称。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English from Old French lancete, a diminutive of lance meaning a small spear. Its pointed shape explains both the name of the medical instrument and the later architectural use for a narrow, pointed window.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 lancet 作为完整词干记忆；历史上可分析为 lance（矛）＋指小成分 -et，但它不是现代英语中按常规删去 e 后构成的新词。常用形式与组合：lancets（复数）、lancet-shaped（柳叶刀形的）、lancet window（尖拱窄窗）、lancet arch（柳叶形尖拱）。相关词包括 lance（矛）、lancer（长矛骑兵）、lanceolate（披针形的），它们并非都直接由 lancet 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, lancet is normally treated as a whole stem. Historically, it contains lance plus the diminutive element -et; it is not a new English formation produced by a regular rule deleting e. Common forms and combinations include lancets, lancet-shaped, lancet window, and lancet arch. Related words include lance, lancer, and lanceolate, although these are not all direct derivatives of lancet.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: scalpel（手术刀）主要用于切开或解剖，lancet 通常更小，常用于刺破皮肤；needle（针）是更宽泛的尖细器具名称，也可指注射针；lancet window（尖拱窄窗）比 pointed window（尖顶窗）更强调狭长的建筑形制。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A scalpel is primarily a cutting or dissecting instrument, while a lancet is usually smaller and often used to puncture skin. Needle is a broader term for a slender pointed instrument and can refer to an injection needle. In architecture, lancet window is more specific than pointed window because it emphasizes a tall, narrow shape.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 小矛尖：缩小成采血刀，拉长成尖拱窗。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a little spear: its point becomes a skin-pricking blade, and its outline becomes a narrow pointed window.

etymology_story.zh: 表示“堆、拥挤的一群”的 ruck 一般被认为来自斯堪的纳维亚语言中表示“堆”的词，后来扩展出“普通的一群”和体育争球义。表示“褶皱”的 ruck 通常另列词源，也可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语言中表示皱褶的词，不能把两支词源确定地合并。
etymology_story.en: The ruck meaning a heap or crowded group is generally traced to Scandinavian words for a heap, and later developed senses referring to the ordinary majority and sporting contests. The fold or wrinkle meaning is usually treated as a separate etymological entry, also possibly Scandinavian, so the two histories should not be confidently merged.

morphology_enriched.zh: ruck 是现代英语中的完整词根；名词与动词可同形转换。屈折形式：rucks（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、rucked（过去式及过去分词）、rucking（现在分词及动名词）；常见短语：ruck up（皱起）。澳式足球词族包括 ruckman（争高球球员，复数 ruckmen）和 ruckwork（争高球方面的表现或技术）。
morphology_enriched.en: Ruck is a whole modern English root, with noun and verb uses related by conversion. Inflected forms are rucks, rucked, and rucking; ruck up is a common phrasal form for gathering into folds. The Australian football family includes ruckman, plural ruckmen, and ruckwork.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: crowd（人群）较中性，ruck 更强调拥挤、混杂，或带有“平庸大众”的贬义；scrum（拉格比中的司克兰争球）是有组织的重新开球形式，与围绕地面球形成的 ruck 不同；crease（折痕）常指较清晰的折线，ruck 更强调材料堆起的皱褶。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Crowd is relatively neutral, while ruck emphasizes crowding or disorder and can disparage an undistinguished majority. A scrum is a structured rugby restart, whereas a ruck forms over a ball on the ground. A crease is often a distinct fold line, while a ruck emphasizes material gathered into a raised fold.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 画面记忆：人挤成一团，布堆成一褶；两幅图可联想，词源不必强合。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture people bunching together and cloth bunching into a fold; connect the images without assuming a single historical root.

meaning: 化生（一种成熟细胞或组织被另一种类型取代）

morphology.text: meta-（改变） + -plasia（组织形成） → metaplasia（组织类型发生改变，即化生）。

etymology.text: 近代医学借用希腊语构词成分 meta-（改变）与表示形成的 -plasia 造词；记成组织“换了一种成熟类型”。

relations.meaning: 细胞数量增多所致的增生

usage_note: 医学术语。化生强调类型替换，不能直接等同癌症，也不同于单纯细胞数量增加。

question: 这个句子中，metaplasia 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 化生：一种成熟细胞类型被另一种成熟细胞类型取代
senses.meaning_en: replacement of one mature cell type by another mature cell type
senses.english_definition: Metaplasia is a change in which one mature type of cell in a tissue is replaced by another mature type.
senses.collocation_en: intestinal metaplasia; squamous metaplasia
senses.collocation_zh: 肠上皮化生；鳞状上皮化生
senses.sentence_en: The biopsy showed intestinal metaplasia in the stomach lining.
senses.sentence_zh: 活检显示胃黏膜存在肠上皮化生。

etymology_story.zh: 这是近代医学利用希腊语构词成分创造的术语：meta- 在这里表示“改变”，-plasia 与“形成、塑造”有关。其医学含义逐渐固定为组织中一种成熟细胞类型被另一种成熟细胞类型取代。
etymology_story.en: This modern medical term was formed from Greek elements: meta- here expresses change, and -plasia refers to formation or molding. Its medical meaning became established as the replacement of one mature cell type by another within a tissue.

morphology_enriched.zh: meta-（改变）＋-plasia（形成、发育）→ metaplasia（化生）。核心词族：metaplastic（化生的），少见副词 metaplastically（以化生方式）；metaplasias 可用于表示多种或多处化生，但通常使用不可数形式。hyperplasia（增生）、dysplasia（异型增生；发育异常）和 neoplasia（肿瘤形成）共享 -plasia，并非 metaplasia 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Meta- meaning change plus -plasia meaning formation or development gives metaplasia. The core family includes metaplastic and the uncommon adverb metaplastically. The plural metaplasias can refer to multiple forms or instances, although the noun is normally uncountable. Hyperplasia, dysplasia, and neoplasia share -plasia but are not direct derivatives of metaplasia.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有在所有医学语境中都能替换 metaplasia 的常用单词近义词。cell-type replacement（细胞类型替换）是解释性近义表达；transdifferentiation（转分化）强调分化细胞身份的转变，不能一概等同于组织层面的化生；dysplasia（异型增生）强调细胞形态和排列异常，是相关但不同的概念。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common single-word synonym that replaces metaplasia in every medical context. Cell-type replacement is an explanatory near-equivalent. Transdifferentiation emphasizes a change in differentiated cell identity and is not universally interchangeable with tissue-level metaplasia. Dysplasia concerns abnormal cellular appearance and organization and is a related but distinct concept.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: meta- 改变＋-plasia 形成：组织换了一种成熟细胞类型。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Change plus formation: a tissue acquires a different mature cell type.

question: 这个句子中，limerick 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 五行打油诗，通常采用 AABBA 韵式
senses.meaning_en: a humorous five-line poem, usually with an AABBA rhyme scheme
senses.english_definition: A limerick is a short, usually funny poem with five lines, in which the first, second, and fifth lines rhyme and the third and fourth lines rhyme.
senses.collocation_en: write a limerick; a bawdy limerick
senses.collocation_zh: 写五行打油诗；带有荤笑话的五行打油诗
senses.sentence_en: She wrote a limerick about a cat that refused to get wet.
senses.sentence_zh: 她写了一首五行打油诗，讲的是一只不肯沾水的猫。

etymology_story.zh: 这个诗体名称通常被认为与爱尔兰地名 Limerick 有关，但具体命名经过并不确定。一种常见解释将它与含有这一地名的歌唱副歌联系起来，不能据此断言这种诗体起源于该城。
etymology_story.en: The name is generally associated with Limerick in Ireland, although the precise naming history is uncertain. A common explanation connects it with a sung refrain containing the place name, but this does not establish that the verse form originated in the city.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 limerick 是不可再作实用词缀拆分的完整词干，不能分析为 lime＋rick。常用屈折形式为 limericks（复数）；limerick writer（五行打油诗作者）是自然的组合表达，limerickist（五行打油诗作者）是较少见的派生词。地名 Limerick 首字母大写，诗体名 limerick 通常小写。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, limerick is a whole stem without a useful productive affix breakdown; it is not lime plus rick. The normal plural is limericks. Limerick writer is a natural compound expression, while limerickist is a less common derivative. The place name Limerick is capitalized, whereas the verse-form noun limerick is normally lowercase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: comic verse（诙谐诗）是范围更大的类别，不限行数或韵式；nonsense verse（荒诞诗）强调荒诞内容，未必是五行；doggerel（拙劣打油诗）通常含有格律粗糙、艺术性低的贬义，而 limerick 可以写得十分精巧。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Comic verse is a broader category with no fixed line count or rhyme scheme. Nonsense verse emphasizes absurd content and need not have five lines. Doggerel usually disparages clumsy or artistically poor verse, whereas a limerick can be skillfully crafted.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 五行小笑话：一、二、五押同韵，三、四另押韵。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A five-line joke in verse: lines one, two, and five rhyme; three and four form another pair.

senses.meaning_zh: 上清液：沉淀或沉降物上方的多份液体
senses.meaning_en: liquids remaining above settled or separated solid material
senses.english_definition: Supernatants are the liquids above material that has settled or been separated out, for example by centrifugation.
senses.collocation_en: collect the supernatants; cell culture supernatants
senses.collocation_zh: 收集上清液；细胞培养上清液
senses.sentence_en: The supernatants from the three tubes were transferred to clean containers.
senses.sentence_zh: 三个试管中的上清液被转移到了干净的容器中。

etymology_story.zh: 单数 supernatant 的历史来源可追溯到拉丁语 supernatant-，与表示“浮在上面”的 supernatare 有关，其中 super- 表示“在上”，natare 表示“游动、漂浮”。英语先有“浮在上面的”这一形容词用法，后来把该词用作名词，指沉降物上方的液体；supernatants 是其复数。
etymology_story.en: The singular supernatant ultimately comes from Latin supernatant-, associated with supernatare, meaning to float above, from super- meaning above and natare meaning to swim or float. English used the adjective for something floating above and later the noun for liquid above settled material; supernatants is its plural.

morphology_enriched.zh: super-（在上）＋natant（漂浮的）构成 supernatant，再加名词复数后缀 -s → supernatants。natant 的历史基础是拉丁语 natare（游动、漂浮）。核心词族为 supernatant（上清液；浮在上面的）和 supernatants（上清液的复数）；supernate 是实验室英语中较少见的相关形式。输入词 supernatants 仅是复数名词，形容词形式仍为 supernatant，不加 -s。
morphology_enriched.en: Super- meaning above plus natant meaning floating forms supernatant; adding the noun plural suffix -s gives supernatants. Natant ultimately relates to Latin natare, meaning to swim or float. The core family is supernatant, used as both noun and adjective, and the plural noun supernatants; supernate is a less common related laboratory form. The input supernatants is only a plural noun: the adjective remains supernatant without -s.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: supernatant liquids（上清液）是明确展开的同义表达；supernates（上清液）是较少见的实验室同义形式；filtrates（滤液）指通过过滤介质得到的液体，命名依据是过滤过程，不能与沉降物上方的 supernatants 随意互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Supernatant liquids is an explicit equivalent. Supernates is a less common laboratory synonym. Filtrates are liquids that have passed through a filter, so the term identifies a filtration process and is not freely interchangeable with supernatants above settled material.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: super 在上，natant 浮着，-s 多份：沉淀上方的一份份液体。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Super means above, natant suggests floating, and -s means more than one: liquids above the sediment.

senses.meaning_en: a member or supporter of the Spanish Falange, usually spelled Falangist
senses.english_definition: In writing about Spain, a Phalangist is a member or supporter of the Falange, a fascist political movement; the usual spelling is Falangist.
senses.collocation_en: Spanish Phalangists; a Phalangist militant
senses.collocation_zh: 西班牙长枪党成员；长枪党激进分子
senses.sentence_en: In this account of the Spanish Civil War, the author uses Phalangist as a variant of Falangist.
senses.sentence_zh: 在这部关于西班牙内战的著作中，作者将 Phalangist 用作 Falangist 的异体拼写。

senses.meaning_zh: 黎巴嫩长枪党的；西班牙长枪党的
senses.meaning_en: relating to the Lebanese Phalange or, less usually under this spelling, the Spanish Falange
senses.english_definition: Phalangist organizations, policies, or activities are connected with the Lebanese Phalange or, in some historical writing, the Spanish Falange.
senses.collocation_en: Phalangist forces; the Phalangist movement
senses.collocation_zh: 长枪党武装；长枪党运动
senses.sentence_en: The chapter examines Phalangist political activity in Lebanon.
senses.sentence_zh: 这一章考察了黎巴嫩长枪党的政治活动。

etymology_story.zh: Phalangist 与法语 phalangiste、Phalange 有关，最终可追溯到希腊语 phalanx（密集战斗方阵）；组织名称借用了团结列阵的意象。西班牙的相关形式是 Falange 和 Falangist，实际使用时须区分西班牙与黎巴嫩的组织。
etymology_story.en: Phalangist is associated with French phalangiste and Phalange, ultimately from Greek phalanx, a close military formation; the political name evokes people standing together in ranks. The corresponding Spanish forms are Falange and Falangist, so the Lebanese and Spanish organizations must be distinguished by context.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Phalang(e)（长枪党名称词干）+ -ist（成员、支持者；也构成关系形容词）→ Phalangist。词族：Phalange（黎巴嫩长枪党）、Phalangist（成员；该党的）、Phalangists（成员复数）、Phalangism（相关政治思想，较少见）；西班牙语背景的对应形式为 Falange、Falangist、Falangism。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: Phalang(e), the party-name stem, + -ist, marking membership or support and also forming a relational adjective, → Phalangist. The family includes Phalange, Phalangist, plural Phalangists, and the less common Phalangism; corresponding forms associated with Spain include Falange, Falangist, and Falangism.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Kataeb member（黎巴嫩卡塔伊卜党成员）明确指黎巴嫩长枪党成员；Falangist（西班牙长枪党成员）通常指西班牙组织，不能在未说明背景时与黎巴嫩义互换；supporter of the Phalange（长枪党支持者）可包括并未正式入党的支持者。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Kataeb member explicitly identifies membership in the Lebanese party; Falangist normally points to the Spanish organization and is not freely interchangeable with the Lebanese sense; supporter of the Phalange can include someone who is not a formal party member.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 方阵 phalanx → 以方阵命名的政党 → -ist 党派成员；国家背景决定具体所指。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Phalanx → a party named after a formation → -ist, a party member; the country supplies the reference.

meaning: 使年老或体弱者退休并领取养老金

pronunciation.note: 重音和长音按所列 IPA 读取。

forms: 三单 superannuates；过去式及过去分词 superannuated；现在分词 superannuating。
family: superannuation 退休金制度；superannuated 年老退休的，也可指过时的。

morphology.text: super-（超过） + annu-（年） + -ate（动词成分） → superannuate（使因年老等退休）；这是历史成分提示。

etymology.text: 英语从 superannuated 逆构出动词，背后是拉丁语 super（超过）和 annus（年）；从“过了工作年限”联想到退休。

usage_note: 较正式，常见于旧式或制度性表述；本课教“给养老金使退休”，不考另一种“使过时”义。

senses.meaning_zh: 使因年老或健康原因退休并领取养老金
senses.meaning_en: to retire someone with a pension because of age or ill health
senses.english_definition: If an employer superannuates someone, they arrange for that person to stop working and receive a pension because of their age or health.
senses.collocation_en: superannuate an employee; be superannuated on medical grounds
senses.collocation_zh: 安排雇员退休并领取养老金；因健康原因获准退休并领取养老金
senses.sentence_en: The employee was superannuated on medical grounds.
senses.sentence_zh: 这名雇员因健康原因获准退休并领取养老金。

senses.meaning_zh: 使过时；使因陈旧而被淘汰
senses.meaning_en: to make something obsolete or retire it from use
senses.english_definition: If a new development superannuates something, it makes that thing too old-fashioned or unsuitable to remain in use.
senses.collocation_en: superannuate old equipment; superannuate an existing system
senses.collocation_zh: 淘汰旧设备；使现有系统过时
senses.sentence_en: The new technology threatened to superannuate the entire system.
senses.sentence_zh: 这项新技术可能使整个系统遭到淘汰。

etymology_story.zh: superannuate 通常被解释为从更早的 superannuated 逆构而来，历史上与中世纪拉丁语 superannuatus 有关，其中 super 表示“超过”，annus 表示“年”。“超过适用年限”的概念发展出年老退休以及事物陈旧过时的含义。
etymology_story.en: Superannuate is generally explained as a back-formation from the earlier superannuated, historically related to Medieval Latin superannuatus, containing super, meaning beyond, and annus, meaning year. The idea of being beyond one's useful years developed into retirement through age and, by extension, obsolescence.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史成分提示：super-（超过）+ annu-（年）+ -ate（动词形式）；annu- 是历史词根，不是现代独立英语词。常用词族与屈折形式：superannuates、superannuating、superannuated（过去式、过去分词；也作形容词，意为退休的或过时的）、superannuation（退休金制度；退休金）。原形动词属于正式且低频用语。
morphology_enriched.en: Historical components: super- meaning beyond + annu- meaning year + the verbal ending -ate; annu- is a historical root rather than an independent modern English word. The main family and inflections are superannuates, superannuating, superannuated, also an adjective meaning retired or obsolete, and superannuation, referring to pension provision or benefits. The base verb is formal and uncommon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: retire（使退休；使退役）适用范围最广，本身不保证领取养老金；pension off（让某人领养老金退休）明确包含养老金安排，语气较口语化；render obsolete（使过时）对应事物被技术或时代淘汰的引申义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Retire is the broadest term and does not itself guarantee a pension; pension off explicitly includes pension arrangements and is more conversational; render obsolete matches the extended sense of making equipment or practices outdated.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: super 超过 + annu 年：超过工作年限，人退休，物淘汰。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Beyond the useful years: people retire, and things become obsolete.

meaning: 主席团；代行较大机构职权的常务委员会

pronunciation.note: 重音和长音按所列 IPA 读取。

forms: 复数 presidiums 或 presidia；另有拼写 praesidium。
family: preside 主持（历史词源相关）；presidia 主席团（另一复数形式）。

morphology.text: presidium 整词作为独立词素记忆；presidium + -like → presidium-like（类似主席团的）；-like 可用于表达组织形式相似，这里是可生成的教学派生示例。

etymology.text: 经俄语 prezidium 进入英语，源头是拉丁语 praesidium；相关动词 praesidere 有主持、监管之意，可联想负责主持事务的一小组人。

usage_note: 常见于社会主义国家或某些组织的机构名称。特定机构正式名称常写 Presidium，泛指时小写。

question: 这个句子中，presidium 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 主席团；代表较大机构行使职权的常设领导委员会
senses.meaning_en: a presiding or standing executive committee of a larger organization
senses.english_definition: A presidium is a small group of people who chair an assembly or carry out leadership duties on behalf of a larger political or other organization.
senses.collocation_en: elect a presidium; a member of the presidium
senses.collocation_zh: 选举主席团；主席团成员
senses.sentence_en: The congress elected a presidium to conduct its proceedings.
senses.sentence_zh: 大会选举了一个主席团来主持会议。

etymology_story.zh: presidium 与德语 Präsidium、俄语 prezidium 等欧洲语言形式有关，最终源于拉丁语 praesidium，原有“保护、守卫、驻防力量”等含义。这个词后来用于主持会议或代表较大政治机构行使领导职权的小组，在苏联及相关政治语境中尤其常见。
etymology_story.en: Presidium is related to European forms such as German Präsidium and Russian prezidium and ultimately derives from Latin praesidium, meaning protection, a guard, or a garrison. It came to denote a body that presides over proceedings or exercises leadership for a larger political institution, especially in Soviet and related contexts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜把 presidium 作为整体借词学习，不宜机械拆成可自由组合的英语词根与后缀。复数为 presidiums 或 presidia；没有常用的直接派生词。preside（主持）、president（主席；总统）、presidency（主席或总统职位、任期）可作相关词汇联系，但不是由 presidium 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, presidium is best learned as a whole borrowed word rather than split into productive English roots and suffixes. Its plurals are presidiums and presidia, and it has no common direct derivatives. Preside, president, and presidency provide related vocabulary connections but are not direct derivatives of presidium.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: executive committee（执行委员会）强调日常执行和决策职责；bureau（领导局；常务机构）可指某些政治组织的领导机关，但也有办事处等其他含义；steering committee（指导委员会）强调方向协调与监督，不一定拥有正式常设领导权。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Executive committee emphasizes ongoing executive and decision-making duties; bureau can name a political organization's leadership body but also has unrelated administrative meanings; steering committee emphasizes direction and coordination and need not hold formal standing authority.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 presidium 与 preside“主持”联系：坐在主席台、代表大会主持事务的一组人；这是联想，不是现代构词拆分。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect presidium with preside: the group at the head of an assembly conducting its business. This is a memory association, not a modern morphological breakdown.

meaning: 面向高收入消费者的；高档的

pronunciation.note: 重音和长音按所列 IPA 读取。

forms: 常用 more upmarket、most upmarket；也可作副词，如 move upmarket。
family: market 市场；downmarket 面向低价市场的。

morphology.text: up-（向上） + market（市场） → upmarket（面向较高消费档次的）。

etymology.text: 英语用 up 和 market 组合，借市场价格与消费层级的“向上”表达高档定位。

usage_note: 英式常用。描述餐厅、商店、产品等的市场定位，不等于质量在所有方面都更好。

question: 这个句子中，upmarket 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 高档的；面向高收入消费者的
senses.meaning_en: relatively expensive and intended for customers seeking higher quality or status
senses.english_definition: An upmarket product, shop, or service is relatively expensive and is intended for people who want higher quality or a more exclusive image.
senses.collocation_en: an upmarket restaurant; an upmarket brand
senses.collocation_zh: 高档餐厅；高端品牌
senses.sentence_en: They opened an upmarket restaurant near the station.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们在车站附近开了一家高档餐厅。

senses.meaning_zh: 向高端市场；朝更高档次
senses.meaning_en: towards a more expensive or exclusive part of the market
senses.english_definition: If a business moves upmarket, it starts offering more expensive or exclusive products or services to attract customers willing to pay more.
senses.collocation_en: move upmarket; go upmarket
senses.collocation_zh: 向高端市场转型；提升市场定位
senses.sentence_en: The company is moving upmarket with a new range of premium products.
senses.sentence_zh: 这家公司正通过推出一系列高端产品向高端市场转型。

etymology_story.zh: upmarket 由 up（向上）和 market（市场）组合而成，用空间上的“向上”比喻价格、品质或消费定位的提高。它既可形容高档商品与服务，也可表示企业朝高端市场发展的方向。
etymology_story.en: Upmarket combines up with market, using upward movement as a metaphor for higher prices, quality, or market positioning. It can describe expensive goods and services or indicate a business's movement towards a higher-priced market segment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：up（向上）+ market（市场）→ upmarket，可作形容词和副词，两种词性读音相同。相关构词：downmarket（低档的；向低端市场）、mid-market（中端市场的）；美式近义对应词为 upscale。没有必须掌握的常用直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: up + market → upmarket, used as both an adjective and an adverb with the same pronunciation. Related formations include downmarket and mid-market; upscale is a common American English equivalent. There are no essential common direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: upscale（高档的；向高端）是常见美式对应词；high-end（高端的）强调产品或服务处于市场较高档次；luxury（奢华的；奢侈品的）强调昂贵、享受或排他性，程度通常比 upmarket 更强。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Upscale is a common American English equivalent; high-end emphasizes a product's or service's position near the top of a market; luxury stresses costly comfort, indulgence, or exclusivity and is usually stronger than upmarket.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 市场有档次阶梯：up + market，就是往更高、更贵的档次走。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a market ladder: upmarket means higher on the price and positioning ladder.

pronunciation.note: 重音和长音按所列 IPA 读取。

forms: 复数 introns。
family: intronic 内含子的；exon 外显子。

morphology.text: intra-（内部，缩为 intr-） + -on（科学名称成分） → intron（基因内部的内含子）。

etymology.text: 20世纪遗传学中的新造词，名称与 intragenic region（基因内部区域）相连；记住它在基因内部，转录后常从 RNA 中剪去。

relations.meaning: 剪接后保留在成熟RNA中的外显子

usage_note: 遗传学术语。内含子会被转录，但在常见的 RNA 剪接过程中被移除，不能误解为“根本不会被转录”。

question: 这个句子中，intron 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 内含子；转录后通常在RNA剪接过程中被去除的基因内部序列
senses.meaning_en: An intervening sequence within a gene that is usually removed from its RNA transcript during splicing.
senses.english_definition: An intron is a section of a gene that is copied into RNA but is usually removed when that RNA is processed.
senses.collocation_en: intron removal; intron retention
senses.collocation_zh: 内含子去除；内含子保留
senses.sentence_en: The intron is removed from the RNA before the mature messenger RNA is translated.
senses.sentence_zh: 在成熟的信使RNA被翻译之前，这段内含子会从RNA中被去除。

etymology_story.zh: 遗传学家沃尔特·吉尔伯特于1978年提出 intron 一词，以 intragenic region（基因内部区域）为命名依据，并与 exon（外显子）相对应。它指基因中位于外显子之间、通常在RNA加工时被剪除的序列。
etymology_story.en: Geneticist Walter Gilbert introduced intron in 1978, basing the name on intragenic region and contrasting it with exon. It denotes a sequence between exons that is usually removed during RNA processing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 intron 为完整词基，不宜把它当作规则形成的 intra- + -on。常见词族及相关构词：intron + -ic → intronic（内含子的）；intron + -less → intronless（无内含子的）；intron-containing（含内含子的）；intronization（内含子化，即原有外显子序列转变为内含子）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, intron functions as a complete base rather than a regularly formed intra- + -on combination. Its family and related formations include intron + -ic → intronic, intron + -less → intronless, intron-containing, and intronization, the conversion of an exonic sequence into an intron.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: intervening sequence（间隔序列）和 noncoding intervening sequence（非编码间隔序列）可在适当的基因及RNA剪接语境中解释 intron；前者范围更宽，后者突出通常不参与蛋白质编码的特点，但并非所有非编码序列都是内含子。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Intervening sequence and noncoding intervening sequence can describe an intron in an appropriate gene or RNA-splicing context. The former is broader, while the latter emphasizes its usual exclusion from protein-coding sequence; neither means that all noncoding sequences are introns.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 基因内部的插入段：先被转录，通常再被剪去。
mnemonic_anchor.en: An inside segment: copied into RNA first, usually spliced out later.

senses.meaning_zh: 特技飞行的；涉及飞机翻滚、筋斗等高难度动作的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to skilled aircraft maneuvers such as rolls and loops.

senses.collocation_en: an aerobatic display; an aerobatic team

etymology_story.zh: aerobatic 形成于20世纪初，将表示“空气、航空”的 aero- 与 acrobatic（杂技的）融合，把杂技动作的概念转用于飞行。两个来源最终都涉及希腊语构词材料。
etymology_story.en: Aerobatic arose in the early twentieth century by blending aero-, meaning air or aviation, with acrobatic, transferring the idea of acrobatics to flight. Both elements ultimately draw on Greek word-forming material.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：aero-（航空）+ acrobatic（杂技的，通过重叠缩合）→ aerobatic。词族：aerobatics（特技飞行，通常按单数概念使用）；aerobatically（以特技飞行方式）；aerobat（特技飞行员，较少见）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: aero- meaning aviation + acrobatic, combined through blending → aerobatic. The family includes aerobatics, normally treated as a singular activity; aerobatically, meaning in an aerobatic manner; and the less common aerobat, an aerobatic pilot.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: acrobatic（杂技般的）适用范围更广，可形容人体或其他灵活动作；stunt（作定语时表示“特技表演的”）强调惊险或表演效果；aerobatic 专指航空中的特技机动，也用于规范的训练与竞赛。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Acrobatic is broader and can describe agile bodily or other movements. Attributive stunt emphasizes daring or spectacle, whereas aerobatic specifically concerns aircraft maneuvers, including formal training and competition.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: aero（航空）接上 acrobatic（杂技）：把杂技搬到空中。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Aero meets acrobatic: acrobatics performed in the air.

senses.meaning_zh: 产前的；妊娠期间的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to pregnancy and the period before childbirth.
senses.english_definition: Antenatal care, tests, or classes are provided during pregnancy before a baby is born.
senses.collocation_en: antenatal care; antenatal classes

etymology_story.zh: antenatal 由表示“在……之前”的 ante- 和表示“出生的”的 natal 组成，最终分别源于拉丁语 ante 和 natalis。它在医学中用于指分娩之前的妊娠阶段及相关护理，尤常见于英式英语。
etymology_story.en: Antenatal combines ante-, meaning before, with natal, meaning relating to birth, ultimately from Latin ante and natalis. In medicine, it describes the period of pregnancy before childbirth and associated care, especially in British English.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：ante-（在前）+ natal（出生的）→ antenatal（产前的）；antenatal + -ly → antenatally（在产前）。以 natal 为共同词基的相关词包括 prenatal（产前的）、postnatal（产后的）、perinatal（围产期的）和 neonatal（新生儿的）；这些是同词基词，并非都由 antenatal 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: ante- meaning before + natal meaning relating to birth → antenatal; antenatal + -ly → antenatally. Related formations sharing natal include prenatal, postnatal, perinatal, and neonatal; these share its base rather than all deriving from antenatal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: prenatal（产前的）与 antenatal 基本同义，在美式英语中更常见；antepartum（分娩前的）更偏临床术语，常用来区分分娩前与分娩中、分娩后的阶段。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Prenatal is essentially synonymous and is more usual in American English. Antepartum is more clinical and often distinguishes the period before labor or delivery from the periods during and after it.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ante＝之前，natal＝出生：出生之前，就是产前。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ante means before; natal means birth: before birth.

etymology_story.en: Gorse is a native English plant name inherited through Middle English from Old English gors and gorst. It has continued to name the prickly shrub rather than developing from a combination of modern English words.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 gorse 是不可再作常用构词分析的单纯词，通常作不可数名词。主要派生词为 gorsy，也拼作 gorsey（长满荆豆的）；常见复合表达有 gorse-covered（长满荆豆的）、gorse bush（荆豆灌木）和 gorse heath（荆豆荒原）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gorse is a simple word without a productive internal breakdown and is usually a mass noun. Its main derivative is gorsy, also spelled gorsey, meaning covered with gorse; common combinations include gorse-covered, gorse bush, and gorse heath.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Furze and whin are traditional alternative names for gorse. Gorse is the general name, furze often occurs in traditional or regional usage, and whin is particularly associated with Scotland and northern England.

etymology_story.zh: daemon 经拉丁语 daemon 源于希腊语 daimōn，原指神灵或神秘力量，并不必然带有邪恶含义。20世纪60年代的计算机用法借鉴了“麦克斯韦妖”的意象，把在幕后持续执行任务的程序称为 daemon。
etymology_story.en: Daemon comes through Latin daemon from Greek daimōn, a spirit or divine power that was not necessarily evil. Its computing use arose in the 1960s with reference to Maxwell's demon, applying the image of a continuously working hidden agent to a background program.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 daemon 是完整借入词，不作常用词根与词缀拆分。计算机词族包括 daemon + -ize → daemonize（使程序成为守护进程；以守护进程方式运行）、daemonization（守护进程化）和 daemonized（已转为守护进程的）；英式拼写也可用 daemonise、daemonisation。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, daemon is a complete borrowed base without a productive internal breakdown. Its computing family includes daemon + -ize → daemonize, meaning to make or become a daemon; daemonization; and daemonized. British spellings also include daemonise and daemonisation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 计算机义：background process（后台进程）范围更广，并非每个后台进程都提供长期服务；service（服务）强调提供的功能及其管理方式。神灵义：spirit（灵体、神灵）范围较广，而 daemon 带有古典文化或守护、引导力量的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: In computing, background process is broader, since not every background process provides a continuing service; service emphasizes the function supplied and how it is managed. In the supernatural sense, spirit is broader, while daemon suggests classical tradition or a guiding power.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 幕后小助手：神灵暗中引导，程序后台服务。
mnemonic_anchor.en: An unseen helper: a spirit guides behind the scenes, and a program serves in the background.

question: 这个句子中，Comintern 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 共产国际；第三国际（1919—1943年）
senses.meaning_en: the Communist International, an international organization of communist parties active from 1919 to 1943
senses.english_definition: The Comintern was an international organization established in 1919 to bring communist parties together and promote communist revolution.
senses.collocation_en: the Comintern Congress; Comintern policy
senses.collocation_zh: 共产国际代表大会；共产国际的政策
senses.sentence_en: The historian examined how Comintern policy influenced local communist parties.
senses.sentence_zh: 这位历史学家研究了共产国际的政策如何影响各地的共产党。

etymology_story.zh: Comintern 源于俄语 Коминтерн，是 Коммунистический Интернационал（共产国际）的缩合名称；英语形式也对应 Communist International 的截短组合。该简称后来固定指1919年至1943年间存在的这一组织。[词源参考](https://www.etymonline.com/word/Comintern)
etymology_story.en: Comintern comes from Russian Коминтерн, a contracted name for Коммунистический Интернационал, meaning Communist International; its English form also corresponds to shortened portions of Communist International. It became the established short name of the organization active from 1919 to 1943. [Etymology reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/Comintern)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代识记公式：Com(munist) + Intern(ational) → Comintern，属于截短拼合，不是普通的前缀加词根。相关构词有 anti- + Comintern → anti-Comintern（反共产国际的），如 Anti-Comintern Pact（《反共产国际协定》）；没有常用的屈折变化或丰富的派生词族。Cominform（共产党情报局）是另一个组织的名称，不是它的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern learning formula: Com(munist) + Intern(ational) → Comintern, a clipped blend rather than an ordinary prefix–root construction. A related formation is anti- + Comintern → anti-Comintern, as in the Anti-Comintern Pact; there are no usual inflected forms or extensive common derivatives. Cominform names a different organization and is not a derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Communist International（共产国际）是正式全称；Third International（第三国际）强调其在国际社会主义组织历史中的序列位置。两者均可指同一组织，而 communism（共产主义）指思想或制度，不能替换这个专名。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Communist International is the full name; Third International identifies the same organization by its historical position among socialist internationals. Communism names an ideology or system and cannot replace this organizational name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 Communist International 压缩成 Com + intern：跨国共产党的联合组织。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Compress Communist International into Com + intern: communist parties organized internationally.

etymology.text: 借自德语 Zeppelin，得名于飞艇设计者斐迪南·冯·齐柏林的姓氏；由人名变成他设计的硬式飞艇名称。
