question: 这个句子中，zeppelin 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 齐柏林式硬式飞艇
senses.meaning_en: a large rigid airship of the type developed by Ferdinand von Zeppelin
senses.english_definition: A zeppelin is a large airship whose shape is maintained by a rigid framework containing gas cells.
senses.collocation_en: a zeppelin raid; a zeppelin flight
senses.collocation_zh: 齐柏林飞艇空袭；齐柏林飞艇飞行
senses.sentence_en: The museum displayed a model of a zeppelin with its internal framework exposed.
senses.sentence_zh: 博物馆展出了一架内部骨架外露的齐柏林飞艇模型。

etymology_story.zh: zeppelin 得名于德国飞艇设计者斐迪南·冯·齐柏林，其姓氏成为所设计飞艇的名称。这个人名来源的词后来也用于泛指同类硬式飞艇，英语中首字母大小写均有使用。[词源参考](https://www.etymonline.com/word/zeppelin)
etymology_story.en: Zeppelin takes its name from the German airship designer Ferdinand von Zeppelin, whose surname became the name of his airships. The name subsequently extended to similar rigid airships, and both capitalized and lowercase forms occur in English. [Etymology reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/zeppelin)

morphology_enriched.zh: zeppelin 是不可再按现代英语词缀切分的专名来源名词，末尾 -in 不是这里的派生后缀。屈折形式：zeppelin + -s → zeppelins（复数）；可构成 zeppelin-like（像齐柏林飞艇的）。zep 是非正式截短形式；Zeppelinous（像齐柏林飞艇的、庞大的）有文献记录，但非常罕见。zeppelin raid 中的 zeppelin 是名词作定语，不因此另立常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Zeppelin is an eponymous noun without a productive modern English internal breakdown; its final -in is not a derivational suffix here. Its plural is zeppelin + -s → zeppelins, and zeppelin-like is a transparent compound adjective. Zep is an informal clipping; Zeppelinous, meaning resembling a zeppelin or very large, is attested but very rare. Zeppelin in zeppelin raid is an attributive noun rather than a separate common adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: airship（飞艇）是上位词，涵盖不同结构类型；dirigible（可操纵飞艇）强调能够控制航向；blimp（软式飞艇）没有刚性内部骨架，因此不能精确替换 zeppelin。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Airship is the general term covering different structural types; dirigible emphasizes that the craft can be steered. A blimp lacks a rigid internal framework and is therefore not an exact substitute for zeppelin.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 齐柏林先生的姓 → 有硬骨架的巨大飞艇。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Count Zeppelin’s name → a giant airship with a rigid skeleton.

meaning: 老的；旧时的（苏格兰用语）

pronunciation.note: 采用 Collins 所列苏格兰词读法 /ɔːld/。

forms: 相当于标准英语 old；地区变体不宜机械套用规则比较级。
family: auldness 年老、老迈（苏格兰语）；old 标准英语对应词；auld lang syne 往昔的日子。

morphology.text: auld 整词作为独立词素记忆；auld + -ness（状态） → auldness（年老、老迈，苏格兰语名词）。

etymology.text: 由古英语 ald 经北部中古英语传到苏格兰语和相关英语用法，与 old 同源；可从《友谊地久天长》的苏格兰语歌名联想“旧时光”。

usage_note: 苏格兰或北英格兰地区用语，普通标准英语通常写 old。用于地方人物对白可保留 auld；歌名写 Auld Lang Syne。

question: 这个句子中，auld 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 老的；旧的；往昔的（苏格兰语及相关地域用法）
senses.meaning_en: old, long-standing, or belonging to former times, in Scots and related regional usage
senses.english_definition: Auld means old in Scots and some regional varieties of English, and can describe people, things, or relationships.
senses.collocation_en: auld acquaintance; the Auld Alliance
senses.collocation_zh: 旧相识；苏法旧同盟
senses.sentence_en: He greeted his auld friend with a smile.
senses.sentence_zh: 他微笑着向老朋友打招呼。

etymology_story.zh: auld 与标准英语 old 同源，经北部中古英语承接古英语 ald 等形式，在苏格兰语中保留下来。它并非为了歌曲而创造的拼写，但因《Auld Lang Syne》（字面意为“往昔时光”）而广为人知。[词源参考](https://www.etymonline.com/word/auld)
etymology_story.en: Auld shares its ancestry with standard English old, continuing Old English forms such as ald through northern Middle English into Scots. It was not invented for a song, although Auld Lang Syne, literally referring to times long past, made it widely familiar. [Etymology reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/auld)

morphology_enriched.zh: auld 是单一词根，不能拆成 a- + uld。苏格兰语比较级为 auld + -er → aulder（更老的），最高级为 auld + -est → auldest（最老的）；派生名词 auld + -ness → auldness（年老；陈旧）属地域用语，现代通用英语中少见。相关复合词有 auld-fashioned（老式的）、auld-warld（古风的）和 auld-farrant（早熟老成的，亦拼 auld-farrand）。[苏格兰语词形参考](https://dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/aulder)；[auldness](https://www.dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/auldness)
morphology_enriched.en: Auld is a single root, not a- + uld. Scots inflections include auld + -er → aulder and auld + -est → auldest; auld + -ness → auldness is a regional noun meaning oldness or age and is uncommon in general modern English. Related compounds include auld-fashioned, meaning old-fashioned; auld-warld, meaning old-world; and auld-farrant, also auld-farrand, meaning precociously mature. [Scots inflection reference](https://dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/aulder); [auldness](https://www.dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/auldness)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: old（老的、旧的）是中性的通用对应词；aged（年迈的）主要突出人或生物的高龄；ancient（古老的）强调年代久远。auld 的主要特色是苏格兰或地域色彩，表达旧交情时也常带亲切、怀旧意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Old is the neutral general equivalent; aged chiefly emphasizes advanced age in a person or living thing; ancient stresses a very remote origin. Auld is distinguished mainly by its Scots or regional character and can convey affection or nostalgia when describing long-standing relationships.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: auld 就是带苏格兰口音与乡情的 old：老朋友、旧时光。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Auld is old with a Scots voice: old friends and remembered times.

senses.meaning_zh: 堵塞；塞满（通常用于 bung up，口语）
senses.meaning_en: to block an opening or passage, usually in the phrasal verb bung up
senses.english_definition: If something bungs up a pipe or other passage, it blocks it so that things cannot move through it normally.

senses.sentence_en: Grease had bunged up the kitchen drain.

senses.meaning_zh: 坏掉的；失灵的；受伤而不好使的（澳大利亚、新西兰口语）
senses.meaning_en: broken, faulty, or impaired by injury, in informal Australian and New Zealand English
senses.english_definition: If a machine or part of your body is bung, it is damaged or does not work properly.
senses.collocation_en: a bung knee; go bung

etymology_story.zh: 表示“塞子”的 bung 在中古英语中已有记录，来源未定，可能与中古荷兰语 bonge 或法语 bonde 有关；表示“随手放、扔”的动词另有拟声或表意来源的解释，贿款义与这种给付用法相关。[英语词源参考](https://www.etymonline.com/word/bung) 表示“坏掉的”的澳新形容词则来自雅加拉语中意为“死的”的 bang，经殖民时期接触语扩展为“失灵、损坏”。[澳大利亚国家词典中心参考](https://history.cass.anu.edu.au/centres/andc/meanings-origins/all)
etymology_story.en: Bung meaning a stopper is recorded in Middle English and has an uncertain origin, possibly involving Middle Dutch bonge or French bonde; the casual putting or throwing verb is also explained as a separate expressive formation, with the bribe sense associated with giving payments. [English etymology reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/bung) The Australian and New Zealand adjective has a separate origin in Yagara bang, meaning dead, which passed through colonial contact language and developed senses of failure or damage. [Australian National Dictionary Centre reference](https://history.cass.anu.edu.au/centres/andc/meanings-origins/all)

morphology_enriched.zh: bung 是单音节自由词根；“塞子”名词可零派生为“用塞子封住”的动词，但各同形词并非都出自同一历史词根。屈折形式为 bungs（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、bunged（过去式及过去分词）、bunging（现在分词）；复合词 bung + hole → bunghole（桶孔；另有粗俗义），前缀派生 un- + bung → unbung（拔去塞子，少见）。bung up 是短语动词，bunged-up 可作形容词，表示“堵塞的、鼻塞的”。bungalow、bungee、bungle 不属于这个词的派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Bung is a monosyllabic free root; the stopper noun can undergo conversion to the sealing verb, but the homographs do not all share one historical root. Inflections are bungs, bunged, and bunging. Compounding gives bung + hole → bunghole, an opening in a barrel, also used vulgarly; prefixation gives un- + bung → unbung, meaning remove a stopper, an uncommon verb. Bung up is a phrasal verb, and bunged-up can function as an adjective meaning blocked or congested. Bungalow, bungee, and bungle are not derivatives of bung.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 塞子义：stopper（塞子）最通用，plug（堵头）强调填住孔口，cork（软木塞）常指软木制瓶塞。随手放置义：chuck（扔）更突出抛掷动作，shove（塞、推）更突出推挤；贿款义最接近 bribe（贿赂）。形容词义：broken（坏的）通用，faulty（有故障的）强调缺陷，dodgy（不可靠、状态不佳的）更口语且不一定完全失灵。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the stopper sense, stopper is general, plug emphasizes filling a hole, and cork commonly denotes a bottle stopper made of cork. For casual placement, chuck emphasizes throwing and shove emphasizes pushing; the illicit-payment noun corresponds most closely to bribe. For the adjective, broken is general, faulty emphasizes a defect, and dodgy is informal and can suggest unreliability without complete failure.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 分三路记：bung 塞子→塞住；bung 东西进去→随手放或给；澳新 bung→坏了。最后一路词源独立。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep three tracks: a bung stops a hole; bung something in means put or give it casually; Australian and New Zealand bung means broken. The last track has a separate origin.

forms: 复数 curias 或 curiae；特指罗马教廷机构常写 the Roman Curia。
family: curial 教廷行政机构的。

morphology.text: curi(a)（教廷行政机构，去末尾 a） + -al → curial（教廷行政机构的）；curia 整词作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 借自拉丁语 curia，古罗马时指议事机构或议事场所，后来用于教廷行政机构；从“议事办事的机构”记忆。

usage_note: 本课教罗马天主教会的行政机构义；在正式名称 Roman Curia 中大写 Curia。不是表示教堂建筑的一般词。

senses.meaning_zh: 罗马教廷的行政机构，通常写作 the Roman Curia 或 the Curia

senses.meaning_zh: 古罗马议事厅，尤指元老院议事厅（历史术语）
senses.meaning_en: an ancient Roman meeting house, especially the senate house
senses.english_definition: In ancient Rome, a curia was a building where an assembly met, especially the building used by the Senate.

etymology_story.zh: curia 借自拉丁语 cūria，古罗马时期可指公民分组、其集会场所或元老院议事厅。后来它用于教廷及其他教会行政机构，保留了“议事、治理机构”的核心联系。[词源参考](https://www.etymonline.com/word/curia)
etymology_story.en: Curia was borrowed from Latin cūria, which could denote a Roman civic division, its meeting place, or the senate house. It later came to name papal and other ecclesiastical administrative bodies, preserving an association with deliberation and government. [Etymology reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/curia)

morphology_enriched.zh: curia 在现代英语中是整体借词，没有可独立使用的英语词根 cur；传统复数为 curiae。派生形容词 curial（教廷行政机构的；议事机构的）可用 curia 去末尾 -a + -al 来识记；curialist（教廷行政机构成员或其支持者）是较少见的专门词。法律短语 amicus curiae（法庭之友）中的 curiae 是拉丁语属格单数，不是该短语中的英语复数。
morphology_enriched.en: Curia is a whole-word borrowing in modern English, without an independently usable English root cur; its traditional plural is curiae. The adjective curial, relating to a curia, can be learned as curia minus final -a + -al; curialist is a less common specialist noun for a member or supporter of the papal curia. In the legal phrase amicus curiae, meaning friend of the court, curiae is a Latin genitive singular rather than an English plural.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 教会行政义：church administration（教会行政机构）是概括性释义；papal administration（教宗行政机构）较接近 Roman Curia；Holy See（圣座）则是范围不同的教会治理与法律概念，不能与 Curia 严格互换。历史建筑义可用 senate house（元老院议事厅）或 council chamber（议事厅）解释。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For ecclesiastical administration, church administration is a broad paraphrase, while papal administration is closer to Roman Curia. The Holy See is a distinct ecclesiastical and legal concept and is not strictly interchangeable with Curia. For the historical building sense, senate house or council chamber provides a useful paraphrase.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从古罗马的议事厅，到教会的办事机构：始终围绕“集会议事与治理”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: From Rome’s meeting house to church administration: the connecting idea is deliberation and government.

senses.meaning_zh: 皮平苹果；若干苹果品种名称中使用的称呼，通常指适合鲜食的苹果
senses.meaning_en: An apple belonging to one of several varieties traditionally called pippins, usually suitable for eating fresh.
senses.english_definition: A pippin is an apple of one of several varieties whose names traditionally include the word pippin.
senses.collocation_en: a Cox's Orange Pippin; a pippin apple
senses.collocation_zh: 一个考克斯橙皮平苹果；一个皮平苹果
senses.sentence_en: She chose a Cox's Orange Pippin for its rich flavour.
senses.sentence_zh: 她选了一个考克斯橙皮平苹果，看中的是它浓郁的风味。

etymology_story.zh: 来自古法语 pepin，意为“种子、果核”，经中古英语 pipin 进入英语。这个名称最初与从种子培育出的苹果树及其果实有关，后来保留在多个苹果品种的名称中。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English as pipin from Old French pepin, meaning a seed or pip. It was associated with apple trees grown from seed and their fruit, and later survived in the names of several apple varieties.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再作常规词根、词缀拆分的单纯词：pippin；复数为 pippins。没有常用的派生词族；不应把结尾 -in 当作现代英语中的独立后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, pippin is a simple word without a productive root-and-affix breakdown; its plural is pippins. It has no established common family of derivatives, and its ending -in should not be treated as a separate modern suffix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: apple（苹果）是上位词；dessert apple（鲜食苹果）按用途分类；Cox's Orange Pippin（考克斯橙皮平苹果）是具体品种。三者分别表示大类、用途类别和特定品种，不能在所有语境中互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Apple is the general category; dessert apple classifies an apple by its suitability for eating fresh; Cox's Orange Pippin names a particular variety. These are related terms at different levels of specificity, rather than freely interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 pip“果籽”联想到“由籽育成的苹果”：pippin。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect pip, an apple seed, with an apple originally grown from seed: pippin.

senses.collocation_en: Virginia bluebells; a patch of bluebells

etymology_story.zh: 由英语 blue“蓝色”和 bell“铃”复合而成，直接描写花朵的颜色和形状。不同地区把这个形象化名称用于不同植物，因此它并不对应唯一的植物物种。
etymology_story.en: Bluebell combines blue and bell, describing the colour and shape of the flowers. Different regions applied this descriptive name to different plants, so it does not identify a single botanical species.

morphology_enriched.zh: blue（蓝色）＋ bell（铃）→ bluebell，是名词性复合词；复数为 bluebells。没有常用的派生词族；bluebell wood“蓝铃花林地”等是短语组合。
morphology_enriched.en: Blue + bell forms the compound noun bluebell; the plural is bluebells. There is no established common family of derivatives; expressions such as bluebell wood are phrase combinations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wild hyacinth（野风信子）可指英国常见的蓝铃花；harebell（圆叶风铃草）对应苏格兰用法中的 bluebell；Virginia bluebells（弗吉尼亚滨紫草）指北美的另一种植物。这些名称须按地区和植物种类区分。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wild hyacinth can name the familiar British woodland bluebell; harebell names the plant called bluebell in Scottish usage; Virginia bluebells identifies a different North American plant. These names must be distinguished by region and species.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: blue＋bell：枝头挂着蓝色小铃。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Blue + bell: picture little blue bells hanging from a stem.

pronunciation.note: 重音和长音按所列 IPA 读取。

forms: 复数 ohms；单位符号 Ω 不随数量变形。
family: ohmic 欧姆的、与电阻有关的；ohmmeter 欧姆表。

morphology.text: ohm 整词作为独立词素记忆；ohm + -ic → ohmic（与欧姆或电阻有关的）。

etymology.text: 单位以德国物理学家 Georg Ohm（格奥尔格·欧姆）的姓氏命名；人名进入单位名称后，英文全拼写作小写 ohm。

usage_note: 单位名称小写 ohm，人物姓氏大写 Ohm，符号为大写希腊字母 Ω。写 one ohm、ten ohms。

question: 这个句子中，ohm 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 欧姆；电阻的国际单位制单位，符号为 Ω
senses.meaning_en: The SI unit of electrical resistance, represented by Ω.
senses.english_definition: An ohm is a unit of electrical resistance equal to the resistance through which one volt produces a current of one ampere.
senses.collocation_en: a resistance of ten ohms; a 100-ohm resistor
senses.collocation_zh: 十欧姆的电阻；一个阻值为一百欧姆的电阻器
senses.sentence_en: The resistor has a resistance of 100 ohms.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个电阻器的阻值为一百欧姆。

etymology_story.zh: 以德国物理学家 Georg Simon Ohm（格奥尔格·西蒙·欧姆）的姓氏命名，以纪念他对电流、电压与电阻关系的研究。作为单位名称时，英文通常写作小写 ohm，单位符号为大写希腊字母 Ω。
etymology_story.en: The unit is named after the German physicist Georg Simon Ohm, honouring his work on the relationship between current, voltage, and resistance. The unit name is normally lowercase ohm, while its symbol is the capital Greek letter Ω.

morphology_enriched.zh: ohm 是由人名转化而来的单纯名词，复数为 ohms。常见词族及组合包括 ohmic（欧姆的；服从欧姆定律的）、ohmically（按欧姆定律地）、non-ohmic（非欧姆的）、ohmmeter（欧姆表），以及 milliohm（毫欧）、kilohm（千欧）、megohm（兆欧）。
morphology_enriched.en: Ohm is a simple noun derived from a surname; its plural is ohms. Its family and related formations include ohmic, ohmically, non-ohmic, ohmmeter, and the prefixed unit names milliohm, kilohm, and megohm.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有常用的严格同义词。Ω 是单位符号；volt per ampere（伏特每安培）是其等价单位表达；electrical resistance（电阻）则是所测量的物理量，不是单位名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact lexical synonym. Ω is the unit symbol; volt per ampere is an equivalent unit expression; electrical resistance is the quantity being measured, rather than the unit.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住 1 Ω＝1 V/A：一伏推动一安培，对应一欧姆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember 1 Ω = 1 V/A: one volt producing one ampere corresponds to one ohm.

pronunciation.note: geo- 读 /dʒiːəʊ/，主重音在 chemical 的首音节。

forms: 通常不作比较；副词 geochemically。
family: geochemistry 地球化学；geochemist 地球化学家。

morphology.text: geo-（地球） + chemical（化学的） → geochemical（地球化学的）。

etymology.text: 英语以源自希腊语 gē（地球）的 geo- 连接 chemical，形成描述地球物质化学组成与变化的学科词。

usage_note: 常修饰 analysis、survey、evidence；强调岩石、土壤、水等的化学组成或过程，不泛指所有地理位置资料。

question: 这个句子中，geochemical 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 地球化学的；与地球物质的化学组成、分布及变化有关的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to the chemical composition of Earth materials and the distribution and movement of chemical elements within them.
senses.english_definition: Geochemical processes, measurements, or studies concern the chemicals in rocks, soil, water, and other Earth materials and how those chemicals behave.
senses.collocation_en: geochemical analysis; geochemical processes
senses.collocation_zh: 地球化学分析；地球化学过程
senses.sentence_en: Geochemical analysis helped identify the source of the groundwater contamination.
senses.sentence_zh: 地球化学分析有助于确定地下水污染的来源。

etymology_story.zh: 由表示“地球”的构词成分 geo- 与 chemical“化学的”结合而成，其中 geo- 源自希腊语 gē“地球”。它随地球化学研究的发展，用于描述地球物质中的化学组成、元素分布及相关过程。
etymology_story.en: Geochemical combines geo-, from Greek gē meaning Earth, with chemical. As geochemistry developed, the adjective came to describe the chemical composition, distribution of elements, and chemical processes of Earth materials.

morphology_enriched.zh: geo-（地球）＋ chemical（化学的）→ geochemical；词族包括 geochemistry（地球化学）、geochemist（地球化学家）和 geochemically（从地球化学角度；以地球化学方式）。这些形式共享 geo- 与 chemistry／chemical 的构词基础。
morphology_enriched.en: Geo- + chemical forms geochemical. The word family includes geochemistry, geochemist, and geochemically; these forms share the combining element geo- and the chemistry/chemical base.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chemical（化学的）范围最广；geological（地质的）涉及地球结构、物质及历史；biogeochemical（生物地球化学的）特别强调生物过程与地球化学过程之间的联系。这些是相关形容词，并非严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chemical has the broadest scope; geological concerns Earth's materials, structure, and history; biogeochemical specifically involves interactions between biological and geochemical processes. These are related adjectives rather than exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: geo-＝地球：把地球当作一个化学系统来研究。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Geo- means Earth: think of studying Earth as a chemical system.

pronunciation.note: 重音和长音按所列 IPA 读取。

forms: 复数 cholecystectomies，词尾 y 变 ies。
family: cholecyst 胆囊；cholecystitis 胆囊炎。

morphology.text: cholecyst（胆囊） + -ectomy（切除术） → cholecystectomy（胆囊切除术）。

etymology.text: 近代医学用希腊语材料造词：cholē 指胆汁，kystis 指囊，表示切除的 -ectomy 也来自希腊语；记作“胆囊被切除的手术”。

usage_note: 外科术语，-ectomy 表示手术切除，不能把本词理解为胆囊发炎或常规影像检查。

question: 这个句子中，cholecystectomy 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 胆囊切除术；通过外科手术切除胆囊
senses.meaning_en: Surgical removal of the gallbladder.
senses.english_definition: A cholecystectomy is an operation in which a surgeon removes the gallbladder.
senses.collocation_en: laparoscopic cholecystectomy; undergo a cholecystectomy
senses.collocation_zh: 腹腔镜胆囊切除术；接受胆囊切除术
senses.sentence_en: She underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy to treat symptomatic gallstones.
senses.sentence_zh: 她接受了腹腔镜胆囊切除术，以治疗引起症状的胆结石。

etymology_story.zh: 这是用希腊语词素构成的近代医学术语：cholē 意为“胆汁”，kystis 意为“囊”，ektomē 意为“切除”。这些成分组合起来，字面上表示“切除储存胆汁的囊”，即胆囊切除术。
etymology_story.en: This modern medical term was formed from Greek elements: cholē meaning bile, kystis meaning a sac or bladder, and ektomē meaning excision. Together they literally describe removal of the bile-containing sac, the gallbladder.

morphology_enriched.zh: cholecyst-（胆囊）＋ -ectomy（外科切除术）→ cholecystectomy；cholecyst- 又包含 chole-（胆汁）和 cyst-（囊）。复数为 cholecystectomies；相关形式包括 postcholecystectomy（胆囊切除术后的）；同根医学词包括 cholecystitis（胆囊炎）和 cholecystography（胆囊造影术），后两者不是由 cholecystectomy 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Cholecyst- meaning gallbladder + -ectomy meaning surgical removal forms cholecystectomy; cholecyst- contains chole- meaning bile and cyst- meaning sac or bladder. The plural is cholecystectomies; related formations include postcholecystectomy, while cholecystitis and cholecystography share the same anatomical base but are not direct derivatives of cholecystectomy.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gallbladder removal（胆囊切除）是通俗的等义表达；laparoscopic cholecystectomy（腹腔镜胆囊切除术）指经腹腔镜完成的具体术式；open cholecystectomy（开腹胆囊切除术）指经较大腹部切口完成的术式。后两者是下位术式名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gallbladder removal is the plain-English equivalent; laparoscopic cholecystectomy specifies removal using a laparoscope; open cholecystectomy specifies removal through a larger abdominal incision. The latter two name particular surgical approaches.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 胆汁 chole-＋囊 cyst-＋切除 -ectomy＝切除胆囊。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bile + sac + surgical removal: remove the gallbladder.

pronunciation.note: 重音和长音按所列 IPA 读取。

family: puffinry 海鹦群居地。

morphology.text: puffin 整词作为独立词素记忆；puffin + -ry（群体或聚集处） → puffinry（海鹦群居地）。

etymology.text: 从中古英语 poffin、puffon 一类海鸟名称延续而来；可把这个短词和圆胖身体、鲜艳嘴喙一起记忆。

usage_note: 可数海鸟名称，典型特征是繁殖季鲜艳的大嘴；不是 penguin（企鹅）。

question: 这个句子中，puffin 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 海鹦；一种嘴喙粗大、繁殖期喙色鲜艳的海鸟
senses.meaning_en: a seabird with a large bill that becomes brightly coloured during breeding
senses.english_definition: A puffin is a small seabird with black-and-white feathers and a large bill that becomes brightly coloured during the breeding season.
senses.collocation_en: Atlantic puffin; a puffin colony
senses.collocation_zh: 大西洋海鹦；海鹦繁殖群
senses.sentence_en: The puffin returned to its burrow with several small fish in its bill.
senses.sentence_zh: 那只海鹦嘴里衔着几条小鱼，回到了自己的洞穴。

etymology_story.zh: puffin 可追溯至中古英语的海鸟名称，早期曾用于肥胖的鹱类幼鸟，后来转指今天所说的海鹦。其更早的来源不确定，可能与 puff 所表达的鼓起、圆胖形象有关。
etymology_story.en: Puffin goes back to a Middle English seabird name, formerly applied to fat young shearwaters before being transferred to the bird now called a puffin. Its deeper origin is uncertain, though it may be connected with puff and the idea of a swollen or rounded shape.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 puffin 作为完整词干掌握，不宜把历史来源不确定的部分强行拆成词根和词缀。常用形式：puffins（复数）；相关构词：puffin-like（像海鹦的）、puffin colony（海鹦繁殖群）；罕见集合词 puffinry 指海鹦群或其聚居地。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, treat puffin as a whole stem rather than forcing an uncertain historical analysis into roots and affixes. Common form: puffins, the plural; related formations include puffin-like and puffin colony. The rare collective noun puffinry denotes a group or colony of puffins.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sea parrot（海鹦的俗称）突出其彩色大喙；auk（海雀科鸟类）是更宽泛的分类名称；seabird（海鸟）范围最广，不能与 puffin 精确互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sea parrot is an informal name highlighting the colourful bill; auk is a broader term for birds in the same family; seabird is broader still. The latter two are category terms rather than exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 puff 的“鼓起来”联想到海鹦圆胖的身体；这是形象记忆，不是确定的词源拆解。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a puffed-up, round-bodied seabird; this is a visual memory aid, not a certain etymological breakdown.

meaning: 语素；最小有意义的语言单位

pronunciation.note: 重音和长音按所列 IPA 读取。

forms: 复数 morphemes。
family: morphemic 语素的；morphology 词形学、构词学。

morphology.text: morph（形式） + -eme（语言学单位） → morpheme（语素，最小有意义单位）。

etymology.text: 借自法语 morphème，根源是希腊语 morphē（形式）；英语语言学用它命名不能再分出更小意义单位的形式。

usage_note: 语素可以独立成词，也可像表示复数的 -s 一样依附别的部分；它不等于音节。

question: 这个句子中，morpheme 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 语素；语言中最小的有意义或具有语法功能的单位
senses.meaning_en: the smallest linguistic unit carrying meaning or grammatical function
senses.english_definition: A morpheme is the smallest part of a language that has a meaning or a grammatical function of its own.
senses.collocation_en: a free morpheme; a bound morpheme
senses.collocation_zh: 自由语素；黏着语素
senses.sentence_en: The word 'cats' contains two morphemes: 'cat' and the plural ending '-s'.
senses.sentence_zh: cats 一词包含两个语素：cat 和表示复数的词尾 -s。

etymology_story.zh: morpheme 借自法语语言学术语 morphème，其构成联系希腊语 morphē（形式）和表示基本单位的 -ème。它被用于命名承载意义或语法功能的最小语言单位。
etymology_story.en: Morpheme was borrowed from the French linguistic term morphème, built from Greek morphē, meaning 'form', and -ème, a unit-forming suffix. It came to designate the smallest linguistic unit carrying meaning or grammatical function.

morphology_enriched.zh: 学术构词：morph-（形式）＋-eme（基本单位）→ morpheme。常用词族：morphemes（复数）、morphemic（语素的）、morphemically（从语素角度）；相关复合派生词包括 monomorphemic（单语素的）、bimorphemic（双语素的）和 polymorphemic／multimorphemic（多语素的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Learned formation: morph- 'form' + -eme 'basic unit' → morpheme. The common family includes morphemes, morphemic, and morphemically; related compound derivatives include monomorphemic, bimorphemic, and polymorphemic or multimorphemic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有严格的日常近义词。相关术语 morph（语素形式）指语素的具体表现形式；lexeme（词位）是统摄某个词各屈折形式的词汇单位；phoneme（音位）是区别意义的语音单位，本身不必承载意义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym. Related terms are morph, a concrete realization of a morpheme; lexeme, a vocabulary unit encompassing its inflected forms; and phoneme, a sound unit that distinguishes meanings without necessarily carrying meaning itself.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: morph＝形式，-eme＝基本单位：拆到再拆就失去意义或语法功能，就是语素。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Morph means 'form' and -eme marks a basic unit: stop dividing when another split would destroy the meaning or grammatical function.

usage_note: 英式常用 soya，美式常用 soy；可作名词修饰语，如 soya milk。不能把 soya 单独理解为任意一种豆。

question: 这个句子中，soya 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 大豆；用作食品原料的大豆及其制品，主要用于英式英语
senses.meaning_en: soybeans or food material made from them, chiefly in British English
senses.english_definition: Soya is a crop whose beans are rich in protein, or food material made from these beans.
senses.collocation_en: soya milk; soya protein
senses.collocation_zh: 豆奶；大豆蛋白
senses.sentence_en: This meat-free burger is made with soya protein.
senses.sentence_zh: 这款不含肉的汉堡是用大豆蛋白制成的。

etymology_story.zh: soya 经荷兰语 soja 传入英语，最终联系日语 shōyu（酱油）。这个名称随食品贸易传播，英语中的用法后来扩展到大豆及其食品原料。
etymology_story.en: Soya entered English through Dutch soja and ultimately goes back to Japanese shōyu, meaning 'soy sauce'. The name spread through food trading and developed English uses referring to the beans and food material made from them.

morphology_enriched.zh: soya 是整体借入的单纯词，现代英语中无须拆分词根和词缀。常用相关形式：soy（主要用于美式英语）、soya bean／soybean（大豆）、soya milk（豆奶）、soya flour（大豆粉）、soya protein（大豆蛋白）；这些主要是变体和复合词，并非词缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Soya is a simple borrowed word with no useful modern root-and-affix division. Common related forms include soy, chiefly American English; soya bean or soybean; soya milk; soya flour; and soya protein. These are mainly variants and compounds rather than affixal derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: soy 与 soya 基本同义，但 soy 更常见于美式英语；soybean 和 soya bean 都明确指大豆豆粒，也可指植株，而 soya 常作为不可数名词表示作物或食品原料。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Soy is essentially equivalent to soya but is more usual in American English. Soybean and soya bean specifically name the bean, or sometimes the plant, whereas soya commonly functions as an uncountable noun for the crop or food material.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: soya 与 soy 是一对变体：soy sauce 是酱油，soya milk 是豆奶，共同连到大豆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the variants soya and soy: soy sauce and soya milk both lead back to the soybean.

meaning: 火成的（由熔融岩浆或熔岩冷却形成）

forms: 通常不作比较；常用于 igneous rock。

morphology.text: ign-（火） + -eous（具有某种性质的） → igneous（火的；地质学中指火成的）。

etymology.text: 借自拉丁语 igneus（火的），与 ignis（火）相连；把岩浆的高温与冷却后形成的岩石联系起来记。

usage_note: 地质学常用 igneous rock，强调由熔融物冷却形成；不是把任何受热过的岩石都称为火成岩。

question: 这个句子中，igneous 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 火成的；由岩浆或熔岩冷却凝固形成的
senses.meaning_en: formed by the cooling and solidification of magma or lava
senses.english_definition: Igneous rocks are rocks that form when hot liquid rock cools and becomes solid.
senses.collocation_en: igneous rock; an igneous intrusion
senses.collocation_zh: 火成岩；火成侵入体
senses.sentence_en: Granite is an igneous rock that forms when magma cools slowly underground.
senses.sentence_zh: 花岗岩是一种火成岩，由岩浆在地下缓慢冷却形成。

etymology_story.zh: igneous 源自拉丁语 igneus（火的、炽热的），其基础是 ignis（火）。这个原本与火和高温有关的形容词，在地质学中专门用于描述熔融岩石冷却凝固的成因。
etymology_story.en: Igneous comes from Latin igneus, meaning 'fiery' or 'of fire', based on ignis, 'fire'. An adjective associated with fire and heat acquired its specialized geological use for rocks formed from cooling molten material.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习可识别为 ign-（火）＋-eous（具有某种性质的），但整个词是历史借词，并非现代英语临时拼接的结果。无常用直接派生词；常见组合有 igneous rock（火成岩）和 igneous activity（岩浆活动）；ignite（点燃）、ignition（点火）是同源相关词，并非由 igneous 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern learning, recognize ign- 'fire' + -eous 'having a particular nature', while remembering that the word was historically borrowed as a whole. There are no common direct derivatives; frequent combinations include igneous rock and igneous activity. Ignite and ignition are related through their origin, not derived from igneous.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有覆盖全部含义的严格近义词。magmatic（岩浆的）强调与岩浆或岩浆过程有关；volcanic（火山的）强调火山及喷出作用；plutonic（深成的）强调岩浆在地下深处凝固，后两者只对应部分火成岩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact synonym covering the full meaning. Magmatic emphasizes magma or magma-related processes; volcanic emphasizes volcanoes and eruption; plutonic describes formation deep underground. The latter two apply to particular categories of igneous rocks.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ign- 连到“火”：地下熔融，冷却成石，就是 igneous。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect ign- with fire: molten rock cools into solid rock—igneous.

question: 这个句子中，perambulate 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 步行走遍；四处漫步，常带正式或诙谐色彩
senses.meaning_en: to walk through or around a place, often in formal or humorous usage
senses.english_definition: If you perambulate, you walk around a place, usually in a leisurely way.
senses.collocation_en: perambulate around the town; perambulate through the park
senses.collocation_zh: 在镇上四处漫步；步行穿游公园
senses.sentence_en: After lunch, we perambulated around the town, stopping occasionally to admire the old buildings.
senses.sentence_zh: 午饭后，我们在镇上漫步，偶尔停下来欣赏古老的建筑。

etymology_story.zh: perambulate 源自拉丁语 perambulare，由 per-（穿过、遍及）和 ambulare（步行）组成。英语中它曾用于步行巡查地区或界线，如今也可正式或诙谐地表示四处步行、闲逛。
etymology_story.en: Perambulate comes from Latin perambulare, combining per- 'through or throughout' with ambulare 'to walk'. English uses have included walking over an area or inspecting boundaries, while modern usage also describes walking around in a formal or humorous way.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 per-（遍及）＋ambulate（步行）→ perambulate。常用屈折形式：perambulates、perambulated、perambulating；派生词族：perambulation（步行巡游；漫步）、perambulator（步行者；英式英语中旧称婴儿车）、perambulatory（步行巡游的，较少见）；pram 是 perambulator 在婴儿车义上的缩略形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: per- 'throughout' + ambulate 'walk' → perambulate. Inflections are perambulates, perambulated, and perambulating. The derivative family includes perambulation, perambulator, and the less common adjective perambulatory. Pram is a shortened form of perambulator in its British baby-carriage sense.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: walk（步行）最中性，不限定速度或目的；stroll（散步）强调轻松、休闲；amble（缓步走）强调从容缓慢的步态。perambulate 更正式，且常带刻意文雅或诙谐的语气。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Walk is neutral about pace and purpose; stroll emphasizes relaxed recreation; amble emphasizes an easy, unhurried gait. Perambulate is more formal and often deliberately elevated or humorous.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: per-＝遍及，ambulate＝走路：靠双脚把一个地方走一圈。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Per- means 'throughout' and ambulate means 'walk': cover a place on foot.

etymology_story.zh: 借自阿拉伯语 amīr，意为“指挥官、王公”，与表示“命令”的动词 amara 同源。这个词原来强调指挥和统领的身份，后来也用作统治者的称号；emir 是同源的另一种英语拼写。
etymology_story.en: Amir comes from Arabic amīr, meaning “commander” or “prince,” related to amara, “to command.” A designation for someone who commanded others also became a title for a ruler; emir is an alternative English spelling.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，amir 是不可进一步拆分的借词词干；复数为 amirs。amir + -ate → amirate，表示埃米尔的职位或领地；常见拼写对应形式为 emir、emirs 和 emirate。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, amir is an unanalyzed borrowed stem; its plural is amirs. Amir + -ate forms amirate, meaning an amir’s office or territory; corresponding forms with the alternative spelling are emir, emirs, and emirate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: emir 是同一称号的另一种拼写，通常没有意义差别；prince（王公、王子）范围更广，也可仅指君主之子；ruler（统治者）只说明统治身份，不指定具体称号。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Emir is an alternative spelling of the same title, usually without a difference in meaning. Prince is broader and can simply mean a monarch’s son, while ruler describes governing authority without identifying a particular title.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“发号施令的人”：指挥官 → 首领 → 埃米尔。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “someone who commands”: commander → chief → amir.

forms: 三单 debars；过去式及过去分词 debarred；现在分词 debarring，末尾 r 双写。
family: debarment 禁止参加、取消资格。

morphology.text: de-（加强或排除的历史前缀） + bar（阻挡） → debar（阻止参加、使无资格）；不要把 de- 当作取消阻挡。

etymology.text: 经盎格鲁诺曼语 debarrer 进入英语，与设置障碍的 bar 相连；想象门口的一道栅栏，记住被挡在资格之外。

usage_note: 正式用语，常见 debar somebody from doing something；涉及活动或资格，后接 from，不用 debar somebody to do。

question: 这个句子中，debar 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 正式禁止参加；取消资格；阻止获得某种权利或机会
senses.meaning_en: To officially exclude someone from participation, eligibility, or access.
senses.english_definition: If an authority debars someone from an activity or opportunity, it officially prevents them from taking part in it or having access to it.
senses.chinese_definition: 如果某个机构禁止某人参加活动或获得机会，就是正式阻止其参与或取得相应资格。
senses.collocation_en: debar someone from bidding; debar someone from holding office
senses.collocation_zh: 禁止某人投标；取消某人担任公职的资格
senses.sentence_en: The company was debarred from bidding for public contracts.
senses.sentence_zh: 该公司被取消了公共合同的投标资格。

etymology_story.zh: 经盎格鲁法语、古法语中的相关形式进入英语，由 de- 与表示“阻挡”的 barrer 构成，后者与英语 bar 同源。历史上的 de- 在这里起加强作用，因此词义是“挡在外面”，而不是“解除阻挡”。
etymology_story.en: Debar entered English through Anglo-French and Old French forms combining de- with barrer, “to bar,” which is related to English bar. The historical prefix reinforces the blocking sense here, so the word means exclusion rather than removal of a barrier.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按历史结构理解为 de-（加强）+ bar（阻挡），但现代英语中宜把 debar 作为固定动词整体掌握。词族及屈折形式：debars；debarred（过去式、过去分词）；debarring（现在分词）；debarment（禁止参加、取消资格）；debarments（复数）。加元音开头的屈折后缀时，末尾 r 双写。
morphology_enriched.en: Its historical structure is de- (intensive) + bar, although modern learners should treat debar as an established verb. Its family and inflections include debars, debarred, debarring, debarment, and debarments. The final r doubles before the vowel-initial inflectional endings.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bar（禁止）用途较广，语气可正式也可普通；exclude（排除）强调不让进入某个群体或范围；disqualify（取消资格）强调因不符合条件或违反规则而失去资格。debar 尤其突出正式或制度性的禁止。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bar is a broad verb for preventing access or participation; exclude emphasizes keeping someone outside a group or category; disqualify emphasizes loss of eligibility through unmet requirements or broken rules. Debar particularly suggests formal or institutional exclusion.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 bar 想成资格入口的栏杆：debar 就是正式把人挡在栏杆外。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a bar across an entrance: to debar someone is to officially keep them outside.

usage_note: 地理或登山语境用语，指一整块山体或相连山峰组成的山块，不等于普通小山丘。

question: 这个句子中，massif 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 山块；由相连山峰构成、整体较独立的山体
senses.meaning_en: A compact mountain mass or group of mountains forming a distinct unit.
senses.english_definition: A massif is a large mountain mass or a compact group of mountains that forms a distinct unit within a surrounding landscape.
senses.chinese_definition: 山块是指在周围地形中形成一个相对独立整体的大型山体或紧密相连的山群。
senses.collocation_en: a mountain massif; a granite massif
senses.collocation_zh: 山地中的独立山块；花岗岩山体
senses.sentence_en: Snow covered the highest peaks of the massif.
senses.sentence_zh: 积雪覆盖了这片山体的最高几座山峰。

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语名词 massif，其相关形容词表示“厚实的、成块的”，最终源于拉丁语 massa，意为“一团、一块”。地理意义保留了这种整体性：多座山峰可以组成一块相对独立的山体。
etymology_story.en: Massif was borrowed from the French noun massif, associated with the adjective meaning “solid” or “massive,” ultimately from Latin massa, “a lump” or “mass.” Its geographical meaning preserves the idea of mountains forming one substantial, distinct block.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，massif 是完整的借词词干，不拆作 mass + 英语后缀 -if；复数为 massifs。它没有常用的直接派生词；mass、massive、massively 和 massiveness 属于相关同源词，不是由 massif 直接派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, massif is a complete borrowed stem, not mass plus an English suffix -if; its plural is massifs. It has no common direct derivatives. Mass, massive, massively, and massiveness are etymologically related forms rather than derivatives of massif.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mountain mass（山体）是较宽泛的描述性近义表达；mountain range（山脉）通常强调沿一定方向延伸的一系列山峰；mountain group（山群）只强调群聚，不一定具有 massif 所突出的整体块状结构。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mountain mass is a broader descriptive equivalent; mountain range usually emphasizes mountains extending along a line; mountain group emphasizes a cluster without necessarily suggesting the compact, unified structure conveyed by massif.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用同源词 mass（一大块）联想：massif 就是群峰连成的一大块山体。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with the related word mass: a massif is a great mass of connected mountains.

meaning: 磷酸酶；催化去除磷酸基团的酶

pronunciation.note: Collins 同列词尾 /teɪs/ 和 /teɪz/；这里采用 /teɪs/。

forms: 复数 phosphatases；具体酶名中常作不可数用法。
family: phosphate 磷酸盐、磷酸基团；phosphatase inhibitor 磷酸酶抑制剂。

morphology.text: phosphat(e)（磷酸盐，去末尾 e） + -ase（酶） → phosphatase（磷酸酶）。

etymology.text: 英语生物化学用 phosphate 与酶名后缀 -ase 造词；看到后缀可联想它是一类酶，作用与磷酸基团有关。

relations.meaning: 激酶，常催化加上磷酸基团

usage_note: 常见 alkaline phosphatase（碱性磷酸酶）和 acid phosphatase（酸性磷酸酶）。本词指酶，不是磷酸盐本身。

question: 这个句子中，phosphatase 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 磷酸酶，催化水解除去底物磷酸基团的酶
senses.meaning_en: An enzyme that removes phosphate groups from substrates by hydrolysis.
senses.english_definition: A phosphatase is an enzyme that uses water to remove a phosphate group from a molecule, releasing inorganic phosphate.
senses.chinese_definition: 磷酸酶是一类利用水从分子上去除磷酸基团、释放无机磷酸的酶。
senses.collocation_en: alkaline phosphatase; protein phosphatase
senses.collocation_zh: 碱性磷酸酶；蛋白磷酸酶
senses.sentence_en: The phosphatase removed a phosphate group from the protein.
senses.sentence_zh: 这种磷酸酶去除了该蛋白质上的一个磷酸基团。

etymology_story.zh: 这是生物化学术语，由 phosphate（磷酸盐）与表示酶的后缀 -ase 构成。名称指出其作用涉及磷酸基团，而这种酶的典型作用是通过水解去除磷酸基团。
etymology_story.en: Phosphatase was formed in biochemical terminology from phosphate and the enzyme-forming suffix -ase. The name identifies its connection with phosphate groups, which these enzymes characteristically remove by hydrolysis.

morphology_enriched.zh: phosphat(e)（phosphate 去掉末尾 e）+ -ase（酶）→ phosphatase；复数为 phosphatases。相关词族包括 phosphate（磷酸盐）、phosphorylate（使磷酸化）、phosphorylation（磷酸化）、dephosphorylate（使去磷酸化）和 dephosphorylation（去磷酸化）；后几项是相关生化构词，并非 phosphatase 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Phosphat(e), formed by dropping the final e of phosphate, + -ase (enzyme) gives phosphatase; the plural is phosphatases. Related biochemical forms include phosphate, phosphorylate, phosphorylation, dephosphorylate, and dephosphorylation; these are related formations rather than direct derivatives of phosphatase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: phosphomonoesterase（磷酸单酯酶）和 phosphoric-monoester hydrolase（磷酸单酯水解酶）是针对磷酸单酯水解作用的技术性近义名称；protein phosphatase（蛋白磷酸酶）则是作用于蛋白质的具体类别，不能替代所有语境中的 phosphatase。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Phosphomonoesterase and phosphoric-monoester hydrolase are technical near-equivalents specifying phosphate monoester hydrolysis. Protein phosphatase is a narrower term for enzymes acting on proteins, so it cannot replace phosphatase in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: phosphat- 提示磷酸基团，-ase 提示酶：记住“把磷酸基团拆下来的酶”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Phosphat- points to phosphate and -ase signals an enzyme: remember “the enzyme that takes phosphate off.”

forms: 地质年代专名通常无复数，写 the Mesozoic；也可作形容词。

morphology.text: meso-（中间） + -zoic（生命的） → Mesozoic（中生代，意为中间的生命时代）。

etymology.text: 19世纪地质学以源自希腊语 mesos（中间）和 zōē（生命）的构词成分命名；它处在古生代与新生代之间。

usage_note: 规范写 Mesozoic，首字母大写；作名词通常用 the Mesozoic。本卡教地质年代名称，不将其等同某一种动物。

question: 这个句子中，Mesozoic 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 中生代，包括三叠纪、侏罗纪和白垩纪的地质年代
senses.meaning_en: The geological era comprising the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods.
senses.english_definition: The Mesozoic is the geological era between the Paleozoic and the Cenozoic, comprising the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods.
senses.chinese_definition: 中生代是介于古生代和新生代之间的地质年代，包括三叠纪、侏罗纪和白垩纪。
senses.collocation_en: during the Mesozoic; the end of the Mesozoic
senses.collocation_zh: 在中生代期间；中生代末期
senses.sentence_en: Dinosaurs dominated many terrestrial ecosystems during the Mesozoic.
senses.sentence_zh: 在中生代，恐龙在许多陆地生态系统中占据主导地位。

senses.meaning_zh: 中生代的；形成于中生代的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to or dating from the Mesozoic era.
senses.english_definition: Something that is Mesozoic belongs to, dates from, or relates to the geological era between the Paleozoic and the Cenozoic.
senses.chinese_definition: 称某事物为中生代的，表示它属于、形成于或涉及古生代与新生代之间的这一地质年代。
senses.collocation_en: Mesozoic rocks; Mesozoic fossils
senses.collocation_zh: 中生代岩石；中生代化石
senses.sentence_en: The cliffs expose several layers of Mesozoic rock.
senses.sentence_zh: 这些峭壁露出了数层中生代岩石。

etymology_story.zh: 这一名称形成于19世纪的地质学术语体系，结合了源自希腊语 mesos（中间）的 meso- 和源自 zōē（生命）的构词成分。它字面上表示“中间的生命时代”，对应其位于古生代与新生代之间的位置。
etymology_story.en: The name was formed in nineteenth-century geology using meso-, from Greek mesos, “middle,” and a combining element derived from zōē, “life.” It literally suggests a “middle age of life,” reflecting its position between the Paleozoic and the Cenozoic.

morphology_enriched.zh: meso-（中间）+ -zoic（与生命有关的）→ Mesozoic；-zoic 可进一步联系 zo-（生命）和 -ic（形容词后缀）。同形词兼作形容词和名词，名词用法通常为 the Mesozoic；Paleozoic（古生代）和 Cenozoic（新生代）是平行构词，不是它的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Meso- (middle) + -zoic (relating to life) forms Mesozoic; -zoic can be associated with zo- (life) and the adjective-forming suffix -ic. The same form functions as an adjective and a noun, with the noun normally appearing as the Mesozoic. Paleozoic and Cenozoic are parallel formations, not derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Mesozoic Era（中生代）是完整的正式名称；Age of Reptiles（爬行动物时代）突出爬行动物的重要地位；Age of Dinosaurs（恐龙时代）是强调恐龙的通俗说法。后两者都是非正式描述，不能在精确地层表述中完全替代正式名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mesozoic Era is the full formal name; Age of Reptiles emphasizes the prominence of reptiles; Age of Dinosaurs is a popular description emphasizing dinosaurs. The latter two are informal descriptions rather than fully interchangeable terms in precise stratigraphic writing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: meso- 是“中间”，-zoic 关联“生命”：古生代与新生代之间，就是中生代。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Meso- means “middle” and -zoic relates to life: place the Mesozoic between the Paleozoic and the Cenozoic.

meaning: 蠢人；傻瓜（英式冒犯用语）

usage_note: 英式非正式用语，有冒犯性，不适合称呼陌生人或用于正式场合；make a prat of oneself 表示让自己出丑。

question: 这个句子中，prat 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 蠢人；傻瓜（英式非正式用语，略带冒犯）
senses.meaning_en: A stupid or foolish person; an informal, mildly offensive British insult.
senses.english_definition: If you call someone a prat, you mean that they are stupid or have behaved foolishly.
senses.collocation_en: a complete prat; make yourself look a prat
senses.collocation_zh: 十足的蠢货；让自己显得像个傻瓜
senses.sentence_en: I felt like a complete prat when I realised I had been waiting outside the wrong house.
senses.sentence_zh: 发现自己一直等在别人家门外时，我觉得自己简直是个大傻瓜。

etymology_story.zh: prat 在16世纪英语俚语中指“屁股”，更早来源不明。后来它发展出指人的贬义用法，表示“蠢人；傻瓜”。
etymology_story.en: Prat was used in sixteenth-century English slang to mean the buttocks, but its earlier origin is unknown. It later developed into an insulting term for a foolish person.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，prat 是不可进一步分析的简单词，复数为 prats。常见派生词包括 prattish（愚蠢的；像傻瓜的）、prattishness（愚蠢行为或特质）和 prattishly（愚蠢地）；prattish 在加 -ish 时双写 t。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, prat is a simple base with no productive internal division; its plural is prats. Its derivative family includes prattish, prattishness, and prattishly; the t is doubled before -ish in prattish.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fool（傻瓜）适用范围较广，也可只指一时判断失误的人；idiot（白痴；蠢货）通常更直接、更具侮辱性；twit（笨蛋）与 prat 一样常见于英式非正式表达，往往带轻蔑或打趣语气。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fool is broader and can describe someone who merely makes a poor decision; idiot is usually a more direct and stronger insult; twit, like prat, is informal British English and often conveys dismissive or teasing criticism.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把旧义“屁股”联想到“出丑”：做了傻事，显得像个 prat。这是助记联想，并非已经证实的语义演变机制。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the old meaning, buttocks, with making a fool of yourself: foolish behaviour makes you look a prat. This is a memory association, not a proven account of the semantic change.

pronunciation.note: 重音和长音按所列 IPA 读取。

forms: 通常不可数；指多种病因时可用 aetiologies。
family: etiology 美式拼写；aetiological 病因学的。

morphology.text: aetio-（原因） + -logy（学说、研究） → aetiology（病因学；也指病因）。

etymology.text: 经拉丁语 aetiologia 来自希腊语 aitiologia，包含 aitia（原因）和表示论述的成分；记成追问“为什么会得这种病”。

usage_note: 英式 aetiology，美式 etiology；本课教医学中的病因或病因研究，不能与治疗方法混淆。

question: 这个句子中，aetiology 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 病因；疾病或其他现象的起因
senses.meaning_en: The cause or set of causes of a disease or another phenomenon.
senses.english_definition: The aetiology of a disease or condition is the cause or combination of causes that produces it.
senses.collocation_en: unknown aetiology; the aetiology of cancer
senses.collocation_zh: 病因不明；癌症的病因
senses.sentence_en: The patient had a persistent fever of unknown aetiology.
senses.sentence_zh: 这名患者持续发热，病因不明。

senses.meaning_zh: 病因学；对起因的研究
senses.meaning_en: The study of causes, especially the causes of diseases.
senses.english_definition: Aetiology is the study of what causes diseases or other conditions.
senses.collocation_en: research into the aetiology of disease; aetiology and pathogenesis
senses.collocation_zh: 对疾病病因的研究；病因学与发病机制
senses.sentence_en: Her research focuses on the aetiology of autoimmune diseases.
senses.sentence_zh: 她的研究主要探讨自身免疫性疾病的病因。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经拉丁语 aetiologia 源自希腊语 aitiologia，表示“对原因的说明”，由 aitia（原因）和 -logia（论述；研究）构成。它后来尤其用于医学，既指疾病的原因，也指研究这些原因的学科。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through Latin aetiologia from Greek aitiologia, an account of causes, formed from aitia, meaning cause, and -logia, meaning discourse or study. It became particularly associated with medicine, referring both to the causes of disease and to their study.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学术构词可分析为 aetio-（原因）+ -logy（研究；学科）。词族包括 aetiological（病因的；病因学的）、aetiologic（同义形容词）、aetiologically（从病因角度）和 aetiologist（病因学研究者）；美式拼写对应为 etiology、etiological、etiologic、etiologically 和 etiologist。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern learned formation is aetio- (cause) + -logy (study or discipline). Its family includes aetiological, aetiologic, aetiologically, and aetiologist; the corresponding American spellings are etiology, etiological, etiologic, etiologically, and etiologist.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cause（原因）是最普通、最直接的近义表达；causation（因果作用；致因过程）强调某因素如何产生结果；pathogenesis（发病机制）是相关概念，强调疾病如何发生和发展，而 aetiology 主要追问是什么引起疾病。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cause is the ordinary, direct equivalent; causation emphasizes the causal relationship or process. Pathogenesis is a related term rather than an exact synonym: it concerns how a disease develops, while aetiology primarily concerns what causes it.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: aetio- 表示“原因”，-logy 表示“研究”：追问“为什么会得这种病”，就是 aetiology。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Aetio- means cause and -logy means study: asking why a disease occurs leads you to its aetiology.

pronunciation.note: 重音和长音按所列 IPA 读取。

forms: 三单 deprecates；过去式及过去分词 deprecated；现在分词 deprecating。
family: deprecation 不赞成；deprecating 表示不赞许的；deprecatingly 不赞许地。

morphology.text: de-（向外、离开） + prec-（祈求） + -ate（动词成分） → deprecate；历史上“祈求免除”发展为“表示反对”。

etymology.text: 来自拉丁语 deprecari（祈求免除），由 de- 与 precari（祈求）组成；从希望坏事别发生，联想到对其表示不赞成。

usage_note: 正式及物动词，直接接所反对的事；本课教一般反对义。计算机中的“弃用”有专门含义，不等于已删除。

question: 这个句子中，deprecate 是什么意思？

senses.meaning_zh: 不赞成；对……表示反对或贬抑（正式用语）
senses.meaning_en: To express disapproval of something or speak of it disparagingly.
senses.english_definition: If you deprecate something, you express disapproval of it or suggest that it has little value.
senses.collocation_en: deprecate the use of something; deprecate violence
senses.collocation_zh: 不赞成使用某物；反对暴力
senses.sentence_en: She deprecated the use of threats to settle the dispute.
senses.sentence_zh: 她不赞成用威胁的方式解决争端。

senses.meaning_zh: 将软件功能等标记为不建议继续使用；弃用
senses.meaning_en: To designate a software feature or interface as no longer recommended for use.
senses.english_definition: If developers deprecate a feature, they advise people to stop using it, although it may still be available.
senses.collocation_en: deprecate an API; a deprecated function
senses.collocation_zh: 将某个 API 标记为弃用；已标记为弃用的函数
senses.sentence_en: The developers deprecated the old function and recommended a safer replacement.
senses.sentence_zh: 开发者将旧函数标记为弃用，并推荐了一个更安全的替代函数。

etymology_story.zh: 该词源自拉丁语 deprecari，意为“祈求免除；恳求避开”，由 de-（离开；免除）和 precari（祈求）构成。它从“请求某事不要发生”发展为“表示反对”，计算机领域又将其用于表示不再建议使用某项功能。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin deprecari, meaning to pray to avert something or plead for deliverance, formed from de- (away) and precari (pray). The meaning developed into expressing disapproval, and computing adopted it for advising against continued use of a feature.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代派生以 deprecate 为词基；历史上的 de- + prec- + -ate 不宜当作完全能产的现代构词公式。词形有 deprecates、deprecated、deprecating；派生词包括 deprecation（反对；贬抑；软件弃用）、deprecatory／deprecative（表示反对或贬抑的）、deprecatingly（表示贬抑地）及 deprecator（反对者，较少见）；常见复合形式有 self-deprecating（自嘲的）、self-deprecation（自嘲）和 self-deprecatingly（自嘲地）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern derivatives use deprecate as their base; the historical elements de-, prec-, and -ate should not be treated as a fully productive modern formula. Inflected forms are deprecates, deprecated, and deprecating; derivatives include deprecation, deprecatory, deprecative, deprecatingly, and the less common deprecator. Common compounds include self-deprecating, self-deprecation, and self-deprecatingly.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: disapprove of（不赞成）最中性、最常用；disparage（贬低）着重说某人或某事价值不高；condemn（谴责）表达更强烈、常带道德判断的反对。软件语境中的 deprecate 表示不建议继续使用，并不等于已经删除。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Disapprove of is the most neutral and everyday equivalent; disparage emphasizes speaking of someone or something as having little worth; condemn expresses stronger, often moral criticism. In software, deprecate means discourage continued use and does not itself mean remove.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住历史逻辑“祈求免除”：希望某事别发生，于是表示不赞成；软件中则是“请别再使用”。不要与 depreciate（贬值）混淆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the historical idea of praying something away: wishing it would not happen becomes disapproval; in software, it becomes please stop using this. Keep it distinct from depreciate, meaning lose value.

meaning: 杓鹬（长腿、长而下弯嘴的涉禽）

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标出主重音；采用这一常见读法。

forms: 可数名词；复数 curlews，也可用 curlew。
family: curlew-like 像杓鹬的（-like 表示“像……的”）。

morphology.text: curlew 整词作为独立词素记忆；curlew + -like → curlew-like（像杓鹬的），不要把 curlew 硬拆成 curl。

etymology.text: 中古英语从盎格鲁法语 curleu 借入；名称模仿鸟鸣。可以把它和湿地上传来的悠长叫声联系起来。

senses.meaning_zh: 杓鹬：腿长、喙长而向下弯曲的涉禽
senses.meaning_en: A long-legged wading bird with a long, downward-curving bill.
senses.english_definition: A curlew is a bird with long legs and a long curved bill that feeds in wet ground or shallow water.
senses.collocation_en: a flock of curlews; the call of a curlew
senses.collocation_zh: 一群杓鹬；杓鹬的鸣叫声
senses.sentence_en: A curlew searched the mud for food as the tide went out.
senses.sentence_zh: 退潮时，一只杓鹬在泥滩上觅食。

etymology_story.zh: curlew 经中古英语借自盎格鲁法语 curleu，与古法语 corlieu 等形式相关。这个名称通常被认为源于对鸟鸣声的模仿，而不是由英语 curl（卷曲）构成。
etymology_story.en: Curlew entered Middle English from Anglo-French curleu, related to Old French forms such as corlieu. The name is generally considered imitative of the bird's call, rather than a formation from English curl.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，curlew 是不可进一步分析的简单名词，复数为 curlews，没有常用的独立派生词族。curlew-like／curlewlike（像杓鹬的）是透明的形容词组合；Eurasian curlew（白腰杓鹬）和 whimbrel（中杓鹬）等属于鸟名，不是由 curlew 派生出的词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, curlew is a simple noun without a productive internal division; its plural is curlews, and it has no established common derivative family. Curlew-like or curlewlike is a transparent adjectival formation; names such as Eurasian curlew and whimbrel identify birds rather than derivatives of curlew.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: curlew 没有完全可互换的常用近义词。wader（涉禽）是范围更广的上位词；shorebird（滨鸟）也是较宽泛的类别名称；whimbrel（中杓鹬）指杓鹬类中的特定鸟种，不能替代所有 curlew。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Curlew has no exact everyday synonym. Wader is a broader category, shorebird is another broad grouping, and whimbrel names a particular kind of curlew rather than all curlews.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 curlew 的声音联想到湿地上悠长的鸟鸣，再配上“长腿、下弯长嘴”的画面；这是拟声记忆，不是把它拆成 curl。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hear curlew as an echoing wetland call, then picture long legs and a long downcurved bill. Use the sound association without treating curl as its root.

meaning: 马麦酱（Marmite 品牌的酵母提取物涂酱）

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标出主重音；采用这一常见读法。

etymology_story.zh: 20世纪初创立的 Marmite 品牌借用了法语 marmite，意为“带盖炖锅”，这一形象也出现在品牌标识上。后来，围绕其鲜明口味形成的“爱它或恨它”宣传，使品牌名进一步获得“让人爱憎分明的”这一比喻义。
etymology_story.en: The Marmite brand, established in the early twentieth century, took its name from French marmite, a covered cooking pot also depicted in its branding. The spread's distinctive taste and its love-it-or-hate-it advertising later gave the name a figurative meaning describing something that divides opinion sharply.

morphology_enriched.zh: Marmite 是整体借入的品牌名，现代英语中不可拆为有意义的词根和词缀。名词转为形容词表示“让人爱憎分明的”属于零派生；Marmite-flavoured（马麦酱味的）、Marmite-loving（喜爱马麦酱的）和 Marmite-like（像马麦酱的；让人爱憎分明的）是透明的复合形式，没有固定而丰富的派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Marmite is a borrowed brand name with no meaningful modern English root-and-affix division. Its figurative adjective is formed by conversion without an added suffix; Marmite-flavoured, Marmite-loving, and Marmite-like are transparent compounds. It has no extensive established derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 名词义没有完全等同的近义词：yeast extract（酵母提取物）是产品类别名称，Vegemite（维吉麦酱）是另一品牌，不能与 Marmite 等同。形容词义可近似用 polarizing（使意见两极分化的）或 divisive（引起分歧的）；Marmite 更突出“有人爱、有人恨”，divisive 则更容易暗示冲突或不和。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The noun has no exact synonym: yeast extract names the product category, while Vegemite is a different brand. For the adjective, polarizing and divisive are close alternatives; Marmite particularly suggests strong love-or-hate reactions, while divisive more readily suggests conflict or disunity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看见罐身上的小炖锅，记住法语锅名；想到浓烈口味让人“爱或恨”，便能连接品牌义和比喻义。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the little cooking pot on the jar to remember the French name, then connect its strong taste with love-or-hate reactions to recall the figurative adjective.

etymology_story.zh: tyrosine 是十九世纪形成的科学名称，由希腊语 tyros（奶酪）和化学名词后缀 -ine 构成。这个名称源于该物质最初从奶酪中的酪蛋白分解产物中被分离出来。
etymology_story.en: Tyrosine is a nineteenth-century scientific name formed from Greek tyros, meaning cheese, and the chemical suffix -ine. The name reflects its original isolation from the breakdown products of casein, a protein found in cheese.

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学构词：tyr(o)-（奶酪，历史词根）+ -ine（化学物质后缀）；现代普通英语通常把 tyrosine 作为完整词项学习。主要词族：tyrosinase（酪氨酸酶）、tyrosyl（酪氨酰基；酪氨酰的）、tyrosinemia／tyrosinaemia（酪氨酸血症）、tyrosinuria（酪氨酸尿）。常见复合术语：L-tyrosine（L-酪氨酸）、tyrosine kinase（酪氨酸激酶）、tyrosine hydroxylase（酪氨酸羟化酶）。
morphology_enriched.en: Scientific formation: tyr(o)-, the historical element meaning cheese, + -ine, a chemical suffix; in ordinary modern English, tyrosine is generally learned as a whole lexical item. Principal family members include tyrosinase, an enzyme acting on tyrosine; tyrosyl, a tyrosine-derived group or an adjective describing it; tyrosinemia/tyrosinaemia, excess tyrosine in the blood; and tyrosinuria, tyrosine in the urine. Common compounds include L-tyrosine, tyrosine kinase, and tyrosine hydroxylase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 4-hydroxyphenylalanine（4-羟基苯丙氨酸）是描述其化学结构的名称；L-tyrosine（L-酪氨酸）明确限定天然蛋白质中使用的立体异构体；phenylalanine（苯丙氨酸）是人体可用于合成酪氨酸的另一种氨基酸，并非同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: 4-hydroxyphenylalanine is a structural chemical name for tyrosine; L-tyrosine specifically identifies the stereoisomer used in natural proteins; phenylalanine is a different amino acid from which the body can make tyrosine, not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tyros＝奶酪：从奶酪蛋白中找到的氨基酸，就是酪氨酸。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tyros means cheese: remember tyrosine as the amino acid first found through cheese protein.

etymology_story.zh: dilatation 经法语和拉丁语进入中古英语，源自拉丁语 dilatatio，相关动词 dilatare 意为使变宽、扩大。它保留了变宽或增大的核心意义，后来广泛用于医学和物理学。
etymology_story.en: Dilatation entered Middle English through French and Latin, deriving from Latin dilatatio and the related verb dilatare, meaning to widen or enlarge. It retained this central meaning and became established in medical and physical descriptions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族分析：dilat(e)（扩张）+ -ation（过程或状态）→ dilatation。相关词：dilate（扩张）、dilation（扩张，与 dilatation 常可互换）、dilated（扩张的）、dilating（正在扩张的）、dilator（扩张器；扩张肌）、dilatation 的形容词 dilatational（扩张的；膨胀的），以及 dilative（使扩张的）。dilatory 通常表示拖延的，不宜按现代意义并入这一词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern family analysis: dilat(e), meaning widen, + -ation, marking a process or state, gives dilatation. Related forms include dilate, dilation, dilated, dilating, dilator, dilatational, and dilative. Dilation often overlaps with dilatation; dilator names a widening instrument or muscle, while dilatational and dilative are adjectives. Dilatory normally means delaying and should not be grouped here by modern meaning.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dilation（扩张）与 dilatation 常指同一过程，具体选词取决于地区和专业惯例；expansion（扩大；膨胀）适用范围更广，也可指业务或规模增长；distension（膨隆；胀大）常强调内部压力造成的撑大。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dilation often names the same process, with the choice depending on regional and specialist usage; expansion is broader and also covers growth in activities or scale; distension often emphasizes swelling or stretching caused by pressure from within.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dilate 是变宽，dilatation 就是变宽这一过程或状态。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Dilate means become wider; dilatation names that widening or the resulting enlarged state.

etymology_story.zh: tranche 借自法语 tranche，原意为切下的一片，与动词 trancher（切开）有关。英语把切片这一形象用于从资金、股份或金融产品整体中划出的一部分。
etymology_story.en: Tranche was borrowed from French tranche, meaning a slice, and is related to trancher, meaning to cut. English extended the image of a slice to a separate portion of funding, shares, or a financial product.

morphology_enriched.zh: tranche 是完整借词，在现代英语中没有常用的内部词根与词缀拆分。名词复数 tranches；通过零派生兼作金融动词，其形式为 tranches、tranched、tranching。相关形式包括 retranche（重新分层）、retranching（重新分层的过程），以及复合形容词 tranche-based（按批次或层级安排的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Tranche is a whole-word borrowing with no productive internal root-and-affix division in modern English. Its noun plural is tranches; conversion also gives a financial verb with the forms tranches, tranched, and tranching. Related formations include retranche, meaning divide into tranches again; retranching, the corresponding process; and the compound adjective tranche-based.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: instalment／installment（分期款）强调分期支付的一笔；portion（部分）是最宽泛的整体组成部分；slice（一份；一片）形象地表示从整体中划出的一份。三者都不能完整替代 tranche 在证券风险分层中的专业含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Instalment/installment emphasizes one payment in a series; portion is a general term for part of a whole; slice suggests a share cut from a larger total. None fully replaces the specialist meaning of tranche as a class within a structured security.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把整笔资金想成蛋糕：切出一片，就是一个 tranche；动词表示把它切成不同层级。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a funding package as a cake: one financial slice is a tranche; the verb means dividing it into such classes.

senses.meaning_zh: 比塞塔：西班牙采用欧元前使用的货币单位
senses.meaning_en: the former monetary unit of Spain, replaced by the euro
senses.english_definition: The peseta was the unit of money used in Spain before the country adopted the euro.
senses.collocation_en: the Spanish peseta; a hundred pesetas
senses.collocation_zh: 西班牙比塞塔；一百比塞塔

etymology_story.zh: 英语 peseta 借自西班牙语同形词。其更早来源有不同解释：常见解释联系加泰罗尼亚语 peceta（小块、小钱币），即 peça（块、件）的小称形式；另一些词源解释将它与 peso 联系起来。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed peseta from Spanish. Accounts of its earlier origin differ: a common explanation connects it with Catalan peceta, meaning a small piece or coin and formed as a diminutive of peça, while other accounts associate it with peso.

morphology_enriched.zh: peseta 在现代英语中是不可再作常用词缀分析的货币名称，复数为 pesetas，没有常用的派生动词或形容词。常见复合表达包括 peseta-denominated（以比塞塔计价的）、peseta notes（比塞塔纸币）和 peseta coins（比塞塔硬币）；这些是复合表达，不是独立的词族派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, peseta is a currency name without a productive internal affix analysis; its plural is pesetas, and it has no common derived verb or adjective. Compounds include peseta-denominated, meaning expressed in pesetas; peseta notes; and peseta coins. These are compounds rather than separate derivational family members.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Spanish peseta（西班牙比塞塔）是明确所指国家的同义名称；ESP 是其历史国际货币代码，而非普通词汇同义词；céntimo（分）是比塞塔的百分之一单位，不能与 peseta 互换。其他货币名称如 peso（比索）也不是同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spanish peseta is an equivalent name that specifies the country; ESP is its historical international currency code rather than an ordinary lexical synonym; céntimo names one hundredth of a peseta and is not interchangeable with it. Names of other currencies, such as peso, are not synonyms either.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 peseta 锚定在西班牙旧硬币上：欧元之前，用的是比塞塔。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor peseta to an old Spanish coin: before the euro, Spain used pesetas.

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标出主重音；采用这一常见读法。

morphology.text: tatty 整词作为独立词素记忆；tatty + -ness → tattiness（破旧，y 变 i）。

etymology.text: 十六世纪初的苏格兰英语中已经有 tatty，最初形容纠结、蓬乱，后来常形容破旧。想象一件边缘磨损、毛线纠结的旧衣服。

usage_note: 英式非正式用语，常修饰衣服、书本、家具；也可带嫌弃语气。

senses.meaning_zh: 破旧的；因磨损或疏于照料而显得邋遢的，尤用于英式非正式英语
senses.meaning_en: shabby, worn, or untidy in appearance, especially in informal British English
senses.english_definition: Something that is tatty looks old, worn, or untidy because it has been used a lot or has not been looked after.

etymology_story.zh: tatty 的早期苏格兰英语用法描述毛发等纠结、蓬乱的状态，通常与表示一绺纠结毛发的 tat 联系起来。后来，它的意义扩展为物品破旧、磨损或外观邋遢。
etymology_story.en: Early Scots uses of tatty described tangled or matted hair and similar material, and the word is usually connected with tat, meaning a tangled lock. Its meaning later broadened to describe things that look shabby, worn, or untidy.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习时可将 tatty 作为完整形容词掌握；历史上可联系 tat（纠结的一绺）+ -y（具有某种特征的），拼写中出现双写 t。比较级 tattier、最高级 tattiest；副词 tattily（破旧邋遢地）；名词 tattiness（破旧；邋遢），均体现词尾 y 的相应变化。tattered（破烂的）可用于联想辨义，但不是由 tatty 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern learning, tatty can be treated as a whole adjective; historically it can be related to tat, a tangled lock, + adjectival -y, with doubled t in the spelling. Its comparative is tattier and its superlative tattiest; tattily is the adverb, and tattiness is the noun, with the corresponding changes to final y. Tattered is useful for comparison but is not derived from tatty.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: shabby（破旧的；寒酸的）与 tatty 最接近，也能形容环境和衣着；scruffy（邋遢的）更强调外观不整洁，常形容人或头发；tattered（破烂的）更明确地表示布料、纸张等已经撕裂或磨破。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Shabby is closest to tatty and can describe surroundings or clothing; scruffy emphasizes an untidy appearance and often describes people or hair; tattered more specifically suggests that fabric, paper, or similar material is torn or frayed.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从纠结的毛线想到磨破的衣边：tatty 就是旧得显邋遢。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of tangled threads and worn edges: tatty means visibly shabby from wear or neglect.

meaning: 爱好者自办杂志；粉丝刊物

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标出主重音；采用这一常见读法。

morphology.text: fan（爱好者）+ magazine（取末尾 zine）→ fanzine（粉丝刊物）；这是两个英语词的拼合。

etymology.text: 由英语 fan 和 magazine 拼合而成，起初与爱好者社群的刊物有关。想象粉丝自己写、自己印的杂志。

translation: 我们印了一本介绍最喜爱本地乐队的粉丝刊物。

senses.meaning_zh: 由爱好者自行编印、供同好阅读的杂志；粉丝刊物
senses.meaning_en: A magazine produced by enthusiasts for other enthusiasts.
senses.english_definition: A fanzine is a magazine that fans produce for people who share their interest in a particular subject, performer, or activity.

senses.sentence_zh: 她创办了一份乐迷刊物，刊登对当地乐队的采访。

etymology_story.zh: fanzine 由 fan“爱好者”和 magazine“杂志”拼合而成，通常认为由美国科幻爱好者拉斯·肖韦内于1940年创造。它最初指科幻迷自办的刊物，后来扩展到音乐、体育等爱好者社群的出版物。
etymology_story.en: Fanzine blends fan and magazine and is generally credited to the American science-fiction enthusiast Russ Chauvenet in 1940. It originally described publications made by science-fiction fans and later spread to music, sport, and other enthusiast communities.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：fan“爱好者”＋ magazine 的截取部分 -zine → fanzine，属于拼合词；这里的 -zine 原本不是表示某种意义的传统后缀。屈折形式：fanzines。相关词族：fan“爱好者”、fandom“粉丝群体；同好文化”、fannish“爱好者圈子的”；zine“独立小刊物”和 zinester“独立刊物创作者”与 fanzine 属于同一出版文化词群。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: fan + -zine, clipped from magazine → fanzine, a blend; -zine was not originally a traditional meaning-bearing suffix. Inflection: fanzines. Related family: fan, fandom, and fannish; zine, an independently produced small publication, and zinester, someone who creates such publications, belong to the same publishing vocabulary.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: zine“独立小刊物”范围更广，不一定围绕某个粉丝群体；fan magazine“粉丝杂志”也可能由商业出版商制作；newsletter“通讯”侧重定期传递消息。fanzine 特别强调由爱好者为同好制作。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A zine is broader and need not concern a fandom; a fan magazine may be commercially produced; a newsletter mainly distributes updates. Fanzine particularly emphasizes production by enthusiasts for fellow enthusiasts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fan＋magazine：粉丝自己做的杂志。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fan + magazine: a magazine made by fans.

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标出主重音；采用这一常见读法。

forms: 通常不可数；谈这种能力时不用 a numeracy。
family: numerate 有基本计算能力的；innumeracy 计算能力不足。

morphology.text: numer-（数）+ -acy（能力、状态）→ numeracy（识数与计算能力）；可与 literacy 联记。

etymology.text: 现代英语参照 literacy“读写能力”造词，采用拉丁语 numerus“数”的词根，表示和数字打交道的能力。

usage_note: 教育和就业语境常见，包括理解数字、金额、比例和基本运算，不等于高等数学。

senses.meaning_zh: 识数、基本计算及在日常情境中理解和运用数字的能力
senses.meaning_en: The ability to understand and use numbers in practical situations.
senses.english_definition: Numeracy is the ability to understand numbers and use basic mathematics in everyday situations.
senses.collocation_en: basic numeracy skills; literacy and numeracy
senses.collocation_zh: 基本识数与计算技能；读写能力与识数计算能力

senses.sentence_zh: 这门课程通过比较价格等日常任务培养识数与计算能力。

etymology_story.zh: numeracy 是20世纪参照 literacy“读写能力”构造的词，采用与拉丁语 numerus“数”有关的词干。它将“基本文化能力”的概念扩展到理解数字和实际运用数学的能力。
etymology_story.en: Numeracy was formed in the twentieth century on the model of literacy, using a stem associated with Latin numerus, meaning 'number.' It extends the idea of basic educational competence to understanding numbers and applying mathematics.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代分析：numer-／numer＋-acy“状态、能力”→ numeracy；其构形仿照 literacy，也可与 numerate“具备识数计算能力的”对应理解，但不能机械地分析为 numerate＋-cy。核心词族：numerate、numeracy、innumerate“缺乏识数计算能力的；这类人”、innumeracy“识数计算能力不足”。同源相关词：number“数”、numeral“数字符号”、numeric／numerical“数字的”、numerically“在数字上”、numerous“众多的”、enumerate“列举”、enumeration“列举；计数”、enumerator“计数员；调查员”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: numer- or numer + -acy, expressing a state or ability → numeracy; the formation follows literacy and corresponds to numerate, but is not a mechanical addition of -cy to numerate. Core family: numerate, numeracy, innumerate, and innumeracy. Related words sharing the historical number element include number, numeral, numeric, numerical, numerically, numerous, enumerate, enumeration, and enumerator.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: number sense“数感”强调对数量、大小及数字关系的直觉理解；arithmetic skills“算术技能”侧重具体计算操作；mathematical literacy“数学素养”通常覆盖更广泛的数学理解与应用。numeracy 强调日常生活中理解和使用数字的基本能力。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Number sense emphasizes an intuitive understanding of quantities and numerical relationships; arithmetic skills focus on calculation; mathematical literacy usually covers broader mathematical understanding and application. Numeracy emphasizes basic competence with numbers in everyday life.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: literacy 管文字，numeracy 管数字。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Literacy handles words; numeracy handles numbers.

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标出主重音；采用这一常见读法。

forms: 副词，无比较级、复数或时态变化。
family: therein 在其中；thereof 关于它的。

morphology.text: there（那里、所指之物）+ on（在上面）→ thereon（在其上）。

etymology.text: 古英语已有 thæron，后来成为中古英语 ther on，再连写成 thereon。它保留了早期英语把位置词组合起来的方式。

usage_note: 正式、书面或较古旧，常回指前文提到的表面或文件；日常一般用 on it。本卡只学空间义。

a crown engraved thereon 刻在其上的王冠
context_hint: The word points back to the surface just mentioned.
hint: The word points back to the surface just mentioned.

senses.meaning_zh: 在其上；在前述物体或表面上，属正式用语
senses.meaning_en: On the object or surface just mentioned, in formal usage.
senses.english_definition: Thereon means on the thing or surface that has just been mentioned.
senses.collocation_en: the signature thereon; the words written thereon
senses.collocation_zh: 其上的签名；写在其上的文字
senses.sentence_en: The document was returned because the signature thereon was illegible.
senses.sentence_zh: 这份文件因其上的签名无法辨认而被退回。

senses.meaning_zh: 就前述事项；对前述款项，常用于法律或财务文本
senses.meaning_en: On or concerning the matter or sum just mentioned, especially in legal or financial writing.
senses.english_definition: In formal writing, thereon means on or concerning a matter or amount that has already been mentioned.
senses.collocation_en: interest thereon; a report thereon
senses.collocation_zh: 该款项的利息；关于该事项的报告
senses.sentence_en: The borrower must repay the principal and any interest accrued thereon.
senses.sentence_zh: 借款人必须偿还本金及其产生的全部利息。

etymology_story.zh: thereon 源于古英语中相当于“那里＋在……上”的组合，后来经中古英语形式发展为现代连写形式。它保留了早期英语将 there 与介词组合的方式，如今主要见于正式、法律及较旧的文体。
etymology_story.en: Thereon descends from an Old English combination equivalent to 'there + on,' which developed through Middle English into the modern joined form. It preserves an early English pattern of combining there with a preposition and now occurs mainly in formal, legal, and older styles.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：there“那里；前述事物”＋on“在……上；关于”→ thereon，属于复合副词，没有常用屈折变化或直接派生词。相关构词系列包括 therein“在其中”、thereof“其……；关于它的”、thereto“向其；附于其”、thereby“由此；借此”、thereupon“随即；在其上”和 therewith“与其一起；用它”；这些是平行复合词，不是 thereon 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: there, referring to a place or something previously mentioned, + on → thereon, a compound adverb with no common inflections or direct derivatives. Parallel compounds include therein, thereof, thereto, thereby, thereupon, and therewith; these are related formations rather than derivatives of thereon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: on it“在它上面；对它”是普通表达；upon it“在其上”语气较正式或书面；on that matter“关于该事项”仅对应抽象指代义。thereon 更简练，但通常带有法律或旧式书面语色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: On it is the ordinary expression; upon it sounds more formal or literary; on that matter corresponds only to the abstract reference sense. Thereon is compact but typically has a legal or old-fashioned written tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: there 指前面说过的事物，on 表示“在其上”或“就其而言”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: There points back to something mentioned; on places something on it or relates something to it.

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标出主重音；采用这一常见读法。

forms: varices 已是复数；单数 varix，不能再加 -s 变成 variceses。
family: varix 一条曲张静脉；varicose 静脉曲张的。

morphology.text: varic-（varix 的词干）+ -es（拉丁语复数词尾）→ varices（曲张静脉）；这是不规则复数，不拆成 varice + s。

etymology.text: 来自拉丁语 varix“曲张静脉”；英语保留了拉丁式复数 varices。看到 -ices，可联想到单复数词干的变化。

usage_note: 医学名词，常见 oesophageal varices（食管静脉曲张）；varices 用复数谓语。
sentence: The scan revealed enlarged varices around the oesophagus.

etymology_story.zh: varices 保留了拉丁语 varix“曲张静脉”的复数形式，拉丁语词干为 varic-。该词进入医学英语后沿用了原有的解剖与病理含义。
etymology_story.en: Varices preserves the Latin plural of varix, meaning a dilated vein, whose stem is varic-. Medical English retained both the classical plural and the word's anatomical and pathological meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: 形态关系：单数 varix → 词干 varic-＋拉丁式复数词尾 -es → varices；这里的 -ices 读 /ɪsiːz/，不能拆成 varice＋普通复数 -s。核心相关词族：varix“单条曲张静脉”、varices“多条曲张静脉”、variceal“曲张静脉的”、varicose“静脉曲张的”、varicosity“静脉曲张；曲张部位”、varicosities“多处静脉曲张”。这些词围绕同一医学词干构成，但并非都直接派生自复数 varices。
morphology_enriched.en: Inflectional relationship: singular varix → stem varic- + the Latin plural ending -es → varices; -ices is pronounced /ɪsiːz/, and the word is not varice plus an ordinary plural -s. The core related family includes varix, varices, variceal, varicose, varicosity, and varicosities. These share the medical stem but are not all direct derivatives of the plural varices.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: varicose veins“曲张静脉”是接近的对应表达，在日常语境中常让人想到腿部静脉；dilated veins“扩张的静脉”范围更广，并不必然指具有静脉曲张病变的血管。varices 属医学用语，尤其常见于食管或胃部曲张静脉的描述。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Varicose veins is a close equivalent, though everyday usage often suggests veins in the legs; dilated veins is broader and does not necessarily indicate varicose disease. Varices is a medical term especially common in descriptions of enlarged veins in the oesophagus or stomach.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: varix 是单条，varices 是多条：记住词干 varic-，画面是扩张、迂曲的静脉。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One varix, several varices: keep the stem varic- and picture enlarged, winding veins.

etymology_story.zh: bicameral 由表示“二”的 bi- 与源自拉丁语 camera“房间、厅室”的成分构成，并加上形容词后缀 -al。由于议院可称为 chamber“议事厅；议院”，“两个厅室”的概念发展为政治制度中的“两院制”。
etymology_story.en: Bicameral combines bi-, meaning 'two,' with an element from Latin camera, meaning 'room' or 'chamber,' and the adjective suffix -al. Since a legislative house is called a chamber, the idea of 'two chambers' became a description of a legislature with two houses.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bi-“二”＋camer-“室；议院”＋-al“……的”→ bicameral“两院制的”。直接派生词：bicameralism“两院制；两院制原则”、bicameralist“两院制支持者；支持两院制的”、bicamerally“以两院制方式”。平行相关词：unicameral“一院制的”、unicameralism“一院制”、multicameral“多院的；多室的”；chamber“房间；议院”和 camera“照相机”与 camer- 有历史词源联系。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: bi-, 'two,' + camer-, 'chamber,' + -al, forming an adjective → bicameral. Direct derivatives include bicameralism, bicameralist, and bicamerally. Parallel formations include unicameral, unicameralism, and multicameral; chamber and camera are historically related to the element camer-.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: two-chamber“由两个议院组成的”和 two-house“两院的”是较直白的对应表达；双院制强调两个立法议院，并不必然规定它们权力相等。bicameral 是政治学和宪制讨论中的标准术语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Two-chamber and two-house are plainer equivalents. Having two legislative houses does not necessarily mean that they have equal powers; bicameral is the standard term in political and constitutional discussion.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bi-＝二，camer-＝议事厅：两个议事厅，就是两院制。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bi- means two; camer- means chamber: two legislative chambers make a bicameral system.

senses.meaning_zh: （尤指中世纪贵族宅邸或宫廷的）总管；管家
senses.meaning_en: A senior official responsible for a noble household or estate, especially in medieval times.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经盎格鲁法语进入中古英语，最终源于日耳曼语中表示“年长的”和“仆从”的成分。原本的“资深仆从”逐渐成为掌管贵族家务、庄园事务，有时也承担行政或司法职责的高级官员。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English through Anglo-French and ultimately comes from Germanic elements meaning 'old' and 'servant.' The original idea of a senior servant developed into an official managing a noble household or estate, sometimes with administrative or judicial duties.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 seneschal 视为不可再作常用构词拆分的借入词，而非英语前缀与词根的组合。主要词族：seneschal（总管）→ seneschalship（总管的职位、任期或职权）；复数为 seneschals。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, seneschal is an unanalyzed loanword rather than a combination of productive English prefixes and roots. Its principal word family is seneschal → seneschalship, meaning the office, tenure, or authority of a seneschal; the plural is seneschals.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: steward（管事）侧重财产、庄园或事务管理；chamberlain（宫廷总管）侧重君主或贵族的内廷事务；majordomo（大管家）侧重大宅仆役与家务的统筹。seneschal 尤具中世纪背景，职责可能兼及庄园行政。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A steward manages property, an estate, or practical affairs; a chamberlain oversees a royal or noble household, particularly its inner administration; a majordomo directs domestic staff and household operations. Seneschal has a particularly medieval association and may include estate administration.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史逻辑：“资深仆从”升为统管全宅事务的“总管”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical logic: the senior servant becomes the official in charge of the whole household.

senses.meaning_zh: 腹水；腹膜腔内异常积液
senses.meaning_en: An abnormal accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity.
senses.english_definition: Ascites is a condition in which fluid collects abnormally inside the abdomen, in the space around the abdominal organs.
senses.collocation_en: develop ascites; tense ascites
senses.collocation_zh: 出现腹水；张力性腹水
senses.sentence_en: The ultrasound scan showed ascites in the patient's abdomen.
senses.sentence_zh: 超声检查显示患者腹腔内有腹水。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经医学拉丁语源于希腊语 askitēs，与 askos“皮袋、酒囊”有关。名称借用了皮囊鼓胀的形象，指腹腔积液造成的腹部膨隆。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through medical Latin from Greek askitēs, related to askos, meaning a skin bag or wineskin. Its naming evokes a swollen bag, referring to the abdominal swelling caused by accumulated fluid.

morphology_enriched.zh: ascites 是整体借入的医学名词；其形容词采用词干 ascit- + -ic → ascitic（腹水的、与腹水有关的）。常用词族为 ascites、ascitic；ascites 通常作不可数名词，词尾 -s 不是普通英语复数标记，也不能把词尾误认作表示炎症的 -itis。
morphology_enriched.en: Ascites is a borrowed medical noun; its adjective uses the stem ascit- + -ic → ascitic, meaning relating to ascites. The usual word family is ascites and ascitic; ascites is normally uncountable, its final -s is not an ordinary English plural ending, and its ending should not be confused with the inflammation suffix -itis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hydroperitoneum（腹膜腔积液）是较少见的技术性近义词；peritoneal effusion（腹膜腔积液）侧重液体在腹膜腔内积聚这一现象。ascites 是临床上通常使用的名称，不能与任何原因造成的腹胀一概等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hydroperitoneum is a less common technical synonym; peritoneal effusion emphasizes the accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity. Ascites is the usual clinical term and is more specific than abdominal swelling in general.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: askos 是“皮囊”：腹腔像皮囊一样积液鼓起。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Askos means a skin bag: picture the abdomen swelling like a bag filled with fluid.

senses.meaning_zh: 火盆；炭盆

senses.english_definition: A brazier is a metal container in which charcoal or coal is burned to provide heat or to cook food.

senses.meaning_en: A craftsperson who makes or repairs brass or copper objects, in traditional occupational usage.
senses.english_definition: A brazier is a craftsperson who makes or repairs objects made of brass or copper.

etymology_story.zh: “火盆”义来自法语 brasier，最终与表示“余烬、炭火”的 braise 有关。“铜器匠”义是不同来源的同形词，历史上由表示“黄铜”的 brass 加职业后缀形成，并非火盆义的引申。
etymology_story.en: The fire-container sense comes from French brasier, ultimately related to braise, meaning embers. The metalworker sense is a separate formation historically based on brass with an occupational suffix, rather than an extension of the fire-container meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: 火盆义的 brazier 在现代英语中作为整体借词记忆，不拆成 brass + 后缀；铜器匠义历史上可分析为 brass + -ier（从业者），伴有拼写变化。两义的复数均为 braziers；相关词 braziery 指铜器匠的行业或制品，较少见，brazer（钎焊工）则是 braze + -er，不能直接等同于 brazier。
morphology_enriched.en: For the fire-container sense, brazier is an unanalyzed modern loanword, not brass plus a suffix; the metalworker sense can historically be analyzed as brass + occupational -ier, with a spelling change. Both senses have the plural braziers; the uncommon related noun braziery denotes the trade or products of a brazier, while brazer is braze + -er and specifically means someone who brazes.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: firepan（火盘）泛指盛火的盘状容器；fire pit（火坑、户外火炉）通常是地面凹坑或较大的固定设施；coppersmith（铜匠）对应职业义，专指加工铜器的工匠。brazier 的容器义强调盛放燃烧煤炭的金属器具。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A firepan is a pan-shaped container for a fire; a fire pit is usually a ground-level pit or a larger fixed installation; a coppersmith corresponds to the occupational sense and specifically works copper. The container sense of brazier emphasizes a metal vessel holding burning fuel.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 两条来源分开记：炭火余烬 → 火盆；brass 黄铜 → 铜器匠。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep the two origins separate: embers lead to the fire container; brass leads to the metalworker.

meaning: 重重地放下；随手往下放
